name: 盘古
title: 开辟天地的原初巨人

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 盘古是中国开天神话中的原初巨人，其较早成文记载见于三国吴人徐整的著述，今多由后世引文保存。他并非先秦经典中统一的创世神，形象与南方地方传统及后来的道教宇宙叙事相互交织。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 天地最初混沌如鸡子，盘古生于其中，历经漫长岁月使清轻之气上升为天、重浊之气下沉为地。他随天地分离而不断长高，支撑两者不再合拢。另一组记载说盘古死后，气息成为风云，声音成为雷霆，双目化为日月，血液化作江河，身体化成山岳与土地。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 常见图像把他画成披兽皮、持巨斧的巨人，但巨斧不是所有早期文本都有的道具。开辟混沌与身体化生万物，是比具体服饰更稳定的识别线索。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 盘古故事强调天地从混沌中分化以及人与自然共享身体性的联系。各地盘古庙、节俗与口传保存不同谱系，不能把现代通俗版当作唯一古本，也不宜将其等同于女娲造人的叙事。

en.name: Pangu
en.title: Primordial giant who separates heaven and earth

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Pangu is the primordial giant of a Chinese account of cosmic beginnings. Early written attestations are associated with Xu Zheng, a third-century writer whose works survive mainly through quotations. Pangu was not the single creator of all early Chinese traditions; his story developed through regional transmission and later religious interpretation.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Within an egglike chaos, Pangu grows as clear, light elements become heaven and heavy elements become earth. He keeps the two apart while their separation increases over immense spans of time. A related account turns his dying body into the world: breath becomes wind and clouds, voice becomes thunder, eyes become sun and moon, blood becomes rivers, and flesh becomes soil and mountains.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Popular images show a towering, roughly clothed figure wielding an axe, although the axe is not present in every early source. His most consistent attributes are separating the cosmos and transforming his own body into its landscape.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Pangu traditions connect cosmic order with the living material of the natural world. Local temples and oral narratives preserve different genealogies and details. Modern retellings often combine sources, so a familiar illustrated version should not be mistaken for a single ancient canonical account.

name: 女娲
title: 造人与补天的神圣者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 女娲是中国古代神话中兼具创造与修复力量的神圣人物，见于《楚辞》《淮南子》等不同文献。早期材料呈现多种面貌，后世又将她与伏羲配为兄妹或夫妇；这些关系不能视为所有时代共同接受的定说。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《淮南子》描述四极废坏、洪水烈火并作，女娲炼五色石补苍天，断巨鳌之足立四极，杀黑龙以济冀州，积芦灰止洪水。另一则由《风俗通义》佚文保存的故事说，她以黄土抟造人，又引绳入泥挥洒成人；不同造人方式还被用来解释社会等级的由来。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 汉代画像中女娲常为人首蛇身，与伏羲交尾盘绕，手执规矩一类器物。五色石、补天与泥土造人也是识别标志，但蛇身图像不应简单解读为邪恶或怪物。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 女娲在地方祭祀、婚姻起源传说及文学中具有不同地位。她的补天事迹突出灾变后的修复与生命延续，现代文化常强调其女性创造力，但古代资料并不存在整齐统一的女神教义体系。

en.name: Nüwa
en.title: Sacred creator and restorer of the heavens

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Nüwa is a sacred figure of creation and repair in Chinese traditions, appearing in sources including the Chuci and Huainanzi. These materials do not present one consistent biography. Later traditions frequently pair her with Fuxi as siblings or spouses, relationships that should not be projected unchanged onto every earlier text.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Huainanzi, cosmic supports fail and fire and flood ravage the world. Nüwa smelts stones of five colors to mend heaven, cuts off a giant turtle’s legs to support its corners, kills a black dragon, and dams floodwaters with reed ashes. Another account describes her molding people from yellow earth and creating further people by drawing a cord through mud and scattering its drops.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Han images often depict Nüwa with a human head and serpentine body, intertwined with Fuxi and holding measuring instruments. Colored stones and clay figures provide other clues. Her serpent form does not carry an inherently evil meaning.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Local worship, marriage traditions, and literature give Nüwa different roles. Repairing a damaged cosmos highlights survival and renewed order rather than creation alone. Contemporary interpretations often emphasize female creative power, but surviving ancient accounts never formed one uniform system of goddess theology.

name: 伏羲
title: 制卦授艺的文化始祖

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伏羲又写作伏戏、包牺，是中国古代传统中的文化始祖，常列入三皇，但三皇名单历代并不一致。《周易·系辞下》以包牺氏解释卦象与技艺的起源，汉代图像和后世谱系进一步丰富了他的神圣身份。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《系辞下》说包牺仰观天象、俯察地理，观察鸟兽纹理并取象于自身及万物，由此作八卦以通神明、类万物，又结绳为网罟，教授渔猎。另一些地方洪水故事中，伏羲与女娲成为幸存兄妹，经求取天意后成婚，使人类得以延续；这属于另一类叙事传统。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 伏羲常以人首蛇身出现，与女娲相对或交缠，旁有日月及星象。八卦、规矩和琴等物也可伴随其形象，不同器物对应制卦、定秩序或创制音乐的文化功绩。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伏羲祭祀在甘肃天水等地延续，并与地方祖源认同相连。其故事把观察自然、发明技术和社会组织合为文明起点，既有宗教祭祖意义，也被历代思想家用于讨论知识、秩序与圣王理想。

en.name: Fuxi
en.title: Culture ancestor credited with trigrams and arts

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Fuxi, also called Baoxi in early sources, is a culture ancestor frequently included among the Three Sovereigns, although their membership varies. The appended commentaries to the Book of Changes associate him with trigrams and useful inventions. Han images and later genealogies developed his sacred identity in several different directions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Book of Changes describes Baoxi observing celestial patterns, earthly forms, animals, and his own body before devising the eight trigrams to classify the world. It also credits him with knotted nets used for fishing and hunting. In a different family of regional flood stories, Fuxi and Nüwa survive as siblings and seek heavenly approval before marrying so that human life can continue.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A human head above a serpentine body is a common visual form, especially beside Nüwa. Trigrams, measuring instruments, celestial emblems, and sometimes a zither identify particular achievements. No single object accompanies him in every artistic or ritual setting.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Fuxi ceremonies, notably around Tianshui in Gansu, connect ritual reverence with local ancestral identity. His stories make observation, technology, and social organization parts of civilization’s beginnings. Philosophers also used this culture ancestor to discuss knowledge, ordered government, and the ideal of the sage ruler.

name: 玉皇大帝
title: 统摄天廷的至高尊神之一

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 玉皇大帝是道教及中国民间信仰中统摄天界的重要尊神，通常被尊称为玉皇上帝。他的地位随经典、朝廷封号与地方祭祀逐渐发展；道教三清另有更根本的神学位置，不能简单把天廷想成全中国唯一一致的神谱。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 道教《高上玉皇本行集经》叙述他原为王子，舍弃王位入山修道，历劫成就慈悲与救度功德，最终成为玉皇。民间故事和《西游记》则常将其置于有奏章、职官及赏罚制度的天廷；孙悟空扰乱天宫时，玉皇调遣天兵，并请如来降伏悟空，呈现文学中的跨宗教神界。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 造像多为端坐的帝王，戴垂旒冠冕、着衮服，持笏或有侍臣列班。天宫、奏章、印玺体现治理秩序的意象，不应把小说中具体官署全当作道教经典的统一制度。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 农历正月初九在不少地区称为玉皇诞或天公生，闽台等地有隆重祭拜。玉皇形象借人间官僚制度说明天界秩序，同时承载祈福、悔过和公正裁断的期待；不同地方对其权能边界理解不尽相同。

en.name: Jade Emperor
en.title: Exalted sovereign of the celestial court

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: The Jade Emperor is a major celestial sovereign in Daoism and Chinese popular religion. His prominence developed through scriptures, imperial recognition, and local worship. He should not be described as the universally supreme figure of every Chinese tradition: the Three Pure Ones occupy distinct, foundational positions in many Daoist theological systems.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: A Daoist scripture recounts his beginnings as a compassionate prince who renounces royal succession, cultivates the Way, and achieves exalted status through successive ages of practice. Popular tales and Journey to the West instead emphasize his administrative court. When the Monkey King disrupts heaven, the emperor deploys celestial forces and requests the Buddha’s assistance, creating a literary universe where several religious traditions interact.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: He usually appears enthroned in imperial robes and a ceremonial crown with hanging bead strings. A court tablet, attendants, memorials, and seals express celestial government. Specific offices in popular fiction do not constitute a universally binding Daoist administrative chart.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The ninth day of the first lunar month is celebrated as his birthday in many communities, especially in Fujian and Taiwan. Worship joins prayers for protection with expectations of moral oversight. His bureaucratic imagery makes heavenly order understandable through institutions familiar from imperial society.

name: 后羿
title: 射落烈日的神射英雄

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 后羿通常指射日英雄羿，但古代材料还记载与夏代权力斗争有关的有穷后羿，二者关系历来有争议。《淮南子》等书中的神射手受命平息灾害，后来与嫦娥奔月故事结合，形成今日最熟悉的英雄形象。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《淮南子》说尧时十日并出，庄稼焦枯，凶兽毒害人民，尧遂使羿射日，并诛杀猰貐、九婴、大风等灾害性怪物。后世通行版本说他射落九日，留一日照耀人间。另有羿向西王母求得不死药、嫦娥取药奔月的故事，说明射日与失妻并非同一事件的简单因果。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 强弓、长箭、天上的多个太阳是后羿最鲜明的标志。射日图中有时以三足乌代表太阳；箭射日乌表现对失控热力的制约，而不是对正常日照与自然生命的否定。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 后羿在诗赋、画像与现代影视中常被塑造成救民英雄，或因爱情而受苦的人物。阅读时宜分辨先秦两汉材料、夏史传说与后起文学，射落九日及徒弟逢蒙害羿等细节也有各自的文本来源。

en.name: Hou Yi
en.title: Archer who restores balance to the blazing sky

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hou Yi commonly names the archer who subdues excessive suns. Ancient sources also describe a ruler called Yi of Youqiong associated with struggles over Xia power; their relationship remains disputed. The heroic archer of texts such as the Huainanzi was later joined more tightly to traditions about Chang’e and the moon.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When ten suns appear together, crops wither and dangerous creatures afflict humanity. In the Huainanzi, the ruler Yao sends Yi to shoot at the suns and eliminate monsters including Jiuying and the Great Wind. Familiar later versions specify that nine suns fall and one remains. Another narrative has Yi obtain an immortality drug from the Queen Mother of the West, only for Chang’e to take it.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A powerful bow, arrows, and several suns identify the archer. Some images represent solar bodies as three-legged crows. Shooting them expresses the regulation of destructive excess, rather than a rejection of the ordinary sunlight needed for life.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Poetry, visual art, and modern screen adaptations present Yi as both public rescuer and tragic husband. Readers should distinguish early mythic accounts from Xia royal legends and later fiction. Details such as nine fallen suns or his death at an apprentice’s hands have separate textual histories.

name: 嫦娥
title: 奔月而居的月中仙子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 嫦娥又称姮娥，是中国月亮传说中的重要女性人物，与羿求不死药的故事相连。汉代材料已经记述其奔月，但动机、结局及月中形态存在差异；今天熟悉的广寒宫仙子形象是在长期文学与图像传统中逐渐形成的。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《淮南子》记羿向西王母求不死药，嫦娥窃取后奔月，却没有展开今日常见的爱情情节。《灵宪》所见传统又说她奔月前占问吉凶，入月后化为蟾蜍。后来的故事有误服、独吞或为防逢蒙夺药而吞服等版本，分别把奔月解释为欲望、命运或牺牲，不能混作一个古老定本。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 明月、飘带、桂树与月兔常围绕嫦娥出现，早期还可见蟾蜍意象。捣药玉兔与伐桂吴刚原有各自传说，后来汇入月宫图景，并不都属于最初的奔月记载。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 嫦娥成为诗词中孤独、离别与长生代价的象征，也与中秋赏月的节令文化相连。现代航天工程以嫦娥命名，延续了望月想象；民俗、文学及科技命名属于不同语境，不表示统一的祭祀制度。

en.name: Chang’e
en.title: Moon-dwelling immortal of separation and longing

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Chang’e, also known as Heng’e, is a central woman in Chinese lunar traditions. Han sources already link her ascent to Yi’s acquisition of an immortality drug. Her motives, fate, and appearance differ across accounts; the elegant inhabitant of a moon palace emerged through a long history of literary and visual elaboration.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Huainanzi says that Yi obtains an immortality drug from the Queen Mother of the West and Chang’e steals it before fleeing to the moon. A tradition recorded in the Lingxian includes divination before her departure and transformation into a toad afterward. Later stories propose accidental ingestion, selfish appropriation, or swallowing the medicine to prevent its theft, giving the episode very different moral meanings.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The full moon, flowing ribbons, a cassia tree, and a moon rabbit commonly surround her. Earlier traditions also feature a toad. The medicine-pounding rabbit and the woodcutter Wu Gang have their own narrative histories within the broader lunar landscape.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Poets use Chang’e to explore loneliness, separation, and the cost of immortality. She is also associated with Mid-Autumn moon viewing. China’s lunar exploration program adopts her name, extending an old imaginative connection to the moon without implying one continuous or uniform religious practice.

name: 西王母
title: 昆仑仙境与长生权能的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 西王母是中国古代文献和宗教中的重要女神，早期《山海经》将她描写为居西方、具豹尾虎齿的威严存在。汉代以后她逐渐成为仙界尊长，与昆仑、长生及升仙相联系；后世王母娘娘形象并不完全等同于早期记载。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《穆天子传》记周穆王西行，在瑶池与西王母宴饮酬唱，呈现远方圣境与王者相会的情景。羿求不死药的传说则突出她掌握长生资源。后来的汉武帝故事写她降临授桃，仙桃须漫长岁月方能成熟；《西游记》进一步把蟠桃宴写成天界盛会，这是小说对传统的再组织。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 早期辨识线索包括豹尾、虎齿、蓬发与戴胜，汉代画像常配青鸟、龙虎及仙人。成熟的宫廷式形象则戴冠端坐，伴随仙桃与瑶池，体现神格历史性的改变。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 西王母在汉代升仙想象、道教女仙谱系与地方宫观中均有地位。她有时被通俗故事写成玉皇配偶，但这不是各类经典一致的关系；其长期独立的权威不应仅被缩减为天帝家庭中的角色。

en.name: Queen Mother of the West
en.title: Goddess of western paradises and longevity

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: The Queen Mother of the West, or Xiwangmu, is an important goddess whose appearance and functions changed substantially. The Classic of Mountains and Seas describes a formidable western being with animal features. Han and later traditions increasingly associate her with Kunlun, immortality, celestial authority, and communities of perfected beings.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Tale of King Mu describes the Zhou ruler journeying west and exchanging songs with Xiwangmu at the Jade Pool. Stories about Yi place the immortality drug under her control. Later tales of Emperor Wu describe her arrival with peaches that ripen only after extraordinary spans of time. Journey to the West reorganizes these traditions into a celestial peach banquet disrupted by the Monkey King.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Early features include tiger teeth, a leopard tail, disheveled hair, and a distinctive headdress. Blue birds and immortals accompany Han representations. Later images favor an enthroned, crowned lady with peaches and a paradisal court beside the Jade Pool.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Xiwangmu is important in Han hopes for transcendence, Daoist lineages of female immortals, and local worship. Popular accounts sometimes make her the Jade Emperor’s wife, but this is not a universal scriptural relationship. Her independent authority long predates that familiar domestic interpretation.

name: 大禹
title: 疏导洪水并奠定王朝的圣王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 大禹是中国上古传说中的治水英雄与夏王朝奠基者，见于《尚书》《孟子》《山海经》等多种材料。其父鲧治水失败，禹继承任务；不同文本对父子经历、神助方式和政治继承的解释各异，神话与古史叙述长期交织。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《孟子》强调禹疏导九河、排通江汉，使洪水归海，治理方法与鲧筑障壅水形成对照。他劳苦奔走，三过家门而不入，成为克己尽职的典型。另有鲧腹生禹、应龙画地助治水以及禹娶涂山氏的传说；后世又把划定九州、铸造九鼎及王位传子启连入其功业。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 禹常持耒耜等治水工具，衣着朴素或作帝王装束，旁见江河山川。九州与九鼎象征治理疆域和政治秩序，但鼎的铸造归属在不同古代记载中也有差别。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 浙江绍兴等地的大禹祭祀与治水遗迹构成地方记忆。儒家常以禹说明为民勤劳、公共责任和圣王德行；现代讨论亦关注洪水经验，但不能把所有神话细节直接当作可验证的水利工程史。

en.name: Yu the Great
en.title: Flood-taming sage and founder of dynastic order

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Yu the Great is the flood-taming hero and traditional founder of the Xia dynasty. He appears in classical, philosophical, and mythic sources that do not agree on every detail. His father Gun fails to control the waters, leaving Yu a task that links environmental restoration, moral authority, and political succession.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Mencius emphasizes Yu’s opening channels and directing rivers toward the sea, contrasting this approach with attempts to obstruct the flood. His dedication is epitomized by passing his home three times without entering. Other traditions describe his extraordinary birth from Gun, assistance from a dragon, and marriage to a woman of Tushan. Later accounts connect him with the Nine Provinces, bronze cauldrons, and succession by his son Qi.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Yu carries digging or agricultural tools and appears beside rivers and mountains, sometimes in plain working dress and sometimes as a ruler. The Nine Provinces and Nine Cauldrons evoke ordered territory, although ancient sources differ about the cauldrons’ origin.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Sites and ceremonies associated with Yu, including those around Shaoxing, sustain regional historical memory. Confucian interpretations emphasize service, diligence, and public responsibility. Flood traditions may preserve environmental experience, but their supernatural episodes cannot simply be treated as directly verifiable records of hydraulic engineering.

name: 伊邪那岐
title: 造岛与禊祓的创生之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊邪那岐是《古事记》《日本书纪》所载的创生神，与伊邪那美共同承担生成国土和诸神的使命。两书保留的次序与异传不完全相同，他既是神代谱系中的父神，也是日本神道禊祓观念的重要叙事来源之一。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 伊邪那岐与伊邪那美立于天浮桥，以天沼矛搅动海水，滴落的盐凝成淤能碁吕岛，随后成婚生岛。伊邪那美死后，他追入黄泉，违约照见其腐败之身，遭追赶而逃，以巨石封住黄泉坂。归来后他入水禊祓，从左眼、右眼和鼻子分别生出天照、月读及须佐之男。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 长矛、海岛与水边净身场景是其常见标志。黄泉坂巨石象征生死边界，禊祓则关涉接触死亡后的污秽与清净，不宜直接套用基督教原罪或道德罪责解释。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊邪那岐见于淡路岛等地神社祭祀，创岛故事与地域圣迹相连。禊祓在后世神道实践中持续发展；古代神话也服务于王权谱系，但今日参拜者对这些叙事的理解不必完全相同。

en.name: Izanagi
en.title: Creator of islands and source of purification

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Izanagi is a generative kami in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, paired with Izanami in the creation of lands and deities. These compilations preserve differing sequences and variants. He is both a father within divine genealogies and a central figure in narratives explaining purification after contact with death.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, the pair stir the sea with a jeweled spear; dripping brine forms an island. After Izanami dies, Izanagi follows her into Yomi but violates her request not to look at her decomposing body. He escapes pursuit and blocks the boundary with a boulder. Washing afterward, he produces Amaterasu from his left eye, Tsukuyomi from his right, and Susanoo from his nose.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The spear, newly formed islands, and ritual washing identify Izanagi. A boulder marks separation between living and dead. Pollution and purification in this setting concern dangerous contact and restored order, not a straightforward equivalent of Christian original sin.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Shrines, including those on Awaji Island, connect Izanagi with local sacred geography. Purification developed into diverse Shinto practices. Ancient court narratives also supported imperial genealogy, but contemporary worshippers need not understand the creation stories or their political implications in one identical way.

name: 伊邪那美
title: 生育诸神并镇守黄泉的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊邪那美是日本神代叙事中的创生女神，与伊邪那岐结为配偶，生成岛屿及众多神灵。《古事记》与《日本书纪》保留不同异传，她由生命之母转为黄泉主宰的过程，使生育、死亡与边界成为同一神话的核心。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 伊邪那美生下火神迦具土时被灼伤，最终死亡，临终及遗体相关情节又产生新的神灵。伊邪那岐追入黄泉求她返回，她说自己已吃过黄泉食物，并禁止他窥看。丈夫违约后，她因羞愤派出追兵；两人在黄泉坂隔石诀别，她宣称每日杀千人，他则回应每日建立一千五百个产屋。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 创岛场景中她与伊邪那岐持矛相对，黄泉故事则以黑暗、追逐与封界巨石为标志。她不是日本传统中一切邪恶的来源，死亡身份也不能抹去原有的生育力量。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 熊野等地的圣地传统与伊邪那美的葬地和死亡叙事相联系。故事把婚姻破裂与人间生死常态结合，但不能当作现实葬俗的单一说明书；地方祭祀往往突出她的母性、土地与再生意义。

en.name: Izanami
en.title: Mother of kami and sovereign of Yomi

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Izanami is the generative female kami paired with Izanagi in Japanese accounts of the divine age. Together they produce islands and numerous deities. The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki preserve different versions, linking her maternal role with a later association with Yomi, the realm reached after death in these narratives.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Giving birth to the fire kami Kagutsuchi fatally burns Izanami, while further deities arise around her dying body. Izanagi follows her to Yomi, where she has already eaten its food, and she forbids him to look at her. His disobedience leads to pursuit and separation at a blocked pass. She vows a thousand deaths daily; he counters with fifteen hundred births, establishing the rhythm of human mortality.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Creation scenes pair her with Izanagi and their spear. Darkness, a forbidden sight, pursuing forces, and the boundary boulder identify the Yomi episode. Her association with death does not make her the universal source of evil in Japanese traditions.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Sacred sites in regions such as Kumano connect Izanami with burial and the landscape of death. The narrative joins marital rupture to human mortality without serving as a complete guide to Japanese funerary practice. Local worship may emphasize maternal, terrestrial, or regenerative dimensions of her presence.

name: 天照大神
title: 照耀高天原的太阳女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 天照大神是日本神道中重要的太阳神，居高天原，并在宫廷神话中被奉为皇室祖神。《古事记》说她由伊邪那岐禊祓左眼而生，《日本书纪》另存出生异传；她的祭祀中心与伊势神宫紧密相连。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 须佐之男在高天原破坏田畔、污损祭场，又把剥皮马投入织殿，引发灾祸，天照遂隐入天石屋，天地陷入黑暗。诸神在洞外悬镜挂玉，天宇受卖起舞逗得众神大笑，诱她探看；天手力男将她拉出，并以注连绳阻止退回。后来她命孙邇邇艺下降苇原中国，展开天孙降临谱系。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 太阳、神镜与洞窟是主要标志，八咫镜尤其联系神圣临在与皇室宝物传统。神社的神体不一定采用人形偶像，镜的宗教意义也不只是普通的外貌映照。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊势神宫以内宫奉祀天照，式年迁宫使建筑与工艺周期性更新。她与皇权的联系曾被近代国家制度重新塑造；理解当代神道须区分古代神话、近代国家神道以及今天多样的参拜实践。

en.name: Amaterasu
en.title: Solar kami of the High Plain of Heaven

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Amaterasu is a major solar kami in Shinto and the imperial ancestress in court mythology. The Kojiki has her emerge from Izanagi’s left eye during purification, while the Nihon Shoki preserves alternatives. Her principal cultic association is with the Inner Shrine at Ise, rather than a single universal Japanese theology.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After Susanoo damages fields and desecrates sacred spaces, culminating in a flayed horse thrown into a weaving hall, Amaterasu withdraws into a rock cave. Darkness spreads. The assembled kami hang a mirror and jewels, while Ame-no-Uzume dances and provokes laughter. Curious, Amaterasu looks outside and is drawn out; a sacred rope prevents retreat. Later she commissions her grandson Ninigi’s descent, grounding the imperial ancestral narrative.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Sunlight, the cave, and especially the sacred mirror are central identifiers. The Yata mirror is associated with divine presence and imperial regalia. Shinto sacred objects need not be anthropomorphic statues, and the mirror signifies more than ordinary visual reflection.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Ise’s Inner Shrine venerates Amaterasu, and periodic rebuilding renews buildings and craft traditions. Her connection with imperial authority was reshaped by modern state institutions. Ancient mythology, modern State Shinto, and present-day shrine practices must therefore be distinguished rather than treated as an unchanged whole.

name: 须佐之男
title: 越界而降伏大蛇的勇猛神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 须佐之男是日本神话中的重要神灵，在《古事记》中由伊邪那岐洗鼻而生，与天照、月读并称三贵子。他兼有狂暴越界者与地方救世英雄的面貌，虽常被称为风暴神，其职能与祭祀范围并不止于天气。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 须佐之男因在高天原肆虐而遭驱逐，来到出云后见老夫妇为女儿奇稻田姬悲泣：八岐大蛇每年来吞一女，如今只剩最后一人。他将女子化作梳子护在发间，命酿烈酒置于八处，引大蛇饮醉后斩杀。剖其尾时发现宝剑，献给天照，后来与草薙剑的宝物传统相连。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 多头多尾的大蛇、酒槽、长剑与发梳是斩蛇故事的识别线索。草薙剑出于蛇尾的情节联系皇室宝物，但须佐之男形象也常强调乡土婚姻、诗歌与开拓。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 出云神乐经常演出八岐大蛇故事。后世须佐之男又与牛头天王等信仰发生习合，关联祇园及疫病防护；这些历史形成的联系不宜全部倒推为《古事记》原有的同一套神格与仪式。

en.name: Susanoo
en.title: Disruptive kami and slayer of the great serpent

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Susanoo is an important Japanese kami with both disruptive and protective roles. In the Kojiki he emerges from Izanagi’s nose and belongs with Amaterasu and Tsukuyomi to the three noble children. Often called a storm god, he also has associations with local settlement, marriage, poetry, and protection from dangerous forces.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Expelled after his offenses in heaven, Susanoo reaches Izumo and finds parents grieving because an eight-headed serpent will devour their last daughter, Kushinadahime. He transforms her into a comb for safekeeping in his hair, prepares strong liquor in eight stations, and kills the intoxicated monster. Inside its tail he discovers a sword, which he offers to Amaterasu and which becomes connected with the Kusanagi regalia tradition.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The many-headed serpent, liquor vats, sword, and protective comb identify the Izumo episode. The blade discovered inside the tail links the tale to imperial regalia. Other representations emphasize a local founder and husband rather than an embodiment of violent weather.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Izumo kagura regularly dramatizes the serpent’s defeat. In later religious history, Susanoo became associated with Gozu Tennō, Gion traditions, and protection against epidemics. These combinations developed over time and should not all be read back into the earliest surviving court compilations as one original system.

name: 月读命
title: 司掌月与夜之秩序的神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 月读命又写作月夜见尊，是日本神话中的月神，与天照和须佐之男构成重要的同辈神组。《古事记》叙其由伊邪那岐右眼而生，但后续事迹很少；《日本书纪》异传则保存月读与食物神冲突的较完整叙述。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《日本书纪》一则异传中，天照派月读拜访保食神。保食神转向大地吐出饭食，又向海与山吐出鱼兽款待来客；月读认为食物污秽，拔剑杀死主人。天照得知后斥责月读，宣称不再相见，于是日月分离。使者再访遗体，发现稻、粟、麦豆与蚕等，解释人间食物和养蚕的起源。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 月轮、夜色和剑可作为辨识线索，但月读没有像天照神镜那样普遍稳定的单一标志。现代作品赋予的发色、服饰或性格设定，不等于古代文本已有明确规定。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊势的月读宫及其他地方神社保存相关祭祀。应注意《古事记》中杀食物神的是须佐之男、对象为大气都比卖，不能与月读版本逐字拼接；相似母题在不同文献中承担不同的神话关系。

en.name: Tsukuyomi
en.title: Lunar kami associated with night and separation

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Tsukuyomi is the lunar kami grouped with Amaterasu and Susanoo among Izanagi’s important children. The Kojiki places his birth in the washing of the right eye but offers little subsequent narrative. A variant in the Nihon Shoki provides a fuller account involving a food deity and separation from the sun.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Amaterasu sends Tsukuyomi to visit Ukemochi, who produces rice, fish, and game from her mouth to entertain him. Disgusted by their bodily origin, Tsukuyomi kills his host with a sword. Amaterasu condemns the act and refuses to see him again, explaining the separation of sun and moon. A later visitor finds grains and silkworms arising from the body, linking the death to human subsistence.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A lunar disc, night scenery, or a sword may identify Tsukuyomi, but no single visual attribute is as consistently established as Amaterasu’s mirror. Elaborate costumes, hair colors, and personalities in modern entertainment are not specifications supplied by ancient sources.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Tsukuyomi is worshipped at Ise’s Tsukiyomi-no-miya and other shrines. The Kojiki assigns a related food-deity killing to Susanoo and Ōgetsuhime instead. These are parallel but distinct narratives, not interchangeable episodes that can be combined without acknowledging their different textual relationships and narrative settings.

name: 大国主
title: 经营国土并结缘的出云大神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 大国主是出云神话中的核心神灵，名号众多，与大穴牟迟等名称相联系。《古事记》将他置于须佐之男的后裔谱系，但不同文本关系有异。他既是经营苇原中国的国土神，也在后世信仰中广受结缘与福德祈愿。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 大国主的兄长们欺骗受伤的白兔，使其以盐水和风治疗而更加痛苦；他教白兔用清水洗身、卧于蒲黄，因而获其预言帮助。后来他赴根之国，受须佐之男试炼，与须势理毗卖相助脱险，继而与少彦名协作营造国土。天上使者要求让国时，他接受安排，自己的祭祀居所也成为谈判内容。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 白兔、大袋与出云大社是常见线索。他后来与源出印度背景的大黑天发生习合，形成持槌背袋的福神形象；两者相关，却不能把全部历史身份完全抹平。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 出云大社以大国主为主祭神，结缘的含义可超越恋爱而涉及人与人、事物与机缘。让国故事调和地方神与天孙权威，既有政治神话意义，也在神乐、地方叙事与今日参拜文化中持续被解释。

en.name: Ōkuninushi
en.title: Land-making deity of Izumo and sacred connections

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ōkuninushi is central to the Izumo traditions and appears under several names, including Ōnamuchi. The Kojiki places him among Susanoo’s descendants, though genealogies vary. He is a maker and organizer of the earthly land, later widely approached for beneficial relationships and good fortune rather than romance alone.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When his brothers mistreat an injured white hare, Ōkuninushi recommends fresh water and reed pollen, earning its prophetic support. He later survives trials in Susanoo’s realm with help from Suseribime, whom he marries. Together with Sukunabikona he develops the land. When heavenly messengers demand its transfer to Amaterasu’s descendants, he ultimately agrees, while arrangements for his own magnificent sacred dwelling become part of the settlement.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The white hare, a large sack, and Izumo Taisha are familiar identifiers. Historical combination with Daikokuten produced an overlapping fortune-god image carrying a mallet and bag. Their association is important, but their origins and earlier identities are not identical.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Izumo Taisha centers on Ōkuninushi, and prayers for enmusubi concern many kinds of meaningful connection. The land-transfer narrative negotiates relationships between local authority and heavenly descendants. Shrine traditions, regional storytelling, and kagura continue to interpret this politically charged myth in varied religious and cultural ways.

name: 稻荷大神
title: 护佑稻作生计与繁荣的神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 稻荷是日本广泛受奉祀的神祇称谓，与稻米、农业、商业和生活繁荣相联系。各社祭神配置与性别表现不尽相同，宇迦之御魂等神常与之关联；稻荷并非一个在所有神社都有固定容貌和单一传记的角色。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 伏见稻荷的缘起传统与秦氏相关，一则古代地方传说叙秦伊吕具以米饼为靶，米饼化白鸟飞落山峰，落处生稻，显现稻荷的神异。中世以后，稻荷信仰与佛教荼吉尼天等发生交涉，狐狸使者故事也不断增多；这些缘起与灵验记构成地方叙事群，而非同一场创世冒险。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 朱红鸟居、稻穗、宝珠以及衔钥匙或卷物的狐狸常见于稻荷神社。狐狸一般被解释为神使，不应把每尊狐像都称为稻荷本体，也不宜将其一概视作妖狐。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 京都伏见稻荷大社是重要中心，成列鸟居多出自个人或商家的奉纳。稻荷信仰随城市商业扩展而超出农耕，遍及店铺与家庭神龛；其多样性体现神佛习合、地方组织和日常祈愿的历史积累。

en.name: Inari
en.title: Kami of rice, livelihoods, and flourishing

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Inari is a widely worshipped designation associated with rice, agriculture, commerce, and prosperity. Individual shrines differ in their divine groupings and representations of gender; Ukanomitama is among the kami closely connected with Inari. There is no single fixed appearance or universally shared personal biography covering every Inari tradition.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: An origin tradition associated with the Hata family recounts Irogu using a rice cake as an archery target. It transforms into a white bird, flies to a mountain peak, and rice grows where it lands. Later traditions connect Inari with Buddhist figures such as Dakiniten and develop numerous stories of fox messengers and miraculous assistance. These narratives form a diverse local corpus, not one continuous creation epic.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Vermilion torii, rice sheaves, wish-fulfilling jewels, and foxes holding keys or scrolls identify Inari shrines. Foxes are commonly understood as messengers rather than automatically being Inari’s own body. Their presence does not imply that every fox image represents a malicious spirit.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Fushimi Inari Taisha in Kyoto is a major center, its many torii reflecting offerings by individuals and businesses. Worship expanded beyond farming into urban trades, shops, and domestic shrines. Inari’s diversity reflects local institutions, everyday petitions, and centuries of interaction between kami worship and Buddhism.

name: 木花咲耶姬
title: 以火中生产证明誓言的花之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 木花咲耶姬是日本神话中山神大山津见的女儿，嫁给天孙邇邇艺，进入皇室祖先谱系。其名令人联想到繁花盛开，后世又成为富士山浅间信仰的重要祭神，但早期婚姻神话与火山祭祀并非起初就完全重合。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 大山津见本欲把木花咲耶姬与姐姐石长姬一同嫁给邇邇艺，后者因嫌姐姐容貌而只留妹妹。父亲解释石长象征长久、花开象征繁盛，由此说明天孙寿命如花有期。妹妹一夜有孕后遭丈夫怀疑，遂封闭产屋并点火，宣称若孩子属天孙便会平安，最终在烈焰中生下诸子。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 樱花、富士山、火焰中的产屋与母子形象有助辨识。花开既象征美丽和生命，也提示短暂；火中生产强调誓言与亲子身份，不宜据此鼓励现实中的危险试验。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 浅间神社网络尤其将她与富士山联系，祈求镇火、防灾与安产。不同地方对火山神及其配偶的解释经过历史发展；她在现代常被简化为樱花女神，但山岳、王统和生育同样是关键语境。

en.name: Konohanasakuya-hime
en.title: Blossom princess who gives birth amid flames

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Konohanasakuya-hime is a daughter of the mountain kami Ōyamatsumi and wife of the heavenly descendant Ninigi. Her marriage places her within imperial ancestral narratives. Later worship closely links her with Mount Fuji and Sengen shrines, although the early marriage account and the history of volcano worship are not identical.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Ōyamatsumi offers both Konohanasakuya-hime and her sister Iwanagahime to Ninigi, who rejects the latter for her appearance. Their father explains that rock signifies enduring life while blossoms signify flourishing, so rejecting the elder sister limits the descendants’ longevity. When Ninigi doubts the paternity of a sudden pregnancy, Konohanasakuya-hime seals and burns her birthing hut, declaring that true heavenly offspring will survive. She delivers her children unharmed.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Blossoms, Mount Fuji, a burning birth hut, and mother-and-child imagery identify her. Flowers evoke both beauty and impermanence. The fiery birth establishes an oath and lineage within a sacred narrative, not a model for testing real pregnancies or personal fidelity.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Sengen shrines associate her with Fuji, protection from fire, safe childbirth, and volcanic danger. These relationships developed through regional religious history. Calling her simply a cherry-blossom goddess misses her important connections with mountains, dynastic ancestry, maternal power, and the management of threatening natural forces.

name: 梵天
title: 印度教宇宙生成的创造神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 梵天是印度教传统中的创造神，常与毗湿奴、湿婆并列为三相神，但这一框架不概括所有宗派。他是有形象与叙事的神祇，不等同于哲学上表示终极实在的梵；其与生主等早期创生观念的联系也经历了发展。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一些往世书叙述毗湿奴卧于宇宙海，脐中生莲，梵天在莲上出现，继而安排世界与众生。另有梵天与毗湿奴争论谁更伟大，湿婆显为无尽光柱，二神上下寻端而不得；梵天在部分版本中谎称已找到顶端，因而受罚。这些叙事表达特定宗派的神学立场，并非所有信众共同排序。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 梵天通常四面四臂，持吠陀书卷、念珠、水罐或祭勺，坐骑为鹅或天鹅形的罕娑。四面寓示方位与知识，不应将其与无人格的终极实在概念混同。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 梵天独立神庙较少，拉贾斯坦邦普什卡是著名礼拜中心，但庙少不等于无人敬奉。印度教各传统对创造、维持与消解有不同解释，阅读往世书应尊重活态信仰，避免以单一故事替全部宗派定论。

en.name: Brahmā
en.title: Creator deity within Hindu cosmic traditions

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Brahmā is a Hindu creator deity often grouped with Vishnu and Shiva in the Trimurti, a framework not equally central to every community. He is distinct from brahman, the philosophical term for ultimate reality. His identity developed in relation to earlier ideas of generation and lordship associated with Prajapati.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Some Puranic accounts place Brahmā on a lotus growing from Vishnu’s navel as Vishnu rests on the cosmic ocean; Brahmā then organizes creation. Another narrative has Brahmā and Vishnu dispute supremacy before Shiva appears as an endless pillar of light. They search unsuccessfully for its limits, and Brahmā is punished in versions where he falsely claims success. Such accounts articulate particular theological perspectives rather than a universally accepted ranking.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Four faces and four arms are common, with Vedic books, prayer beads, a water pot, or a sacrificial ladle. His vehicle is the goose or swanlike hamsa. The faces suggest comprehensive knowledge and orientation across the directions of space.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Independent Brahmā temples are relatively uncommon, with Pushkar in Rajasthan a famous pilgrimage center. Rarity does not mean absence of reverence. Hindu traditions offer varied understandings of creation and divine relationships, so Puranic stories should be read within their living devotional and sectarian contexts.

name: 毗湿奴
title: 护持宇宙并以化身临世的神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 毗湿奴是印度教重要神祇，在毗湿奴派传统中被奉为至高主，具有维持宇宙与护持达摩的力量。从吠陀中的跨步神到史诗与往世书中的至尊形象，其神学表达不断发展；他不只是抽象分工中的保管者。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 搅乳海故事中，众神与阿修罗以曼陀罗山为搅棒、婆苏吉蛇为绳求取甘露，毗湿奴化为巨龟托住山体，又在部分版本中以迷人的摩诃妮形象分配甘露。他也化为人狮那罗辛哈，黄昏时在门槛上以利爪杀死自恃赐福的暴君，突破其免死条件，护佑虔诚的钵罗诃罗陀。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 四臂常持法螺、妙见轮、权杖和莲花，蓝色身躯与神鹰迦楼罗便于识别。他卧于舍沙蛇上、吉祥天女相伴的图像表达宇宙秩序与安稳，而非普通睡眠场面。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 罗摩与克里希纳是其最有影响的化身，但十化身名单并不处处相同。南亚及海外庙宇、朝圣和奉爱诗歌体现持续的敬奉，不同毗湿奴派对至尊与化身关系有精细解释，不能压成单一神话谱表。

en.name: Vishnu
en.title: Divine sustainer who descends to restore dharma

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Vishnu is a major Hindu deity and the supreme Lord in many Vaishnava traditions. His identity develops from Vedic references to cosmic strides into extensive epic and Puranic theologies. Sustaining the world means active care for cosmic and moral order, not merely a passive role in a three-part divine division.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: During the churning of the ocean, gods and asuras use a mountain and the serpent Vasuki to seek immortality nectar. Vishnu supports the mountain as the tortoise Kurma and, in some accounts, distributes the nectar as Mohini. As Narasimha, the man-lion, he protects Prahlada by killing a tyrant at twilight on a threshold, using claws to evade the carefully specified protections granted to his opponent.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Four arms commonly hold a conch, discus, mace, and lotus. Blue coloring and the eagle Garuda are familiar identifiers. Reclining on the serpent Shesha with Lakshmi nearby expresses cosmic stability and divine presence rather than simply an episode of ordinary sleep.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Rama and Krishna are especially influential avatars, but lists of ten incarnations differ. Temples, pilgrimages, and devotional poetry sustain active worship across South Asia and diaspora communities. Vaishnava schools offer sophisticated, differing accounts of the relationship between the supreme Lord, divine manifestations, and devoted persons.

name: 湿婆
title: 以苦行与舞蹈更新宇宙的大神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 湿婆是印度教主要神祇，在湿婆派中常被尊为至高实在与慈悲之主。他与吠陀鲁陀罗等传统有历史联系，兼具苦行者、家长、舞者与解脱赐予者的面貌；简单称其为破坏神，会遮蔽消解与再生相连的神学意义。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 恒河从天界降临时水势足以冲毁大地，湿婆以盘结长发承接并缓释水流，使其成为人间圣河。搅乳海时剧毒出现，他为保护世界将毒含于喉中，形成青颈标志。另一组叙事描写他以宇宙舞蹈显示创造、维持与消解，并以抬起的足赐予庇护与解脱，而非只表现毁灭。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 第三眼、发髻新月、恒河、三叉戟、小鼓与公牛南迪都是重要标志。林伽是其神圣临在的礼拜形式，不能只按现代世俗视角作单一生殖解释或当成装饰。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 湿婆节守夜、圣地朝拜与庙宇日常供奉延续至今。南印度舞王铜像、喜马拉雅苦行想象和家庭中的湿婆各有侧重；不同宗派理解不尽相同，却都不能被缩减为与其他神争胜的奇幻角色。

en.name: Shiva
en.title: Great Lord of transformation, asceticism, and dance

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Shiva is a major Hindu deity, revered in Shaiva traditions as supreme reality and a gracious Lord. Historically connected with Vedic Rudra, he combines the roles of ascetic, householder, dancer, and giver of liberation. Describing him only as a destroyer obscures the relationship between dissolution, renewal, and saving grace.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When the heavenly Ganges descends with force enough to devastate the earth, Shiva catches her in his matted hair and releases her waters safely. During the ocean’s churning, he contains a deadly poison in his throat to protect the world, explaining his blue neck. His cosmic dance presents creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, and grace as intertwined divine activities, with a raised foot offering refuge and liberation.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The third eye, crescent moon, matted hair, Ganges, trident, drum, and bull Nandi are characteristic signs. The linga is a revered form of divine presence; reducing it to decoration or one exclusively sexual interpretation misrepresents its ritual significance.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Shivaratri vigils, pilgrimages, and daily temple offerings remain active practices. South Indian dancing bronzes, Himalayan ascetic imagery, and domestic representations emphasize different dimensions. Shaiva schools vary in theology, but none can be adequately represented by treating Shiva simply as a fantasy character competing with other gods.

name: 提毗
title: 以多种形态显现的神圣女性

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 提毗意为女神，可作尊称，也指印度教神圣女性的总体表达。在性力派传统中，大女神与沙克蒂被奉为宇宙根本力量；杜尔迦、迦梨等形态各有叙事与祭祀，不能把所有地方女神简单认作毫无差别的同一人物。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《女神颂》叙水牛魔摩醯沙击败众神，各神光辉汇聚为女神，并把武器交给她。她骑狮与魔军交战，面对摩醯沙不断变形，最终在其显露真身时将其诛灭。其他篇章描写女神眉间生出迦梨，以及对付血滴化敌的罗讫多毗阇，突出神圣力量为恢复秩序而采取多样形态。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 杜尔迦常骑狮或虎、持多种武器、踏伏水牛魔；迦梨常见深色身躯、项链与伸舌等标志。具体图像有宗教与地区差异，多臂表示能力，不是生理怪异。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 九夜节、杜尔迦祭与各地女神庙体现活跃的礼拜生活。温柔母性和战斗威力在信众理解中可以并存，不能把严厉形象等同邪恶；提毗在不同哲学中作为至尊、力量或配偶的地位也不相同。

en.name: Devī
en.title: Divine feminine manifest in many sacred forms

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Devī means goddess and can function as an honorific or a broad designation of the divine feminine. In Shakta traditions, the Great Goddess and Shakti are understood as fundamental cosmic power. Forms such as Durga and Kali have distinct narratives and practices, while local goddess traditions retain meaningful differences.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Devi Mahatmya, the buffalo demon Mahisha defeats the gods. Their radiance combines into the Goddess, and they equip her with weapons. Riding a lion, she battles his forces and kills him as he emerges from changing animal forms. Other episodes describe Kali springing from the Goddess’s brow and overcoming an enemy whose spilled blood produces more warriors, demonstrating power that adapts to restore order.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Durga commonly rides a lion or tiger, bears many weapons, and overcomes the buffalo demon. Kali’s dark body, garland, and extended tongue belong to different iconographic contexts. Multiple arms communicate divine capacities rather than a claim about abnormal human anatomy.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Navaratri, Durga Puja, and countless regional temples sustain living goddess worship. Maternal care and formidable battle imagery can coexist within devotion; fierce forms are not automatically evil. Different philosophical and devotional traditions understand Devī as supreme reality, divine power, or consort in distinct ways.

name: 象头神
title: 掌管开端与障碍的智慧之主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 象头神即伽内什，是印度教广受敬奉的神祇，通常被视为湿婆与帕尔瓦蒂之子，兼有赐福、智慧与统领神众的身份。他既能清除障碍，也能设置必要的阻碍，因此并非保证所有愿望立即实现的好运符号。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一则著名往世书故事说，帕尔瓦蒂造出少年守门，湿婆归来遭阻拦，冲突中将其斩首，随后以象首使他复生并授予尊位。另有象头神与兄弟竞绕世界的故事，他绕行父母以表父母即世界，因智慧获胜。作为《摩诃婆罗多》书记的传统则强调他与毗耶娑约定不停口述及理解后再写。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 象首、圆腹、断牙、甜食和鼠类坐骑最为醒目，手中常持索与钩。断牙来历有不同说法，写史诗只是其中之一；其亲切形象同时保留庄严的礼拜意义。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 许多印度教仪式、求学与商业开端先礼敬象头神，象头神节尤其以造像迎请和送像入水闻名。家庭与公共庆典的方式不同，现代环保材料也影响实践；不应只将其视为流行设计图案。

en.name: Ganesha
en.title: Elephant-headed lord of beginnings and obstacles

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ganesha is widely revered in Hindu traditions as a lord of beginnings, wisdom, and obstacles, usually the son of Shiva and Parvati. His authority includes both removing obstructions and placing them when appropriate. He is therefore more than a general good-luck emblem promising immediate success for every human undertaking.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In a famous account, Parvati creates a boy to guard her door. When he blocks Shiva, a conflict ends in his beheading; Shiva restores him with an elephant’s head and grants him honor. Another story has Ganesha win a race around the world by circling his parents, treating them as his universe. A scribal tradition pairs him with Vyasa in composing the Mahabharata under demanding conditions of uninterrupted dictation and understanding.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: An elephant head, rounded belly, broken tusk, sweets, and a mouse vehicle identify him. A noose and goad are frequent attributes. The broken tusk has several explanations; its use as a writing tool belongs to one narrative tradition.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Many Hindu ceremonies, educational ventures, and businesses begin by honoring Ganesha. Ganesh Chaturthi includes welcoming images and later immersing them, with household and public forms of celebration. Environmental concerns increasingly influence materials and immersion practices, while devotion remains more substantial than his popularity as a design motif.

name: 哈奴曼
title: 以力量与奉爱侍奉罗摩的猴神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 哈奴曼是印度教《罗摩衍那》传统的重要猴神，通常被称为风神之子，母亲为安阇那。他以强大力量、机敏智慧和对罗摩的忠诚闻名，在不同宗派中具有多重神学解释，不能仅被视为史诗中的动物伙伴。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 悉多遭罗波那掳走后，哈奴曼越海抵达楞伽，在无忧园找到她，出示罗摩的信物并带回消息。他被俘后以燃烧的尾巴焚烧城中建筑，随后返回。战争中，罗什曼那重伤，需要喜马拉雅山的药草救治；哈奴曼因无法辨明药草而搬来整座山，体现为救人不惜承担艰险的奉爱。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 猴面、人身、长尾、权杖与手托药山是常见标志。他跪拜罗摩或展示胸中罗摩与悉多的图像，强调力量服从奉爱；朱红涂饰与健壮体态也见于许多庙宇造像。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 哈奴曼赞歌、诞辰节庆与庙宇参拜延续至今，摔跤和体能训练传统也常尊奉他。其形象随《罗摩衍那》传播至东南亚，但当地戏剧中的性格与经历并不完全相同，不宜混作单一版本。

en.name: Hanuman
en.title: Monkey deity of strength and devoted service to Rama

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hanuman is a revered monkey deity in Hindu Ramayana traditions, commonly described as the son of the wind god and Anjana. Extraordinary strength, intelligence, and loyalty to Rama define his character. Different communities interpret his divine status in different ways, extending far beyond the role of an animal companion.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Hanuman leaps across the sea to Lanka, finds the abducted Sita, and presents Rama’s token before returning with news. Captured by her enemies, he sets buildings ablaze with his burning tail. Later, unable to identify the healing herb needed for the wounded Lakshmana, he carries an entire mountain to the battlefield, making strength an expression of devoted service.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A monkey face, long tail, mace, and mountain held aloft are familiar identifiers. Images showing him kneeling before Rama or revealing Rama and Sita within his chest emphasize devotion. Vermilion coloring and a powerful physique also appear frequently in temple images and popular devotional art.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Hymns, birthday festivals, and temple visits sustain Hanuman’s living worship. Wrestling and physical training communities often honor him as well. Ramayana performance traditions throughout Southeast Asia adapt his personality and adventures differently, so their distinctive portrayals should not be collapsed into one supposedly universal account.

name: 檀君
title: 连接天界谱系与古朝鲜开国的始祖

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 檀君王俭是朝鲜半岛传统中古朝鲜的开国始祖，通常被叙述为桓雄与熊女之子。《三国遗事》保存其著名故事，但成书远晚于故事设定的年代；传统纪年中的公元前二三三三年，不是已获考古证实的建国日期。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 桓雄降临人间后，一熊一虎希望成为人，接受避日并食艾蒜的考验。熊坚持下来化为女子，随后祈求生子，桓雄与她结合，生下檀君。檀君建立古朝鲜，以平壤等地为都的说法见于不同记述。他漫长的统治与后来退隐为山神的结局，把王权、土地与神圣祖先联系起来。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 白须长者、冠服、神圣山林以及熊的母系线索常用于表现檀君，但这些并非同时代肖像。其形象着重始祖和开国者身份，不能仅凭一张后世画像推断古代服制。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 檀君传统见于民族历史叙述、开天节纪念及大倧教等宗教实践，不同群体赋予其不同含义。研究时应区分古朝鲜历史、文献中的始祖叙事与现代民族认同，既不混同史证，也不抹去文化意义。

en.name: Dangun
en.title: Ancestral founder of Gojoseon with a heavenly lineage

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Dangun Wanggeom is the ancestral founder of Gojoseon in Korean tradition, usually the son of Hwanung and the bear woman Ungnyeo. The Samguk Yusa preserves the best known account centuries after its setting. The traditional foundation date of 2333 BCE should not be presented as an archaeologically established historical date.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: A bear and tiger seek human form after Hwanung descends to earth. Only the bear completes the prescribed ordeal, becomes a woman, and later bears Dangun through union with Hwanung. Dangun establishes Gojoseon, with accounts differing about capitals and chronology. His exceptionally long reign and eventual retirement as a mountain spirit connect kingship, territory, and sacred ancestral authority.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Later representations often show an elderly bearded ruler, ceremonial robes, sacred mountains, or references to his bear ancestry. These are retrospective images rather than contemporary portraits. They emphasize ancestral foundation and legitimate rule, and cannot independently establish what actual clothing or royal ceremony looked like in early Gojoseon.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Dangun appears in historical identity, National Foundation Day commemorations, and religious movements including Daejonggyo. These settings do not assign identical meanings to him. Careful interpretation distinguishes the history of Gojoseon, literary accounts of its sacred founder, and modern national narratives without dismissing their continuing cultural significance.

name: 桓雄
title: 降临神市并治理人间的天界之子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 桓雄是朝鲜半岛檀君叙事中的天界之子，父亲通常称桓因。他希望关怀人间生活，获准率众下降，并成为檀君之父。这一谱系见于中世纪保存的文献，其天界称谓也反映佛教词汇与地方传统的交汇。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《三国遗事》叙桓雄携天符印，率三千随从降于太伯山神檀树下，设立神市，并与风伯、雨师、云师治理谷物、疾病、刑罚和善恶等事务。熊与虎求成人时，他给出艾蒜与避日的条件。熊女完成考验后渴望生子，桓雄与她结合，使降世治理的故事进一步连接到檀君开国。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 神檀树、山巅、天符印以及风雨云的随从构成主要辨识线索。现代绘画常赋予他天界君长的冠服，但固定容貌缺少早期依据；他与父亲桓因、儿子檀君应清楚区分。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 桓雄把天界授权、农业秩序与始祖谱系连成一体，常与弘益人间的理想一起解释。后世宗教和民族文化各有发挥，具体降临地点也有不同认定，不宜把任何一种现代解释直接当成远古事实。

en.name: Hwanung
en.title: Heavenly son who descends to establish sacred government

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hwanung is the heavenly son in Korean Dangun traditions, usually identified as the child of Hwanin and father of Dangun. He desires to care for the human world and receives permission to descend. Medieval textual transmission preserves this genealogy within language shaped partly by interaction between Buddhist terminology and local traditions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Samguk Yusa describes Hwanung descending beneath a sacred tree on Mount Taebaek with heavenly seals and three thousand followers. Wind, rain, and cloud officials assist his government of human affairs. He prescribes an ordeal for a bear and tiger seeking humanity. The successful bear woman later becomes his partner and gives birth to Dangun, linking heavenly governance to foundation.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The sacred tree, mountain summit, heavenly seals, and officials of wind, rain, and clouds offer the clearest identifying clues. Modern pictures may dress Hwanung as a celestial sovereign, but no single early portrait fixes his appearance. He should remain distinct from Hwanin and Dangun.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Hwanung connects heavenly authorization with agricultural order and ancestral kingship. Later interpretations often associate him with the ideal of broadly benefiting humanity. Religious movements and national narratives develop these themes differently, while competing geographical identifications of his descent should not be treated as established facts about remote antiquity.

name: 熊女
title: 由熊化人并孕育檀君的始祖之母

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 熊女是朝鲜半岛檀君故事中的女性始祖，其名称直接指出由熊变为女子的经历，而非另有明确传世的个人姓名。《三国遗事》叙她成为桓雄的伴侣、檀君的母亲，使动物祖源与人间王统在同一谱系相遇。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 熊与虎同居洞中，向桓雄请求变成人。桓雄赐艾与蒜，并要求百日不见阳光；虎未能坚持，熊则守禁，在二十一日后成为女子。她没有配偶，常在神檀树下祈愿怀孕。桓雄暂化人身与她结合，生下檀君。故事既以耐心解释变化，也让她主动求子成为开国谱系的重要环节。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 熊、洞穴、艾蒜、神檀树与怀抱婴儿的女性，是后世描绘她的主要线索。她并非只代表野兽被征服；母性、转变与地方祖源同样重要，单一图腾解释仍须审慎。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 熊女形象常见于始祖故事的教育、雕塑与现代重述。关于熊族群、婚姻联盟或仪式禁忌的解读属于研究假说，不能代替文本本身；现代讨论也重新关注她的愿望与行动，而不只把她视为附属人物。

en.name: Ungnyeo
en.title: Bear woman and ancestral mother of Dangun

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ungnyeo is the ancestral mother in Korean Dangun traditions. Her designation means bear woman rather than preserving an independently recorded personal name. In the Samguk Yusa she becomes Hwanung’s partner and Dangun’s mother, bringing animal ancestry and the genealogy of a human kingdom into one sacred narrative.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: A bear and tiger ask Hwanung for human form. He gives them mugwort and garlic and requires a hundred days without sunlight. The tiger fails, but the bear becomes a woman after twenty one days. Without a husband, she prays beneath the sacred tree for a child. Hwanung assumes human form, joins her, and fathers Dangun.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A bear, cave, mugwort, garlic, sacred tree, and woman carrying a child are common visual clues. Her role includes transformation, maternal agency, and ancestral belonging, not simply the conquest of an animal nature. Explanations that treat every detail as evidence of one ancient bear totem remain interpretive hypotheses.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Ungnyeo appears in education, monuments, and contemporary retellings of Korean foundation traditions. Scholarly readings propose clan alliances, ritual prohibitions, or animal ancestry, but none should replace the surviving narrative as unquestioned fact. Modern interpretations also recover her wishes and actions rather than reducing her to a secondary genealogical function.

name: 朱蒙
title: 以神异出生与善射著称的高句丽始祖

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 朱蒙是高句丽开国君主的传统名字，后尊为东明圣王，建国年代通常系于公元前三十七年。碑铭与史书保存不同层次的神圣谱系，常称其母为柳花、父为天界人物解慕漱；历史王统与神异诞生在传述中相交。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 柳花受日光照临而产卵，卵屡遭弃置却获动物保护，最终孵出朱蒙。他自幼善射，因受王子嫉妒而离开扶余。逃至河边时，他向天与河神求助，鱼鳖浮起搭成桥梁，使追兵无法追及。此后他与伙伴建立高句丽，另一些叙事又以儿子寻父和断剑相合来说明王位继承。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 弓箭、巨卵、日光与鱼鳖桥是关键线索，表现射术、天裔和自然援助。现代影视常增加武器与爱情情节，不能把荧幕人物造型直接当作古代文献中的固定形象。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 朱蒙故事见于好太王碑、《三国史记》及《东明王篇》等材料，细节与政治语境并不一致。它说明高句丽王权的神圣来历，也在现代文化中不断重述，阅读时须区分史料层次、文学扩展与影视创作。

en.name: Jumong
en.title: Archer and sacred founder of Goguryeo

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Jumong is the traditional founder of Goguryeo, honored as King Dongmyeong, with his accession conventionally dated to 37 BCE. Inscriptions and histories preserve differing sacred genealogies. Yuhwa is commonly his mother and the heavenly Haemosu his father, joining dynastic history to traditions of extraordinary birth.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Sunlight reaches Yuhwa and she lays an egg, which survives abandonment through animal protection and produces Jumong. A gifted archer, he flees jealous princes in Buyeo. At a river he calls upon heavenly and river ancestry; fish and turtles form a bridge. He escapes and founds Goguryeo, while later recognition stories connect a searching son and matching sword fragments with succession.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A bow, arrows, miraculous egg, sunlight, and bridge of fish and turtles identify Jumong’s narrative. They express exceptional skill and the assistance of sacred ancestry. Modern screen adaptations add distinctive costumes, romances, and combat equipment that should not be mistaken for a fixed ancient iconography.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Gwanggaeto Stele, Samguk Sagi, and Lay of King Dongmyeong preserve different stages of the tradition. Their details and political purposes require separate attention. Jumong continues to feature in modern cultural storytelling, but historical evidence, literary elaboration, and television invention should remain distinguishable when interpreting the founder.

name: 解慕漱
title: 联系天界降临与朱蒙谱系的神圣祖先

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 解慕漱是朝鲜半岛扶余与高句丽相关叙事中的天界人物，常被说成天帝之子、朱蒙之父。他与扶余诸王的关系在不同记载中并不一致，不能把散见的王名与谱系全部拼成一份没有矛盾的历史年表。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在《东明王篇》等保存的叙事中，解慕漱乘五龙车下降，白日处理人间事务，夜晚返回天上。他遇见河伯之女柳花，与她结合后，河伯以变化之术试验其天界身份，解慕漱亦变形相对。婚姻与离别的细节因文本而异，柳花后来又受日光照临，生下的朱蒙承接天与水的双重祖源。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 五龙车、华冠、佩剑与天上往返的形象是常见叙事标记，水域与柳花提示其婚姻关系。他并非朱蒙的另一名字，也不能与檀君故事中的桓雄直接视为同一人物。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 解慕漱的故事服务于王族神圣谱系，也保存天界与河流祖先结合的叙事结构。研究常比较碑铭、史书与诗篇的差异；现代影视会扩写他的战争和情感生活，这些新增内容不宜反推为古代共同传统。

en.name: Haemosu
en.title: Heavenly ancestor in the genealogy of Jumong

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Haemosu is a heavenly figure in traditions concerning Buyeo and Goguryeo, commonly called a son of the heavenly emperor and father of Jumong. Accounts disagree about his relationships with Buyeo rulers. Their names and genealogies should not be forced into a seamless historical chronology that conceals the differences between sources.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In traditions preserved by the Lay of King Dongmyeong, Haemosu descends in a carriage drawn by five dragons and returns to heaven at night. He meets Yuhwa, daughter of the river lord, whose father tests his identity through transformations. Marriage and separation vary between accounts. Yuhwa subsequently conceives through sunlight, giving Jumong ancestry associated with both heaven and water.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The dragon carriage, splendid headgear, sword, and journeys between heaven and earth provide identifying motifs. Rivers and Yuhwa indicate his marital connection. Haemosu is neither another name for Jumong nor automatically identical with Hwanung, the heavenly descendant belonging to the separate Dangun foundation tradition.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Haemosu legitimizes royal ancestry through the meeting of heavenly and river lineages. Comparing inscriptions, histories, and literary poems reveals changes in how that ancestry was narrated. Modern television expands his military and romantic adventures, but these additions cannot simply be projected backward as universally shared ancient tradition.

name: 钵里公主
title: 远赴异界取回生命之水的巫祖

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 钵里公主又有巴里公主、钵里德纪等译名，是韩国巫俗口传叙事中的弃女与救亲者，常被奉为引导亡魂的巫祖。她的身世和结局随地区、表演者与仪式变化，没有一份可以覆盖全部地方传统的固定传记。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 国王盼望男嗣，却接连得女，最小的钵里因此遭到遗弃，由他人抚养。父亲或双亲病危后，其他女儿不愿远行，她却前往遥远异界寻找救命的水与花。途中她承担劳役、经历婚姻和生育等考验，终于带回药物，使亲人复生。部分版本随后让她获得引魂的神职，把受弃者转为跨越生死的帮助者。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 生命之水、复生之花、远行衣装与跨越生死边界的道路构成核心意象。她不是等待搭救的公主，辨识重点在亲自远行和引魂职责；具体花名与器物随版本改变。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 钵里叙事常在与亡者有关的巫俗仪式中演唱，故事与祭仪、音乐和表演彼此关联。它既讨论孝亲，也呈现重男轻女与被遗弃者的处境；现代文学重述丰富其形象，但不应取代活态仪式的多样性。

en.name: Princess Bari
en.title: Abandoned daughter who brings back life and guides souls

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Princess Bari, also known through names rendered Baridegi, is an abandoned daughter and rescuer in Korean shamanic oral traditions. She often becomes an ancestral figure who guides the dead. Regional performances differ in genealogy, trials, and ending, so no single biography represents every community or ritual setting.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: A king seeking a son abandons his youngest daughter. Raised elsewhere, Bari later learns that her father or both parents are dying. Unlike her sisters, she undertakes a journey to obtain restorative water and flowers. Trials may include labor, marriage, and childbirth. Returning with the remedy, she restores her family and, in some versions, receives responsibility for guiding souls.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Life restoring water, reviving flowers, traveling clothes, and passages across the boundary of death are central motifs. Bari acts as a traveler and guide rather than a princess awaiting rescue. Specific flowers, vessels, companions, and costumes vary with regional versions and the performance tradition involved.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Bari narratives are performed in shamanic rites associated with the dead, where storytelling, music, and ritual action belong together. They explore filial care alongside abandonment and preference for sons. Contemporary literary adaptations offer further readings but should not replace attention to the diversity of living ceremonial traditions.

name: 耶稣
title: 基督教信仰核心中的基督与救主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 耶稣是公元一世纪犹太背景中的传道者，也是基督教信仰的核心。主流基督教承认他为道成肉身的圣子、真正的神与真正的人，而非众神之一。有关其生平的主要经典是四部福音书，历史研究与信仰表述应加区分。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 福音书记述耶稣由玛利亚所生，受约翰施洗后宣讲上帝的国，以比喻教导、医治病人并呼召门徒。他在耶路撒冷与门徒共进最后晚餐，随后被捕，在罗马总督彼拉多治下遭钉十字架。基督徒相信他第三日复活，并向门徒显现；这一信仰构成复活节、传教与救赎理解的中心。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 十字架、善牧、鱼形记号与基督圣像是常见线索，受难像与空十字架的使用因传统而异。光环和衣袍属于宗教艺术语言，不能当作其历史容貌或族群外貌的直接证据。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 基督教是持续实践的一神宗教，礼拜、圣餐与教会年历围绕基督展开，各宗派解释和仪式不尽相同。耶稣也见于其他宗教的不同理解，介绍时应说明立场，不能把基督徒的信仰简单归为虚构故事。

en.name: Jesus
en.title: Christ and savior at the center of Christian faith

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Jesus was a Jewish teacher in the first century and is the central figure of Christianity. Mainstream Christian doctrine confesses him as the incarnate Son, truly divine and truly human, not one god among many. The four canonical Gospels are principal sources, while historical inquiry and confessional statements require distinct framing.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Gospels recount his birth to Mary, baptism by John, proclamation of God’s kingdom, healings, parables, and calling of disciples. After a final meal in Jerusalem, he is arrested and crucified under the Roman governor Pontius Pilate. Christians believe that he rose on the third day and appeared to followers, making resurrection central to worship and understandings of salvation.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The cross, Good Shepherd, fish sign, and images of Christ are recognizable Christian symbols. Traditions differ in their use of crucifixes, empty crosses, and sacred pictures. Halos, clothing, and artistic facial types communicate religious meanings rather than supplying direct evidence of Jesus’ historical physical appearance.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Christianity is a living monotheistic religion whose worship, Eucharistic practices, and calendar center on Christ. Churches differ in theology and ritual expression. Other religions understand Jesus differently, so presentations should identify their standpoint and avoid treating Christian faith either as interchangeable folklore or as an unquestioned historical conclusion.

name: 玛利亚
title: 耶稣之母与基督教传统中的信德典范

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 玛利亚是新约中的犹太女性、耶稣的母亲，在许多基督教传统中尊称圣母。天主教和东正教尤其重视对她的敬礼，但不把她当作独立女神；有关其称号、代祷及生平教义，各教会之间存在重要差异。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《路加福音》记加百列向玛利亚报喜，她接受生育耶稣的使命，随后探望伊利莎白，并唱出赞颂上帝的尊主颂。福音书还叙述耶稣诞生、她在圣殿寻回少年耶稣，以及迦拿婚宴上的请求。《约翰福音》将她置于十字架旁，《使徒行传》则记她与门徒一同祈祷，呈现母亲与信徒的双重身份。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 怀抱圣婴、蓝色或红色衣袍、百合与星冠是常见艺术线索，但地区和教派差异很大。圣母图像表达基督降生及信德，不意味着她在一神信仰之外拥有另一个神格。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 圣母节日、圣像与朝圣在天主教和东正教中十分重要，新教各群体的态度则有差异。圣母无染原罪与耶稣由童贞女所生并非同一教义；相关称号须放回具体教会传统，避免混用或误称为女神崇拜。

en.name: Mary
en.title: Mother of Jesus and exemplar of Christian faith

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Mary is the Jewish mother of Jesus in the New Testament, honored as the Virgin Mary in many churches. Catholic and Orthodox traditions give particular importance to her veneration without treating her as an independent goddess. Christian communities differ significantly over Marian titles, intercession, and doctrines concerning her life.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Luke recounts Gabriel’s announcement, Mary’s acceptance, her visit to Elizabeth, and her song praising God. Gospel narratives also place her at Jesus’ birth, his childhood visit to the temple, and the wedding at Cana. John depicts her beside the cross, while Acts includes her praying with the disciples, portraying her as both mother and faithful participant.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The mother holding the infant Jesus, blue or red robes, lilies, and a crown of stars are familiar artistic motifs. Their arrangement varies across regions and churches. Marian images express beliefs about Christ’s birth and faithful response, not the existence of another deity outside Christian monotheism.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Marian feasts, icons, and pilgrimage are important in Catholic and Orthodox life, while Protestant approaches vary. The Immaculate Conception concerns Mary and is not the same doctrine as the virgin birth of Jesus. Titles and practices require their specific ecclesial contexts rather than a generalized label of goddess worship.

name: 米迦勒
title: 守护并争战的天使长

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 米迦勒是犹太教与基督教经典中的天使人物，其名字常解释为谁能像上帝。他在《但以理书》中与以色列的守护有关，在《犹大书》中称为天使长；基督教敬礼中的尊崇不意味着把他视为与上帝并列的神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《但以理书》描写米迦勒帮助天上使者，并在危难时期为百姓站立。《犹大书》提到他与魔鬼争论摩西的遗体，却不擅自作毁谤判断，而求主责备对方。《启示录》则记米迦勒与其天使和龙交战，龙及其使者被摔下天。这些段落各有体裁与语境，不应拼接成一部详尽的天使战争编年史。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 甲胄、长剑或长矛、脚下的龙是主要标志，天平也见于后世审判题材。翅膀属于天使艺术的惯例，不是经典统一描述；米迦勒代表受命的守护者，而非独立的战争神。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 米迦勒节庆、圣堂奉献与守护祈祷见于多种教会传统，有些新教群体不实践天使敬礼。其形象也与犹太教和伊斯兰教传统相关，但各自经典与解释不同，跨宗教比较必须保留这些边界与差异。

en.name: Michael
en.title: Archangel associated with protection and heavenly struggle

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Michael is an angelic figure in Jewish and Christian scriptures, his name commonly understood as a question about who is like God. Daniel associates him with the protection of Israel, while Jude calls him an archangel. Christian honor directed toward him does not make him a deity alongside God.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Daniel, Michael assists a heavenly messenger and stands for the people during crisis. Jude describes a dispute with the devil over Moses’ body, in which Michael appeals to the Lord’s rebuke. Revelation depicts Michael and his angels fighting the dragon and casting it down. These distinct passages should not become a falsely comprehensive chronology of heavenly warfare.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Armor, a sword or spear, and a dragon beneath his feet commonly identify Michael. Scales also appear in later judgment imagery. Wings belong to artistic conventions rather than a uniform scriptural portrait. His authority is understood as commissioned protection and service, not independent divine control over warfare.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Feasts, dedicated churches, and protective prayers honor Michael in several Christian traditions, though some Protestant communities reject angelic veneration. Related figures appear in Jewish and Islamic traditions with their own textual histories. Comparison should preserve these differences instead of blending every reference into a single universal angelic biography.

name: 加百列
title: 解释异象并传达报喜信息的天使

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 加百列是犹太教与基督教经典中的天使，在《但以理书》中解释异象，在《路加福音》中传达降生消息。许多教会传统称他为天使长，但新约相关段落没有直接使用这一称号；他始终是上帝的使者而非神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《但以理书》中，加百列奉命帮助但以理理解异象与时序。《路加福音》记他向祭司撒迦利亚预告施洗约翰出生，随后到拿撒勒向玛利亚宣告她将生子，并为孩子起名耶稣。玛利亚询问后，他说明圣灵临到，并以伊利莎白的怀孕作为记号；报喜场景因此把神圣信息与人的回应连接起来。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 百合、卷轴、报喜手势与面对玛利亚的构图是主要辨识线索，有时也持杖。把加百列固定画为吹号者是部分后世传统，并非所有末日号角经文都明确写出他的名字。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 报喜节与大量圣乐、绘画延续加百列的文化影响。伊斯兰教中的吉卜力勒也有重要启示职分，但不能把两种经典的事件直接互换；不同教会对天使的敬礼程度及艺术表现，也须分别说明。

en.name: Gabriel
en.title: Angelic interpreter and messenger of the Annunciation

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Gabriel is an angel in Jewish and Christian scripture, interpreting visions in Daniel and announcing births in Luke. Many church traditions call Gabriel an archangel, although the relevant New Testament passages do not explicitly use that title. Gabriel acts as God’s messenger, never as an independent deity or rival divine power.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Daniel, Gabriel explains visions and their significance. Luke describes Gabriel announcing John the Baptist’s birth to Zechariah, then visiting Mary in Nazareth to announce that she will bear Jesus. Answering her question, Gabriel speaks of the Holy Spirit and points to Elizabeth’s pregnancy, linking the divine announcement with an invitation to human trust and response.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Lilies, scrolls, a raised greeting hand, and a composition facing Mary commonly identify Gabriel in Annunciation art. A staff may also appear. The familiar association with a final trumpet belongs to particular later traditions; not every scriptural trumpet passage explicitly names Gabriel as its player.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Annunciation feast, sacred music, and painting sustain Gabriel’s prominence in Christian culture. Jibril has a major revelatory role in Islam, but events from the two scriptural traditions are not interchangeable. Churches also differ in angelic veneration and visual representation, requiring attention to particular communities and practices.

name: 彼得
title: 在软弱与更新中作见证的使徒

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 彼得原名西门，是来自加利利的犹太渔夫，成为耶稣十二使徒之一，兄弟安得烈也在门徒之列。彼得的名字与磐石相关，新约同时保留其勇敢表白和软弱失误；他是受尊敬的使徒与圣徒，并非神灵。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 福音书描写彼得回应呼召，承认耶稣为基督，却也在受难前夜三次否认认识他。复活后的耶稣在《约翰福音》中三次询问他的爱，并托付牧养羊群。《使徒行传》记彼得在五旬节公开宣讲，又因异象前往外邦人哥尼流家，成为初期教会讨论接纳外邦信徒的重要人物。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 钥匙、渔网、公鸡与卷曲短发的长者形象常用于辨识，分别联系托付、职业和否认经历。倒置十字架来自后世殉道传统，不是新约对其死亡方式的明确记述。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 天主教将彼得视为首任教宗，并以其职分解释教宗传承；东正教与新教对这一权柄有不同理解。罗马圣彼得大殿和使徒节庆延续其影响，相关纪念应区分新约叙事、后世传统与宗派立场。

en.name: Peter
en.title: Apostolic witness shaped by failure and renewed calling

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Peter, originally Simon, was a Jewish fisherman from Galilee and one of Jesus’ twelve apostles; Andrew was his brother. His name evokes a rock. New Testament accounts preserve both his bold confession and his failures, presenting an honored apostolic witness rather than a divine being or independent object of worship.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Peter answers Jesus’ call and confesses him as Messiah, but denies knowing him three times before the crucifixion. In John, the risen Jesus asks three times about Peter’s love and entrusts him with pastoral care. Acts depicts his Pentecost preaching and visit to Cornelius, episodes important to the early church’s understanding of receiving Gentile believers.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Keys, fishing nets, a rooster, and the familiar elderly figure with short curled hair identify Peter in art. They recall authority, occupation, and denial. An inverted cross belongs to later accounts of his martyrdom, not an explicit New Testament description of the manner of his death.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Catholicism identifies Peter as the first pope and relates his office to papal succession. Orthodox and Protestant Christians interpret the scope of that authority differently. Saint Peter’s Basilica and apostolic feasts preserve his memory, while scriptural narratives, later martyrdom traditions, and denominational claims should be clearly distinguished.

name: 保罗
title: 向外邦人传道并书写教会书信的使徒

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 保罗是来自大数的犹太人，也是早期基督教的重要传道者和书信作者，不属于耶稣生前的十二使徒。他亦名扫罗，两种名字见于同一传统，不宜把使用保罗一名简单说成改宗后的正式更名；他是使徒而非神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 保罗曾迫害耶稣的追随者，后来因与复活基督相遇而转向传道。《使徒行传》以大马士革途中强光和声音描述此事，他的书信则强调启示与蒙召。他在地中海东部建立和联系群体，经历争论、监禁与海难，并讨论外邦信徒是否须受割礼；其书信由具体处境展开信仰、恩典与群体生活的思考。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 书卷、书信、剑与高额长须是常见艺术标志。剑多联系后世关于其被斩首的殉道传统，也可象征属灵言语，不意味着把保罗塑造成以武力传教的战士。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 保罗书信深刻影响基督教神学与礼拜，但学界对部分署名书信的作者问题有讨论。各教会对信心、行为及律法的解释不一，阅读时需关注一世纪犹太背景，避免把他简化为反对犹太教的符号。

en.name: Paul
en.title: Apostle to the Gentiles and writer of church letters

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Paul was a Jew from Tarsus who became a major early Christian missionary and letter writer, though not one of Jesus’ original twelve apostles. He also bore the name Saul. The two names should not automatically be explained as a formal renaming at conversion. He is an apostle, not a deity.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After persecuting Jesus’ followers, Paul understood an encounter with the risen Christ as a calling. Acts describes light and a voice near Damascus; his letters emphasize revelation. He traveled, formed communities, endured imprisonment and shipwreck, and debated Gentile circumcision. His letters address particular situations while developing influential reflections on faith, grace, and communal life.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Books, letters, a sword, and a high forehead with a long beard commonly identify Paul. The sword recalls later traditions of execution by beheading and can also suggest spiritual speech. It should not imply that Paul is being celebrated as a warrior spreading Christianity through armed conquest.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Pauline letters profoundly shape Christian theology and worship, although scholars debate the authorship of some letters attributed to him. Churches interpret faith, works, and law differently. Reading within the Jewish contexts of the first century helps prevent simplistic portrayals of Paul as merely a symbol of opposition to Judaism.

name: 摩西
title: 出埃及叙事中的先知与领受律法者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 摩西是犹太教《妥拉》的核心人物，也是基督教旧约中受到尊重的先知与领袖。经典叙他出身以色列人家庭，在埃及宫廷环境中长大；将他收录在基督教分类只是索引安排，不表示其故事专属于基督教，更不能称其为神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《出埃及记》叙婴儿摩西被放入河边篮中，由法老女儿收养。他成年后逃往米甸，在燃烧而不焚毁的荆棘前蒙召，返回埃及要求释放以色列人。灾祸与逾越节之后，他带领百姓过海、进入旷野，并在西奈山领受律法和盟约。后续经典也记百姓反复抱怨，以及摩西在进入应许之地前去世。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 法杖、两块法版、荆棘火焰与分开的海水是主要线索。部分西方艺术中的角源于古代译文与解释传统，另有光芒形象；这些不是将摩西描绘成恶魔或另一位神。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 逾越节、妥拉诵读与犹太释经使摩西持续居于犹太生活核心，基督教又有自身的预表和礼仪解释。出埃及叙事的历史背景存在学术讨论；信仰意义、考古证据和跨宗教接受史应分别介绍。

en.name: Moses
en.title: Prophet and lawgiver in the Exodus and covenant narratives

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Moses is central to the Jewish Torah and is honored as a prophet and leader in the Christian Old Testament. Scripture presents him as an Israelite raised within an Egyptian royal environment. Placement in a Christian category is only an indexing choice: his narratives are not exclusively Christian, and he is not divine.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Exodus recounts Moses’ rescue from a basket by Pharaoh’s daughter, flight to Midian, and calling at a bush that burns without being consumed. Returning to Egypt, he demands Israel’s release. Plagues and Passover precede the crossing of the sea, wilderness journeys, and the Sinai covenant. Later books describe resistance among the people and his death before entry into the promised land.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A staff, two tablets, the burning bush, and divided waters identify Moses. Horns in some Western artworks reflect an ancient translation and interpretive history, while other images show rays of light. Neither convention makes Moses a demon or an additional god within Jewish or Christian belief.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Passover, Torah reading, and Jewish interpretation keep Moses central within living Judaism. Christianity develops additional liturgical and typological readings without erasing those Jewish contexts. The historical background of Exodus remains debated, making it important to distinguish religious meaning, archaeological evidence, and the separate histories of reception across communities.

name: 亚伯拉罕
title: 蒙召离乡并承受盟约应许的族长

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 亚伯拉罕是犹太教《创世记》中的族长，也是基督教旧约与伊斯兰教共同尊重的人物。他原名亚伯兰，在盟约叙事中获新名，与撒拉、夏甲及后代的关系构成家族故事；他是人间祖先与信仰典范，并非神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《创世记》叙亚伯拉罕回应上帝呼召，离开故土前往迦南，并领受土地与众多后裔的应许。他与夏甲生以实玛利，撒拉晚年生以撒；家庭冲突也伴随应许展开。献以撒故事中，他被要求献子，却在最后一刻受到阻止，以公羊代替。关于待客与为所多玛代求的段落，也呈现信赖和伦理交织的张力。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 帐篷、星空、旅杖、公羊与接待三位访客的场景较常见。献子图像表现经典中的艰难考验，而不是认可现实伤害儿童；访客的身份解释因宗教传统而不同。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 犹太教从盟约与祖先记忆理解亚伯拉罕，基督教常强调他的信心，伊斯兰教则称其为易卜拉欣。各传统在儿子、圣地与祭献细节上有自身叙述，所谓亚伯拉罕诸教并不意味着教义或故事完全一致。

en.name: Abraham
en.title: Patriarch called to journey and receive covenant promises

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Abraham is a patriarch in the Jewish book of Genesis, also honored in Christianity and Islam. Originally Abram, he receives a new name within the covenant narrative. Relationships with Sarah, Hagar, and their descendants shape his story. He remains a human ancestor and exemplar of faith rather than a deity.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Genesis describes Abraham leaving his homeland for Canaan in response to God’s call and receiving promises of land and descendants. Hagar bears Ishmael, and Sarah later bears Isaac amid family tensions. Asked to offer Isaac, Abraham is stopped and substitutes a ram. Narratives of hospitality and intercession for Sodom further explore the tensions between trust, promise, and moral responsibility.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Tents, stars, a traveler’s staff, a ram, and the welcome of three visitors commonly identify Abraham. Images of the binding of Isaac depict a difficult scriptural test, not approval of harming children. Interpretations of the visitors differ across religious communities and within their artistic traditions.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Judaism emphasizes covenant and ancestral memory, Christianity often highlights Abraham’s faith, and Islam honors him as Ibrahim. Each preserves distinctive interpretations of descendants, sacred places, and sacrifice. The expression Abrahamic religions identifies relationships among traditions without implying that their teachings, ritual practices, or narrative details are all identical.

name: 雷公
title: 雷霆之神与天界执法者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 雷公是中国传统信仰中司掌雷霆的神灵，名称与形象历代多有变化。《论衡》记述雷公击鼓的图像，道教又把雷霆纳入神圣官署体系；民间所称雷公并不总与某一位道教雷部尊神完全相同。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 有关雷公的故事常围绕以雷声警戒世人、惩处不义展开，但各地对于受罚者及其缘由的解释并不一致。雷公与电母配合行事的说法在后世广为流传，电光照见目标，雷霆随后降下。这类故事表达民间对天道公正的期待，不宜当作所有道教经典共有的一套定论。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 常见图像以鸟喙、羽翼及鼓表现雷公，手持槌凿或环列雷鼓；各时代造像并不统一。鼓声对应雷鸣，羽翼表现迅疾，凿槌则把难以捉摸的天威化为可见动作。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 雷公见于庙宇、道教仪式、戏曲与口头故事。雷雨既关联农事所需的降水，也带来灾害风险，敬畏与祈求因而并存。理解这些传统，应区分地方祭祀、道教雷法与文学想象。

en.name: Leigong
en.title: Thunder Deity and Heavenly Enforcer

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Leigong is a Chinese deity associated with thunder. His names and appearances changed over time. Wang Chong's Lunheng describes images of a thunder deity beating drums. Daoist thunder administrations developed additional hierarchies, so popular Leigong should not automatically be identified with every major thunder divinity.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
