sections.text: Stories frequently portray Leigong warning people or punishing wrongdoing, but the offenses and circumstances vary locally. Later accounts often pair him with Dianmu, whose lightning reveals a target before thunder strikes. These narratives express hopes for heavenly justice rather than a universally fixed Daoist doctrine.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Familiar representations include a birdlike beak, wings, drums, and implements resembling a hammer and chisel. Historical images differ considerably. Drums make thunder audible in human terms, wings suggest speed, and striking tools translate an invisible atmospheric force into recognizable bodily action.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Leigong appears in temples, Daoist ritual, theater, and oral storytelling. Thunderstorms can bring agricultural rain as well as destruction, encouraging both petition and apprehension. Local worship, specialized Daoist thunder rites, and literary inventions overlap but should remain analytically distinct.

name: 祝融
title: 火神与古代火正传统

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 祝融既是火神名号，也与古代掌火之官的传统相连。《左传》与《史记》保存不同的祖先谱系和任官说法，涉及黎、重黎及吴回等名字。因此，祝融不能简单还原为生平一致的单一历史人物。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《史记·楚世家》记载，重黎任帝喾的火正，因有功而被命为祝融；他未能尽诛作乱的共工氏，后来被杀，其弟吴回继任火正，也称祝融。这一叙事把神名、官职和楚人祖先联系起来，与后世把祝融和共工写成水火交战双方的故事并不完全相同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 火焰与南方是祝融的重要关联。《山海经·海外南经》写他兽身人面、乘两龙，和后世武将式火神造像有所不同。辨识时须结合文本或题名，不能只凭红衣判断。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 祝融进入楚地祖先叙事、地方火神祭祀及后世文学。不同文献中的官名、神格和族群谱系可能互相交织，却不宜强行统一。今天借用祝融命名的科技项目，则属于传统意象的现代转用。

en.name: Zhurong
en.title: Fire Deity and Ancient Fire Official

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Zhurong designates a fire deity and is also associated with an ancient office supervising fire. The Zuozhuan and Shiji preserve differing genealogical and administrative accounts involving Li, Chongli, and Wuhui. These materials do not establish one consistent biography of a single historical individual.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Shiji account of Chu ancestry, Chongli serves Emperor Ku as fire official and receives the designation Zhurong. After failing to eliminate Gonggong's rebels, he is executed; his brother Wuhui succeeds him. Later dramatic battles between personified fire and water represent different narrative developments.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Fire and the southern direction are central associations. The Shanhaijing describes the southern Zhurong with an animal body, human face, and two dragons. This differs from later martial images, reminding viewers that red clothing alone cannot securely identify a particular deity.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Zhurong appears in Chu ancestral traditions, local fire worship, and later literature. Divine identity, official title, and lineage can intersect without becoming identical across sources. Modern technological names reuse this inherited imagery in settings quite different from ancient ritual and genealogy.

name: 天宇受卖
title: 岩户神话中的舞蹈与仪礼之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 天宇受卖是《古事记》和《日本书纪》所载的神祇，汉字表记与具体情节随文献而异。她以天岩户前的表演闻名，也参与迎接猿田彦的故事；其形象与猿女氏承担的宫廷仪礼职能紧密相连。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 天照大神隐入岩户后，世界失去光明。《古事记》叙述天宇受卖踏响倒置的桶，作出引众神大笑的表演，促使天照探问并向外窥看；众神再以镜子及其他手段合力引她出洞。天孙降临时，天宇受卖又奉命询问挡在路口的猿田彦，确认其前来引路的意图。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 岩户叙事中的桶、榊枝与身体表演是重要线索。后世常把她同阿龟面具联系起来，但面具的圆脸笑容并非早期文本给出的固定相貌，也不能涵盖所有祭祀形象。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 她受到神社祭祀，并在神乐及表演艺术的起源叙事中占有要位。不同地区的舞目与解释各有传承，不能把所有神乐都视为岩户表演的直接复原，也不宜仅以娱乐角色理解其神圣身份。

en.name: Ame-no-Uzume
en.title: Deity of Performance and the Heavenly Cave

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Ame-no-Uzume appears in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, whose spellings and narrative details differ. Famous for performing before Amaterasu's cave, she also encounters Sarutahiko. Her stories connect divine performance with the ritual responsibilities claimed by the Sarume lineage at the Japanese court.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: When Amaterasu withdraws into a cave, Uzume stamps on an overturned vessel and performs provocatively, making the assembled deities laugh. Their reaction draws Amaterasu's attention; a mirror and coordinated divine actions complete her emergence. In the heavenly descent narrative, Uzume questions Sarutahiko about his intentions.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The overturned vessel, sacred branches, and emphatic bodily performance are useful narrative identifiers. Later associations with the smiling Okame mask are influential but should not be mistaken for a fixed appearance prescribed by early texts or for the full range of her sacred representations.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Uzume is worshipped at shrines and figures prominently in accounts connecting sacred performance with kagura and other arts. Regional repertoires preserve different interpretations. Not every kagura dance directly reconstructs the cave episode, and describing her merely as an entertainer overlooks living religious significance.

name: 猿田彦
title: 天孙降临时的引路之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 猿田彦见于《古事记》和《日本书纪》的天孙降临叙事，是与地上道路相连的神祇。天宇受卖与他相遇的记载，也解释猿女氏的名号和仪礼传统；各书对于外貌与对话的铺陈并不完全一致。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 琼琼杵尊将从天界降临时，一位光耀的神出现在天之八衢。众神派天宇受卖前去询问，他自称猿田彦，说明自己是来迎接并引导天孙的。《古事记》还写天宇受卖送他返回伊势的阿邪诃。故事重心是相遇、辨明身份和引路，而不是由两神争夺统治权。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 高鼻、明亮的眼睛和威严面貌是常见辨识线索，部分依据《日本书纪》的描写。祭礼中可见执杖引路者，但高鼻并不意味着他就是天狗，两者传统不能混同。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊势的猿田彦神社等处奉祀此神，人们常祈求出行顺利或人生方向。他也与道祖神信仰发生联系，但各地合祀与解释不同，不能把所有道路守护神都直接等同为猿田彦。

en.name: Sarutahiko
en.title: Divine Guide of the Heavenly Descent

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Sarutahiko appears in the heavenly descent narratives of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki as a deity connected with the earthly realm and its routes. His encounter with Ame-no-Uzume also explains Sarume lineage traditions. Descriptions of his appearance and conversation vary between these sources.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: As Ninigi prepares to descend, a radiant deity appears at the heavenly crossroads. Uzume questions him, and he identifies himself as Sarutahiko, offering guidance to the arriving heavenly descendant. The Kojiki subsequently has Uzume escort him to Azaka in Ise, emphasizing encounter and guidance rather than conquest.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: A prominent nose, shining eyes, and an imposing face distinguish many representations, drawing partly on the Nihon Shoki. Festival guides may carry a staff. Although a long nose can resemble later tengu imagery, resemblance does not make Sarutahiko and tengu the same religious figure.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Shrines including Sarutahiko Jinja in Ise honor him, and worshippers seek guidance for journeys or life decisions. Associations with roadside guardian traditions developed unevenly. Local identifications and shared worship require context; not every dosojin or protective road deity should be renamed Sarutahiko.

name: 吉祥天女
title: 拉克希米：吉祥、福祉与繁荣女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 吉祥天女拉克希米是印度教重要女神，与吉祥、丰饶和福祉相连，也常称室利。她在毗湿奴信仰中具有核心地位，但并非仅是附属角色；不同宗派对于她与毗湿奴的关系及其救度作用有不同理解。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 搅乳海是往世书传统中最著名的故事之一：众神与阿修罗共同搅动乳海，拉克希米从海中显现，随后与毗湿奴相联。各部文本对出场次序及细节的叙述不尽相同。在毗湿奴化身叙事中，悉多和鲁克米尼等又常被视为她的显现，不能把每一种地区解释都当成共同定本。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 莲花、双象灌水和赐福手势是常见标志，金钱意象表现丰盛，却不能概括她的全部神格。臂数与持物随造像传统变化，猫头鹰则在部分地区具有特别关联。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 印度及海外印度教社群在家庭与寺庙中敬奉她，排灯节的吉祥天女祭尤为知名，但节日解释因地区而异。孟加拉等地另有重要祭期；这些实践不能被简化成单纯求财的民俗。

en.name: Lakshmi
en.title: Goddess of Auspiciousness, Wellbeing, and Prosperity

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Lakshmi, also called Shri, is a major Hindu goddess associated with auspiciousness, abundance, and wellbeing. She occupies a central place in traditions devoted to Vishnu without being merely an accessory. Different theological communities explain her divine status and role in liberation in distinctive ways.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In famous Puranic accounts, gods and asuras churn the ocean of milk, and Lakshmi emerges before becoming associated with Vishnu. Details and sequence vary among texts. Sita and Rukmini are often understood as her manifestations within Vishnu's incarnation narratives, with further regional and theological variations.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Lotuses, elephants pouring water, and gestures of blessing frequently identify Lakshmi. Coins signify abundance but do not exhaust her religious meaning. The number of arms and accompanying objects varies, while an owl has a particularly important association in some regional traditions.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Hindu households and temples across India and the diaspora honor Lakshmi. Her worship during Diwali is especially prominent, although festival meanings differ regionally. Bengal and other areas maintain additional major observances. These living practices encompass wellbeing and auspicious order, not simply the pursuit of money.

name: 辩才天女
title: 萨拉斯瓦蒂：河流、言语与学艺女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 萨拉斯瓦蒂在《梨俱吠陀》中兼具河流与神圣女神的面向，后来成为印度教知识、言语、音乐及学艺的重要女神。她常与梵天相联，但关系的表述因文本而异；此处讨论印度语境，不等同日本弁才天。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 吠陀赞歌赞颂萨拉斯瓦蒂的河流力量、滋养作用与神圣助佑，不能把它们都改写成后世女神的完整传记。较晚传统把她与创造、言语和梵天联系起来，有时称为梵天的配偶。不同文本对关系与起源各有叙述，并不存在一套为全部印度教社群共同接受的婚姻故事。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 白衣、维纳琴、书卷和念珠常见于她的图像，天鹅或孔雀也可伴随出现。白色常关联纯净与知识；持物和坐骑随地区变化，不宜凭某件乐器便断定所有女神身份。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 春季的婆娑多五日节常见学生、教师和艺术工作者礼敬女神，部分地区另在九夜节供奉书籍与乐器。她的信仰跨越南亚多种传统，传播到佛教及日本后的变化应另作说明。

en.name: Saraswati
en.title: Goddess of Rivers, Speech, Learning, and Music

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Saraswati appears in the Rigveda as both a river and a divine presence. Later Hindu traditions especially associate her with knowledge, speech, music, and learning. Connections with Brahma vary across texts. This account concerns Indian religious contexts rather than treating her as identical with Japanese Benzaiten.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Vedic hymns praise Saraswati's river power, nourishment, and divine assistance rather than presenting one continuous later biography. Subsequent traditions connect her with creation, speech, and Brahma, sometimes as his consort. Accounts of origins and relationships differ and should not be combined into a universally accepted marriage narrative.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: White clothing, a vina, books, and prayer beads commonly accompany Saraswati, with a swan or peacock in different representations. White often suggests purity and knowledge. Objects and mounts vary regionally, so a musical instrument alone cannot securely identify every image of a goddess.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Students, teachers, and artists often honor Saraswati during Vasant Panchami. Some regions also dedicate books and instruments during Navaratri observances. Her worship crosses several South Asian traditions. Transformations through Buddhist transmission and Japanese Benzaiten worship require separate discussion rather than collapsing distinct communities into one.

name: 柳花
title: 高句丽建国叙事中的朱蒙之母

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 柳花是高句丽始祖朱蒙的母亲，在《三国史记》及其他传承中被称为河伯之女。她的来历将水域神圣性与王室祖源联系起来；现存史书成书较晚，所保存的建国神话不宜直接等同于同时代实录。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《三国史记》记柳花自述与解慕漱相遇，后被父亲斥逐，由金蛙收留。日光追随她的身体照耀，她因而怀孕并生下一卵。金蛙试图弃卵，禽兽却不肯伤害，卵最终交还柳花，朱蒙从中出生。这套叙事同时包含天界、水域与卵生母题，其他文献对相遇经过另有铺陈。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 河水、日光和巨卵构成柳花故事的关键线索，强调朱蒙母系的神圣来源。她没有跨时代通行的固定服饰或持物，现代画像中的王冠与衣装不能充作古代统一标准。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 柳花事迹见于史书、相关文学与现代影视重述，并参与高句丽王室祖源的解释。解读时应区分较晚文字记录、可能更早的口传素材与当代创作，不把母神称谓当作各地一致的祭祀事实。

en.name: Yuhwa
en.title: Mother of Jumong in Goguryeo Foundation Traditions

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Yuhwa is the mother of Jumong, Goguryeo's founding ruler, and is described as a daughter of the river deity Habaek. Her ancestry links royal origins with sacred waters. Surviving historical compilations are later sources, not contemporary transcripts of the events they narrate.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Samguk Sagi, Yuhwa recounts meeting Haemosu and being expelled by her father before Geumwa shelters her. Pursuing sunlight brings pregnancy, and she lays an egg. Animals refuse to harm the abandoned egg; returned to Yuhwa, it eventually produces Jumong. Other sources elaborate the encounter differently.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: River water, sunlight, and the extraordinary egg identify Yuhwa's narrative and establish sacred maternal ancestry for Jumong. No single costume or attribute identifies her consistently across all periods. Crowns and garments in modern illustrations should not be presented as standardized ancient iconography.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Historical compilations, later literature, and contemporary screen adaptations transmit Yuhwa's story within interpretations of Goguryeo origins. Written records, potentially earlier oral materials, and modern inventions need distinguishing. Calling her a mother goddess does not by itself demonstrate uniform worship across different communities and periods.

name: 金蛙
title: 东扶余之王与朱蒙故事中的收留者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 金蛙是朱蒙建国叙事中的东扶余国王。《三国史记》说解夫娄在石下发现形似金色蛙儿的孩子，收为嗣子并取名金蛙。此名关联奇异发现的故事，不意味着所有记载都把他视为同一位蛙神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 金蛙继位后遇见并收留柳花，又面对她感日生卵的异事。他曾把卵交给动物、弃于野外，也试图破卵，却未能成功，最后归还柳花。朱蒙长大后善射，引起金蛙诸子的猜忌，最终离开扶余。金蛙在故事中既是庇护者，也是不能完全消除宫廷威胁的君主。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 金色蛙儿与石下发现的场景最能提示金蛙的身世，后来的王者形象则依赖叙事情境。不能仅因名字含蛙，就把所有青蛙图案或祈雨习俗判定为对金蛙的祭祀。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 金蛙主要经由扶余与高句丽建国故事为人熟知，现代历史剧又扩展其人物性格。史书中的奇异出生具有王权合法性的叙事作用，但东扶余历史地理与神话细节仍须分层考察。

en.name: Geumwa
en.title: King of Eastern Buyeo in the Jumong Cycle

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Geumwa is king of Eastern Buyeo in Jumong's foundation narrative. The Samguk Sagi describes Haeburu discovering a child resembling a golden frog beneath a stone and adopting him as heir. This naming story does not establish a universally recognized frog deity across all traditions.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Geumwa shelters Yuhwa but reacts anxiously to her extraordinary egg, exposing it to animals and attempting unsuccessfully to break it before returning it. Jumong later excels at archery, provoking royal sons' jealousy and eventually leaving Buyeo. Geumwa offers protection without fully overcoming the dangers within his court.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The golden frog and discovery beneath a stone identify Geumwa's origin story most clearly. Later royal representations depend on narrative context rather than distinctive ancient attributes. His name alone provides no basis for assigning every frog image or rainmaking custom to worship of this king.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Geumwa is chiefly known through narratives linking Buyeo and Goguryeo origins, while modern historical dramas expand his characterization. Extraordinary origins can authorize royal succession within a story. Such narrative functions must be distinguished from unresolved questions about Eastern Buyeo's historical geography and chronology.

name: 施洗约翰
title: 旷野中的先知与耶稣的先驱

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 施洗约翰是第一世纪犹太地区的宗教人物，基督徒尊为耶稣的先驱。《路加福音》以撒迦利亚和以利沙伯为其父母，并叙述奇异降生；犹太史家约瑟夫斯也记载他，但关注重点与福音书有所不同。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 福音书记约翰在旷野宣讲悔改、为人施洗，并与耶稣受洗的事件相连，各卷的叙述方式并不相同。《马可福音》和《马太福音》把他被杀与希罗底及其女儿的宴席故事联系起来；约瑟夫斯则着重希律安提帕对群众动员的政治忧虑，二者不宜无差别拼接。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 骆驼毛衣、旷野、约旦河与施洗动作是常见标志。羔羊图像关联他指认耶稣为上帝羔羊的经文；托盘上的头颅表现殉难。具体持物随东西方艺术传统而变化。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 天主教、东正教及许多新教传统纪念约翰，但圣人敬礼与图像使用各不相同。曼达安宗教也高度尊崇他，却有独立的经典与神学，不应被写成基督教纪念传统的一个分支。

en.name: John the Baptist
en.title: Wilderness Preacher and Forerunner of Jesus

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: John the Baptist was a first century Jewish religious figure whom Christians honor as Jesus' forerunner. Luke names his parents Zechariah and Elizabeth and narrates a miraculous birth. The Jewish historian Josephus independently discusses John, although his interests and emphasis differ from those of the Gospels.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: The Gospels portray John preaching repentance and administering baptism, with differing presentations of Jesus' baptism. Mark and Matthew connect his execution with Herodias and her daughter's banquet performance. Josephus emphasizes Herod Antipas's fear of political unrest. These accounts should not be merged without acknowledging their different explanations.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Camel hair clothing, wilderness scenery, the Jordan, and baptismal gestures commonly identify John. A lamb recalls his designation of Jesus as the Lamb of God, while a severed head on a platter represents martyrdom. Specific attributes vary across Eastern and Western Christian artistic traditions.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Catholic, Orthodox, and many Protestant communities commemorate John, with differing approaches to saints and images. Mandaeans also hold him in high regard within an independent religious tradition. Their scriptures, rituals, and theology should not be reduced to a branch of Christian devotion to John.

name: 使徒约翰
title: 西庇太之子与约翰著作的归属传统

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 使徒约翰是新约所记十二使徒之一，西庇太之子、雅各的兄弟，与施洗约翰并非同一人。教会传统常将他与第四福音书及其他约翰著作相联，但使徒身份与各书作者的认定应分开说明。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 对观福音记约翰随耶稣受召，并与彼得、雅各见证登山变像和客西马尼园祈祷。《使徒行传》又写他与彼得在圣殿医治瘸腿者后受审。第四福音书中的所爱门徒未直接具名；把这位门徒认作使徒约翰，是重要的教会解释传统，并非经文明说的姓名。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 鹰常象征福音作者约翰，书卷提示著述，杯中蛇见于后世传说图像。年轻无须或年长有须的形象因传统而异；这些符号不能反过来证明使徒就是全部约翰著作的作者。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 许多教会敬奉他为使徒和福音作者。现代研究常区分使徒、所爱门徒、福音书编写者与《启示录》的约翰；书信归属及成书过程也有争论，并不存在一套所有学者一致认可的重建。

en.name: John the Apostle
en.title: Son of Zebedee and Johannine Authorship Traditions

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: John the Apostle is one of the Twelve in the New Testament, a son of Zebedee and brother of James, distinct from John the Baptist. Church traditions associate him with the Fourth Gospel and other Johannine writings, but apostolic identity and literary authorship require separate consideration.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: The Synoptic Gospels place John with Peter and James at the Transfiguration and in Gethsemane. Acts depicts John accompanying Peter in healing a man at the temple and facing interrogation. The Fourth Gospel leaves its beloved disciple unnamed; identifying that disciple as John belongs to influential church tradition.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The eagle commonly represents John the Evangelist, books evoke writing, and a serpent emerging from a cup belongs to later legendary imagery. Youthful beardless and elderly bearded depictions coexist. These artistic conventions cannot establish that the apostle authored every text traditionally associated with his name.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Many churches honor John as apostle and evangelist. Modern scholars often distinguish the apostle, beloved disciple, Gospel writers or editors, and the John of Revelation. The letters' attribution and compositional history also remain debated. No single reconstruction commands agreement among all scholars or Christian communities.

name: 孙悟空
title: 从花果山石卵中走出的齐天大圣

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 孙悟空是《西游记》的核心角色，由花果山顶仙石迸裂而生。其原型可溯至《大唐三藏取经诗话》中的猴行者、宋元话本与民间猴精传说，并吸收了佛教护法神将的形貌。明代百回本《西游记》使其定型，吴承恩的作者身份至今仍有争议。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他远渡学艺，得七十二般变化与筋斗云；闯龙宫取得定海神针，入地府勾销死籍；两度受天庭招安，因弼马温之辱与蟠桃会之愤大闹天宫，被如来压于五行山下。皈依后护送唐僧西行，历八十一难，终封斗战胜佛。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 金箍棒、紧箍、虎皮裙与筋斗云是稳定标识。金箍棒本是东海定海神针，可大可小；紧箍象征戒律对心性的约束。明清评点以“心猿”解释这一形象，把猴性、妄心与修行次第连成一条线索。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 应把孙悟空理解为文学英雄，而非自古普遍受祀的至上神。闽南、台湾与东南亚可见齐天大圣庙，属小说流行后的民间衍生。戏曲、动画与日韩改编不断重塑他，也使其形象逐渐远离原书语境。

en.name: Sun Wukong
en.title: The Monkey King born from a stone on Flower Fruit Mountain

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Sun Wukong is the central figure of the Ming novel Journey to the West. He is born from a stone egg on Flower Fruit Mountain. His lineage runs through the monkey pilgrim of the Tang-era Sutra of the Monkey Pilgrim, Song and Yuan storyteller tales, and older folk monkey spirits, with Buddhist guardian imagery layered on top.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He studies under a Daoist patriarch and gains seventy-two transformations and a cloud-somersault. He seizes the pillar from the Dragon King and erases his name from the registers of death. After two appointments in heaven end in humiliation, he wreaks havoc there and is pinned beneath Five Elements Mountain, later escorting the monk Xuanzang west.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: His staff, the tightened headband, tiger-skin kilt and somersault cloud identify him at once. The staff was a pillar stabilizing the sea and can shrink or grow at will. The headband stands for discipline imposed on a restless mind, a reading Ming commentators developed through the image of the monkey mind.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: He is best understood as a literary hero rather than an ancient universal deity. Temples to the Great Sage appear in Fujian, Taiwan and Southeast Asia, but these are folk offshoots of novel fame. Opera, animation and Japanese and Korean adaptations keep reshaping him, often far from the original text.

name: 哪吒
title: 析骨还父、莲身重生的少年神将

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 哪吒源于佛教护法神那吒，为毗沙门天王之子，唐代密教文献与宋代《景德传灯录》已见其名。中土叙事把他改造成李靖第三子，宋元禅宗灯录与《三教源流搜神大全》逐步丰富其身世，明代《封神演义》与《西游记》完成定型。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《封神演义》中他闹海打死龙王三太子，为免连累父母而剖腹剔骨，归还骨肉；太乙真人以莲花与荷叶为其重塑身体，授火尖枪、风火轮与乾坤圈。此后他辅佐周武王伐纣，屡为先锋，最终肉身成圣。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 莲花化身是其最鲜明的标志，意味脱去凡胎、超越血缘。图像常作童子相，束发、披甲或裸腹，足踏风火轮，手持火尖枪、混天绫与乾坤圈，身周有火焰纹样，脚踏轮宝可日行万里。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 哪吒故事把孝道、父权冲突与重生主题并置，历代讲唱与戏曲各有偏重。闽台与东南亚的哪吒太子信仰仍活跃，庙会中有阵头与乩童传统；1979年动画《哪吒闹海》与近年电影则给这一形象注入新的反抗色彩。

en.name: Nezha
en.title: The lotus-born boy warrior who returns his bones to his father

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Nezha descends from Nata, a Buddhist guardian and son of Vaisravana, attested in Tang esoteric texts and Song Chan records. Chinese storytellers made him the third son of the general Li Jing. Zen lamp records and the Yuan-Ming compendium of popular deities expanded his biography, which the novels Fengshen Yanyi and Journey to the West fixed.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Fengshen Yanyi he kills the Dragon Kings third son while sporting in the sea. To spare his parents retaliation he cuts open his belly and returns his flesh and bones. His master Taiyi Zhenren rebuilds him from lotus root and petals and arms him with spear, wheels and rings. He then fights for King Wu against the Shang.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The lotus body is his sharpest emblem, signalling release from ordinary birth and from blood obligation. He appears as a boy with hair bound, sometimes bare-chested, standing on wind-fire wheels, holding a flame-tipped spear, a length of crimson silk and a golden ring, often framed by flames.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: His story sets filial duty against paternal authority and adds rebirth. Ballads, opera and temple ritual each weight these themes differently. Devotion to Prince Nezha remains active in Fujian, Taiwan and Southeast Asia, with possessed mediums in temple processions, while modern animation recasts him as a rebel.

name: 二郎神
title: 灌口三只眼的猎神与伏魔元帅

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 二郎神以灌口二郎为原型，与战国秦守李冰次子治水传说相关，又有隋代赵昱斩蛟之说，学界亦追溯到氐羌地区的猎神与川西地方神。宋代已获朝廷敕封，后与杨戬之名合流，成为《西游记》《封神演义》中的重要神将。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 传说他居灌江口，率梅山七圣与一千二百草头神，斩蛟治水、护佑川西。他在《西游记》中奉旨擒拿孙悟空，与齐天大圣斗法变化；《封神演义》里则是玉泉山金霞洞的杨戬，善用八九玄功，屡次化险取胜。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 三只眼、三尖两刃刀、哮天犬与弹弓是他的标志，常着鹅黄袍、戴三山帽。天眼象征洞察邪祟，细犬用于追踪擒敌；他也被画成持弓挟弹的狩猎之神，与川西平原的治水记忆相连。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 二郎神信仰以四川灌县为中心，都江堰的二王庙至今祭祀李冰父子，六月二十四日有庙会。文本传统与地方治水祭祀长期并行，戏曲《二郎神醉射锁魔镜》等又添新情节，故其身份始终多元而非单一。

en.name: Erlang Shen
en.title: The three-eyed hunting god of the Guanjiang mouth

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Erlang Shen is rooted in the Guanjiang Erlang cult of western Sichuan, linked to Li Bing, the Qin governor who tamed the Min River, and to his son. A Sui-era tale credits the official Zhao Yu with slaying a dragon. Scholars also trace a Qiang hunting deity. Song courts granted him titles, and he was later merged with the figure Yang Jian.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He is said to command the Seven Sages of Meishan and twelve hundred local spirits from his seat at the Guan River mouth. In Journey to the West he is sent to capture Sun Wukong and matches the monkey in shape-shifting combat. In Fengshen Yanyi, as Yang Jian of Mount Yuquan, he wins battles through transformation.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A third eye, a double-bladed lance, a slender hound and a pellet bow mark him, along with a yellow robe and a three-peaked cap. The eye sees through demons, the dog tracks them down. He is also painted as a hunter with bow and pellets, tying him to the irrigated plains of Sichuan.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: His cult centers on Guanxian in Sichuan, where the Two Kings Temple at Dujiangyan still honours Li Bing and his son, with a fair on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. Local water-management ritual and literary epic have run in parallel, and opera keeps adding episodes, so his identity stays plural.

name: 夸父
title: 追逐落日而道渴的巨人

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 夸父是《山海经》中的巨人，记载分见《海外北经》与《大荒北经》，两处文字略有出入。一处称他为后土之孙、信之子，属炎帝谱系；另一处只记他与日竞走。先秦其他典籍少有提及，其形象基本依赖这部地理博物志保存。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《海外北经》说他与太阳竞逐，追至禺谷，口渴而饮黄河、渭水，不足，又北饮大泽，未至而道渴而死，弃下的手杖化为邓林，即桃林。《大荒北经》另记黄帝命应龙杀蚩尤后，夸父不从命而被杀，情节与逐日一版不同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 巨人形体、桃木杖与渴死道旁的结局构成主要识别要素。图像多画他迈步追赶落日，或倒地而手杖生根成林。桃林在后世兼具路标与庇荫之意，因此夸父也常被读作失败的追求者，或不肯停下的意志化身。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 陶渊明《读山海经》以“夸父诞宏志，乃与日竞走”咏其事，赋予其悲壮色彩；现代教科书与通俗读物则多强调不屈意志。须注意《山海经》各篇非一时一人所撰，不宜把两种死因强行统一为单一版本。

en.name: Kuafu
en.title: The giant who chased the setting sun and died of thirst

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Kuafu is a giant known from the Classic of Mountains and Seas, in two passages that differ in detail. One makes him grandson of Houtu and son of Xin, placing him in the Yan Emperor lineage; the other simply records his race against the sun. Few other pre-Qin texts mention him.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He chases the sun to the Yu Valley, then drinks the Yellow River and the Wei and is still thirsty. He heads north for the Great Marsh but dies on the road. His discarded staff becomes Denglin, the peach grove. A separate passage has him killed for disobeying the Yellow Emperor after the battle with Chiyou.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: His giant body, peach-wood staff and death by the roadside define him. Paintings show him striding after the sinking sun, or fallen while the staff takes root. The grove he leaves behind reads as both a landmark and shade for travellers, so he is often taken as a heroic failure.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Tao Yuanming wrote a famous poem on his grand ambition and race with the sun, giving the tale its tragic colour. Modern textbooks stress perseverance instead. The Classic of Mountains and Seas was compiled by many hands, so the two accounts of his death should not be forced into one.

name: 精卫
title: 衔木石以填东海的炎帝少女

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 精卫出自《山海经·北山经》：她是炎帝之女女娃，游于东海，溺而不返，化为鸟，名精卫，状如乌鸦，头有花纹，白喙赤足。原文极简短，却是后世诗文反复引用的核心文本；《述异记》等书再补其衔石填海与繁衍的情节。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 女娃溺死后化为精卫，常衔西山之木石投入东海，欲填平淹死自己的那片海。《述异记》补充说它与海燕配偶，所生之鸟雌雄同体，故其族不息。故事没有终点，填海的重复动作本身即是全部叙事，构成一种不设完成的循环。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 白喙、赤足、文首的小鸟是辨识标志，图像常作口衔树枝飞越波涛。填海之举被读作复仇、坚忍或徒劳，各时代取舍不同。“精卫填海”后来成为成语，与愚公移山并称，指不计成败的坚持。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《山海经》原文简略，后世注家与类书不断增饰，陶渊明、李白都曾以之为题。现代常把它纳入抗争自然的框架，但原文本的重心更近于丧女之痛与不肯中止的执念。它也被用作地名、船名与女性坚毅的象征。

en.name: Jingwei
en.title: The Yan emperors daughter who fills the eastern sea with twigs

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Jingwei appears in the Classic of Mountains and Seas as the Yan Emperor daughter Nüwa, who drowned while playing in the Eastern Sea and became a bird like a crow, with patterned head, white beak and red feet. The notice is very short, yet later poems return to it constantly, and the Record of Strange Things adds her endless filling of the sea.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Drowned, she flies from the western hills carrying twigs and stones in her beak and drops them into the Eastern Sea, the water that killed her. The later account has her mate with a sea swallow and bear young that are both male and female, so the flock never ends. There is no conclusion, only repetition.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A small bird with white beak, red feet and a marked head, usually painted carrying a branch over the waves. Her labour has been read as vengeance, as endurance, and as futility, with each age choosing its emphasis. The phrase jingwei filling the sea became a proverb for persistence regardless of outcome.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Commentators and encyclopedias kept enlarging the brief original, and poets from Tao Yuanming to Li Bai took it up. Modern retellings often frame it as defiance of nature, though the older text is closer to grief for a lost daughter and an refusal to stop. It also names places, boats and stubborn courage.

name: 蚩尤
title: 涿鹿之战中呼风唤雨的九黎之君

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 蚩尤是九黎之君，先秦文献对其立场分歧明显。《尚书·吕刑》把他写作作乱受罚者，《史记·五帝本纪》记他与黄帝战于涿鹿之野而被擒杀，《山海经·大荒北经》则说黄帝令应龙攻蚩尤。另有记载称他铜头铁额、兄弟八十一人。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 涿鹿之战中，蚩尤请风伯雨师纵大风雨，黄帝乃下天女魃止雨，并作指南车辨别方向，终擒蚩尤。山东、河北的地方传说又说他被肢解，身首分葬两地。苗族口传则尊他为祖先与英雄，与中原文献的乱贼形象形成鲜明对照。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 牛角、铜头、铁额与兵戈是常见标识，后世兵家奉他为“兵主”，汉高祖曾立祠祭祀。图像或作兽面人身，或作手执五兵的首领。他的形象介于部族始祖、战神与叛乱者之间，取决于讲述者所属的传统。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 关于蚩尤并无单一正典：儒典取其乱，兵家取其勇，苗族口传取其祖。秦汉方术与后世小说又添呼风唤雨、铸铁为兵的情节。研究时须留意各文本的政治立场，避免把某一种叙述当作唯一的历史事实。

en.name: Chiyou
en.title: Lord of the Nine Li and storm-raiser at the Zhuolu war

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Chiyou is lord of the Nine Li peoples, and early texts judge him very differently. The Book of Documents casts him as a rebel justly punished; the Records of the Grand Historian has him taken and killed by the Yellow Emperor at Zhuolu; the Classic of Mountains and Seas says the emperor sent the dragon Yinglong against him. He is also described with bronze head and iron brow.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: At Zhuolu he summons the wind and rain masters to batter the Yellow Emperor, who counters with the drought goddess Ba and a south-pointing chariot, then captures him. Regional tales in Shandong and Hebei say his body was quartered and buried in two places. Miao oral tradition honours him as an ancestor.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Horns, a metal-hard head and weapons identify him. Later military specialists honoured him as lord of war, and the Han founder built a shrine to him. He is drawn with a beast face on a human body, or as a chief wielding five weapons, standing somewhere between clan founder, war god and rebel.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: There is no single canonical Chiyou. Confucian texts take his disorder, soldiers his courage, Miao singers his ancestry. Han occult lore and later fiction add storm magic and casting of metal weapons. Any account should note the political stance of its source rather than treating one version as plain history.

name: 刑天
title: 断首犹舞干戚的无头巨人

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 刑天见于《山海经·海外西经》：“刑天与帝至此争神，帝断其首，葬之常羊之山。”原文未言“帝”为谁，注家多解作天帝或黄帝；有版本写作“形天”，属异文。先秦其他典籍不见其人，其形象几乎完全依赖这一条记载。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 被断首之后，他以双乳为目、以脐为口，继续挥舞盾与斧起舞，不肯倒下。文字极短，既无前因也无结局。后世注家推测其象征失败的抗争，陶渊明《读山海经》以“刑天舞干戚，猛志固常在”咏之，赋予他不肯中止的意志。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 无头之身、以乳为目、以脐为口，加上干（盾）与戚（斧），是其唯一稳定的形象要素。图像多画他赤裸上身、双乳作眼，立于常羊之山。陶诗流传之后，“舞干戚”成为不屈的典故，常与精卫填海并提。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 因原文过简，后世解说分歧很大：经学家或读作争位者的下场，文人则取其壮烈。现代通俗读物常把他列为战神，这并非古籍的定位。引用时宜注明出处仅《山海经》，并说明“帝”的身份在学界仍有争论。

en.name: Xingtian
en.title: The headless giant who dances with shield and axe

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Xingtian appears in one passage of the Classic of Mountains and Seas: he contends with the supreme lord for divine power, is beheaded, and is buried at Mount Changyang. The text never names that lord, and commentators identify him either as Heaven or the Yellow Emperor. Some editions write his name differently.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: With his head cut off he uses his nipples as eyes and his navel as a mouth, and keeps dancing with shield and axe instead of falling. The notice gives no cause and no ending. Tao Yuanming turned him into a byword for stubborn resolve that outlasts defeat.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A headless torso, breasts used as eyes, a navel as mouth, and the shield and axe are his only fixed features. He is painted bare-chested on Mount Changyang. After Tao poem circulated, dancing with shield and axe became a set phrase for unyielding defiance, often paired with Jingwei filling the sea.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Because the source is so brief, readings diverge: classical scholars saw a rebel punished, literati saw grandeur. Modern popular books list him as a war god, which the old text does not support. Quotations should note that the Classic of Mountains and Seas is the sole source and that the lords identity remains disputed.

name: 白蛇
title: 西湖断桥畔的蛇身女子白素贞

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 白蛇形象定型于《白蛇传》，远源可溯至宋代《西湖三塔记》的蛇精故事；明代冯梦龙《警世通言》中的《白娘子永镇雷峰塔》已具完整情节，清代方成培《雷峰塔》传奇与各地戏曲再加润色，遂成今日通行的白素贞。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 白素贞修炼千年化人，在西湖断桥与许仙相遇，结为夫妻并行医。法海认她为妖，端午雄黄使她现出原形，许仙惊死，白娘子盗仙草救夫；后水漫金山，终被镇于雷峰塔下，其子祭塔、塔倒团圆为后世所增。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 白衣女子与蛇身原形、断桥与油纸伞、雷峰塔与雄黄酒构成辨识要素。青蛇小青为伴，法海为对立面。故事把医药、水患与寺院权力缠在一起，塔既是镇压也是界限，端午习俗因此与情节相互绑定。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《白蛇传》属民间传说与戏曲传统，并非宗教经典。它与镇江金山寺、杭州雷峰塔的地方记忆彼此塑造；二十世纪五十年代经田汉改编为京剧与电影，情节更趋反抗礼教。各地说唱与宝卷版本差异明显，不宜只取一种。

en.name: White Snake
en.title: The serpent woman Bai Suzhen by Broken Bridge on West Lake

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: The white serpent took her present shape in the Legend of the White Snake. An earlier snake-spirit tale appears in a Song collection about the three pagodas of West Lake; Feng Menglong retold it in the Ming story Bai Niangzi Imprisoned Forever under Leifeng Pagoda, and Qing drama and local opera polished the version now known.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Bai Suzhen, cultivated for a thousand years, meets the pharmacist Xu Xian at Broken Bridge and marries him. The monk Fahai denounces her as a demon; realgar wine at the Dragon Boat festival forces her true form, and Xu Xian dies of fright. She steals the herb of immortality, floods Jinshan, and is buried beneath Leifeng Pagoda.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A woman in white and her serpent body, Broken Bridge and an oil-paper umbrella, the pagoda and realgar wine are the fixed markers. The green snake Xiaoqing attends her; Fahai opposes her. Medicine, flood and monastic power tangle together, and the pagoda works as both prison and boundary.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: This is folk narrative and opera, not scripture. It grew alongside local memory at Jinshan Temple and Leifeng Pagoda. Tian Han rewrote it for stage and film in the 1950s, sharpening its anti-authoritarian edge. Ballad and precious-scroll versions differ widely, so no single text should stand for all.

name: 日本武尊
title: 持草薙剑东征西讨的悲剧皇子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 日本武尊见于《古事记》与《日本书纪》，为景行天皇之子，本名小碓命，又称倭建命。两书成于八世纪初，叙事带有明显的编纂意图，把他塑成服从王权、替父征讨的皇子；“日本武”是后世的追称，熊袭之役时仍称小碓。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他奉命征讨熊袭，男扮女装刺杀川上枭帅；又东征出云与毛野，遭当地人纵火围山，以草薙剑斩草开路脱险。归途在足柄山望见亡妻弟橘媛投海之处，悲叹成疾，最后于伊势能褒野化为白鸟飞去，陵墓与白鸟传说分处多地。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 草薙剑（天丛云剑）是核心标志，与八咫镜、八尺琼勾玉并称三种神器。图像多作持剑的年轻皇子，或作白鸟升空之姿。故事中的火攻、渡海与变身，使他在明治以后被反复用作忠君与武勇的宣传素材。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《古事记》用和文体，重歌谣与情感；《日本书纪》用汉文体，强调制度与天皇权威，两书细节互有出入。中世《平家物语》等屡引其典。近代学校教育与国家神道共同塑造了公众印象，需与八世纪文本区分开看。

en.name: Yamato Takeru
en.title: The tragic prince who carried the grass-cutting sword

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Yamato Takeru appears in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki as a son of Emperor Keiko, born Prince Ousu and also called Yamato Woguna. Both chronicles were compiled in the early eighth century with clear political aims, casting him as a prince who conquers on his fathers behalf. The title Yamato Takeru is a later honorific.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Sent against the Kumaso, he dresses as a woman and stabs their chief. On campaign in Izumo and Kenu he is trapped by a grass fire and cuts his way out with the sword Kusanagi. Grieving for his wife Ototachibana, who drowned for him, he falls ill and rises as a white bird at Nobono in Ise.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The Kusanagi sword, taken from the eight-headed serpent, is his central emblem and one of the three imperial regalia. He is shown as a young prince with a blade, or as a white bird ascending. Fire, sea crossing and shape-shifting in his story made him useful for Meiji-era lessons in loyalty and martial courage.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Kojiki uses Japanese-style prose and highlights songs and grief, while the Nihon Shoki uses literary Chinese and stresses institutions and imperial authority; details disagree. Medieval war tales cite him often. Modern schooling and State Shinto shaped the public image, which should be kept distinct from the eighth-century texts.

name: 八岐大蛇
title: 出云八头八尾的洪水之蛇

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 八岐大蛇是《古事记》《日本书纪》所记的出云巨蛇，八头八尾，背上生桧与杉，身长跨八谷八丘，腹部常溃烂流血。它每年吞食出云国一名少女，是须佐之男神话的前段。作为怪物而非神格，其名又写作“八俣远吕智”。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 须佐之男被逐出高天原，降至出云簸川上游，遇见足名椎、手名椎夫妇为第八个女儿栉名田比卖哭泣。他令酿酒八次，筑八门栅栏，置八桶烈酒。大蛇八头各饮一桶而醉卧，他逐一斩之，在尾部取得天丛云剑，献于天照大神。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 八头八尾、眼如酸浆、背生林木、腹常流血是固定描写。图像多作盘绕山间的巨蛇，八头各据一谷。酒与八门栅栏是制服它的关键道具，草薙剑由此进入三种神器谱系，斩蛇之地与斐伊川上游的须我神社相连。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 故事为洪水与河道变迁提供解释，也标志须佐之男由暴神转为文化英雄，并为其后裔大国主让出出云埋下伏笔。近代常把大蛇读作水患或制铁集团的隐喻，但这些属解释而非文本明言。出云至今存相关神社与祭仪。

en.name: Yamata no Orochi
en.title: The eight-headed serpent of Izumo and the annual flood

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Yamata no Orochi is the serpent of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, with eight heads and eight tails, cedars and cypresses growing on its back, a body spanning eight valleys and eight hills, and a belly that bleeds constantly. It eats one daughter of Izumo each year and belongs to the opening of the Susanoo cycle.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Driven from the high plain of heaven, Susanoo meets an old couple weeping over their eighth daughter, Kushinada. He brews liquor eight times, builds an eightfold fence with eight vats, and the serpent dips one head into each and falls asleep. Cutting it apart, he finds the sword Ame no Murakumo in its tail.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Eight heads and tails, eyes like winter cherries, forest on its back and a bleeding belly are the fixed details. It is painted coiled across mountains with heads in separate valleys. The liquor and the eight gates are the tools that defeat it, and its tail yields a sword of the imperial regalia.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The tale explains floods and shifting rivers, marks Susanoo turning from storm god into culture hero, and prepares the yielding of Izumo by his descendant Okuninushi. Modern readers often take the serpent as a flood or iron-working metaphor. Shrines and rites along the upper Hii River still point to the site.

name: 鲶鱼
title: 被要石镇压的地震之鲶

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 地震鲶是日本民间用来解释地震的巨型鲶鱼，主要流行于近世。它栖于地下或常世之国，翻身即引起地动。鹿岛神宫的祭神武瓮槌命以“要石”将其头尾钉住，另说由香取神宫的经津主神协助镇守。此说在江户文献与鲶绘中大量出现。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 传说鲶鱼被要石压住，一旦松动便引发地震。1855年安政江户地震之后，市井大量印制“鲶绘”，或画鲶鱼作乱、鹿岛神持剑追赶，或画百姓合力痛打鲶鱼。这类版画兼有泄愤、祈福与讥刺世情之用，因幕府查禁而多有变体。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 巨鲶、要石、鹿岛神宫的宝剑与雷纹是辨识要素。鲶绘中常并置鲶鱼、鹿岛大明神、受灾的商人与工匠，构图带讽刺意味。鹿岛要石露出地面的尖端被视为镇压之证，香取要石亦属同一系统。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 地震鲶处在民间信仰与早期地震学的交界，明治以后随近代地震学兴起而转弱，却在动漫、地方祭事与灾害教育中延续。它体现前科学时代以动物行为解释灾异的思路，也保留了江户市民对灾害的幽默与怨气。

en.name: Onamazu
en.title: The giant catfish pinned beneath the earthquake stone

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Onamazu is the giant catfish of Japanese folk belief, used to explain earthquakes, mainly from the early modern period. It lies under the earth or in the land of the everworld, and its turning shakes the ground. The deity of Kashima Shrine, Takemikazuchi, pins its head and tail with a keystone, sometimes helped by Katori Shrine.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: As long as the stone holds, the catfish cannot move; when it slips, the earth quakes. After the Ansei Edo earthquake of 1855, cheap prints called namazu-e flooded the city, showing the fish rampaging, Kashima chasing it with a sword, or townspeople beating it. Censorship produced many variants.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A huge catfish, the keystone, a sword and thunder motifs identify the complex. In the prints the fish appears beside the Kashima deity, ruined shopkeepers and carpenters, often with satirical framing. The tip of the stone that shows above ground at Kashima is displayed as proof of its grip.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The catfish sits between folk cosmology and early seismology, fading as scientific geology arrived in the Meiji era but surviving in animation, local festivals and disaster education. It shows a pre-scientific habit of reading animal behaviour as omen, and preserves Edo humour and anger about catastrophe.

name: 酒吞童子
title: 大江山统领群鬼的鬼王酒吞童子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 酒吞童子是日本最著名的鬼王之一，传说据守丹波国大江山，一说在近江伊吹山，统领群鬼，掠走贵族女子与财宝。其名见于中世《御伽草子》系统的酒吞童子绘卷，能剧《大江山》与谣曲亦演其事，各本情节略有出入。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 源赖光受命讨伐，携赖光四天王渡边纲、坂田金时、碓井贞光、卜部季武入山。他们得山神指点，扮作山伏，以神便鬼毒酒诱童子饮下，趁其醉卧斩首。首级飞起咬向赖光，被头盔挡下；所用太刀因此得名“童子切安纲”。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 赤面、独角、虎皮裈与巨大身躯是常见形象，酒与铁盔是关键道具。图像多作宴饮场面或斩首瞬间。童子切安纲实存并为日本国宝，其与故事的联系属后世附会，却强化了刀剑传说中的英雄谱系。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 酒吞童子与茨木童子、大狱丸等构成鬼退治故事群，经绘卷、能乐、歌舞伎与近代小说不断传播。大江山一带借鬼传说发展观光，福知山等地有相关祭事。其形象也大量进入游戏与动画，与原文本已有相当距离。

en.name: Shuten Doji
en.title: The drunken demon king who ruled the ghosts of Mount Oe

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Shuten Doji is among the best known Japanese demon kings, said to hold Mount Oe in Tamba, or Mount Ibuki in Omi, commanding a band of oni and abducting noble women and treasure. He appears in medieval illustrated tales of the Otogi-zoshi cycle, and in the noh play Oe and its chant, with details varying between versions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The warrior Minamoto no Yorimitsu sets out with his four retainers, including Watanabe no Tsuna and Sakata Kintoki. Guided by mountain deities, they disguise themselves as ascetics and persuade the demon to drink poisoned sake. When he sleeps they cut off his head, which flies at Yorimitsu and is stopped by his helmet.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A red face, single horn, tiger-skin trousers and enormous body are standard, with sake and an iron helmet as the decisive props. He is painted at his banquet or at the instant of beheading. The sword Dojigiri, a national treasure, is linked to the deed by later tradition rather than by the tale itself.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: He belongs with Ibaraki Doji and Oeyama no Shutendoji in a cluster of demon-quelling tales spread through picture scrolls, noh, kabuki and modern fiction. The Oe area markets the legend to visitors and hold related rites. Games and animation reuse him freely, well beyond the medieval texts.

name: 处容
title: 驱散疫神的东海龙王之子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 处容是统一新罗时期的传说人物，事见《三国遗事》卷二“处容郎·望海寺”条。相传他为东海龙王之子，随海神之女来到新罗京城，因歌舞出众得国王赏识，授级干之职并赐宅第。其故事是现存处容歌与处容舞的直接来源。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 传说瘟疫神爱慕其妻，夜入其宅与之同寝。处容归来见状，不怒而歌且舞，退而让之。疫神愧悔，现身谢罪，发誓此后凡见处容之像者不入其门。民间遂贴处容画像以驱疫，处容歌与处容舞由此成为仪式表演。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 面具、歌舞与门前画像构成其主要标识。处容舞为面具舞，动作舒缓，常由五人着不同衣色演出，属宫廷呈才；图像中的处容或作方面长髯的官员形象。其功能是逐疫与调和，而非战争或丰产。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《三国遗事》由高丽僧人一然编成，采录民间旧说，故处容故事兼具史事与神话层次。处容舞在朝鲜王朝宫廷被整理为呈才，2009年列入联合国教科文组织人类非物质文化遗产名录，今由国立国乐院等机构传承。

en.name: Cheoyong
en.title: The dragon kings son who drove plague from the house

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Cheoyong belongs to the Unified Silla period and is recorded in the Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, in the section on the Cheoyong ward and Manghaesa. He is said to be a son of the East Sea dragon king, who comes to the Silla capital with a sea deity daughter, wins royal favour through song and dance, and receives rank and a house.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: A plague spirit falls in love with his wife and lies with her while Cheoyong is away. Returning, he does not rage but sings and dances, then steps aside. Ashamed, the spirit appears, apologizes, and swears never to enter a door where Cheoyongs image hangs. Portraits were pasted up against epidemic.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Masks, song and dance, and the portrait at the gate identify him. Cheoyongmu is a mask dance in slow, measured steps, often performed by five dancers in different colours as court repertoire. He is pictured as a bearded official with a broad face. His power is against plague and disorder, not war.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Memorabilia was compiled by the Goryeo monk Iryeon from older local lore, so history and myth overlap in the entry. Cheoyongmu was codified as court dance in the Joseon period and was inscribed on the UNESCO list of intangible heritage in 2009; the National Gugak Center keeps it today.

name: 罗摩
title: 流放十四年的阿逾陀王子与法之化身

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 罗摩是史诗《罗摩衍那》的主人公，传统归于诗人蚁垤。他是阿逾陀国王十车王的长子，被视为毗湿奴的第七次化身。史诗经数百年层累而成，约自公元前数世纪至公元初年，另有《罗摩功行录》等各地改写本。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 因继母吉迦伊求取旧愿，罗摩被放逐十四年，与妻子悉多、弟罗什曼那入林。楞伽魔王罗波那劫走悉多，罗摩与猴族结盟，哈奴曼越海探讯，大军架桥渡海，杀罗波那而复得悉多。归国登位，史称罗摩之治；后续篇章又写其疑悉多贞节，情节转沉痛。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 弓与箭、深蓝肤色、王冠，以及与悉多并肩的形象最为常见，哈奴曼为其信使与战士。图像多作持弓欲射之姿，或与悉多、罗什曼那、哈奴曼同列。罗摩之治成为理想政治的代称，排灯节即纪念其归国。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 罗摩在印度教中是活态信仰的对象，被视为达摩的化身，阿逾陀等地有其圣地与节庆。史诗经迦梨陀娑、杜尔西达斯及东南亚诸本（如泰国《拉玛坚》、爪哇皮影）多层改写，各地伦理重点与情节均有差异。

en.name: Rama
en.title: The exiled prince of Ayodhya and embodiment of dharma

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Rama is the hero of the Ramayana, traditionally ascribed to the poet Valmiki. He is the eldest son of Dasharatha, king of Ayodhya, and is held to be the seventh avatar of Vishnu. The epic grew over centuries, roughly from the last centuries BCE into the early common era, and regional retellings such as Tulsidas Hindi version reshape it.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His stepmother Kaikeyi claims two old boons, and Rama is exiled for fourteen years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana. Ravana of Lanka abducts Sita; Rama allies with the monkeys, Hanuman leaps the sea, a bridge is built, and Ravana is killed. Later books add the painful doubt over Sita.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Bow and arrows, dark blue skin, a crown, and his place beside Sita are standard, with Hanuman as messenger and warrior. He is shown drawing the bow or standing with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman. Rama Rajya became a byword for just rule, and Diwali marks his return to Ayodhya.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: For Hindus Rama is a living focus of devotion and an embodiment of dharma, with sacred sites and festivals at Ayodhya and elsewhere. The epic was retold by Kalidasa, Tulsidas and across Southeast Asia, including the Thai Ramakien and Javanese shadow theatre, with different ethical emphases.

name: 黑天
title: 持笛的牧牛神与俱卢之野的御者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 黑天是印度教最重要的神祇之一，被视为毗湿奴的第八次化身。其形象综合了《摩诃婆罗多》中的战车御者与《薄伽梵往世书》第十篇的牧童，另有多部往世书与《诃利世系》补充谱系。学界多认为牧童黑天的传统源自马图拉一带的民间崇拜。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他生于马图拉牢狱，父为婆苏提婆，母为提婆吉，为避舅父康萨迫害而被送往牛庄抚养。少年时降伏毒蛇迦梨耶，举起牛增山为牧人遮雨，与牧女拉达相恋。成年后杀康萨，建多门城；在俱卢之野为阿周那御车，宣讲《薄伽梵歌》。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 蓝黑色肤色、孔雀羽冠、黄色绸衣与横笛是标准标识，常作一足交叉的吹笛姿态。少年形象与拉达并置，表达虔诚之爱；《薄伽梵歌》中的御者形象则代表正法与解脱的教导，二者共同构成其神性。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 黑天信仰在印度是活态宗教，马图拉、弗林达文、普里与古吉拉特均有重要圣地与节庆，如黑天诞辰节与洒红节。拉达与黑天之爱被虔诚派诗人反复吟咏，孟加拉、拉贾斯坦与南印度各有地方传统与表演形式。

en.name: Krishna
en.title: The flute-playing cowherd and charioteer at Kurukshetra

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Krishna is among the central deities of Hinduism and the eighth avatar of Vishnu. His figure joins the charioteer of the Mahabharata with the cowherd boy of the tenth book of the Bhagavata Purana, and other Puranas and the Harivamsha add genealogy. Scholars often trace the cowherd tradition to devotion around Mathura.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Born in a Mathura prison to Vasudeva and Devaki, he is carried to a cowherd village to escape his uncle Kamsa. As a boy he subdues the serpent Kaliya, lifts Govardhan hill to shelter the herdsmen, and loves Radha. He kills Kamsa, founds Dvaraka, and teaches the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Dark blue-black skin, a peacock feather crown, yellow silk and a bamboo flute identify him, usually standing with legs crossed as he plays. With Radha he figures the longing of devotional love; as Arjunas charioteer he figures dharma and release. Both together make up his divinity.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Krishna devotion is living religion in India, with major centres at Mathura, Vrindavan, Puri and in Gujarat, and festivals such as Janmashtami and Holi. The love of Radha and Krishna was sung by devotional poets, and Bengal, Rajasthan and South India each developed distinctive traditions and performance styles.

name: 迦楼罗
title: 背负毗湿奴的金翅鸟王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 迦楼罗是印度神话中的鸟王，毗湿奴的坐骑与旗徽。史诗与往世书说他是迦叶波与毗娜达之子；母亲与迦德卢赌博失败，使他沦为众蛇（那伽）的奴仆，须取甘露赎身。汉译佛典称金翅鸟，佛教将其列为八部众之一。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 为救母，他力战众神夺取甘露，途中与因陀罗交手，毗湿奴感其勇而允诺他居于自己的旗帜上并得长生。他与那伽世代为仇，以蛇为食。另一系叙事说甘露最终被蛇族设计取得，成为蛇蜕皮的由来，诸本细节并不一致。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 金翅、人面鸟身、利爪与擒蛇之姿是辨识要素，常作展翅欲飞或足踏那伽。与蛇的对立表达天界与地下势力的张力。其像见于毗湿奴庙旗杆顶端、门楣与护符，东南亚亦奉为守护神与王权象征。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 迦楼罗在印度教、佛教与耆那教中各有位置。印尼国徽与泰国国徽均用其形，爪哇、巴厘的迦楼罗与本地鹰崇拜混合。佛教故事中他与龙族仍为怨敌，汉地寺院常塑于佛座旁，藏传亦有其专门的护法形态。

en.name: Garuda
en.title: The golden-winged bird king who carries Vishnu

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Garuda is the king of birds in Indian myth, the mount and banner emblem of Vishnu. Epic and Puranic texts make him son of Kashyapa and Vinata; when his mother loses a wager to Kadru, he becomes servant to the nagas and must fetch amrita to buy her freedom. Buddhist texts call him the golden-winged bird.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: To free his mother he fights the gods and seizes the amrita, clashing with Indra on the way. Pleased by his courage, Vishnu grants him a place on his banner and long life. He is the eternal enemy of the nagas and feeds on snakes, though versions differ on how the nagas finally obtain the amrita.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Golden wings, a human face on a bird body, talons and a serpent in his grip identify him, shown spreading his wings or standing on a naga. The enmity with serpents figures the tension between sky and underworld. His image crowns temple flagpoles and doorways across India and Southeast Asia.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Garuda holds a place in Hindu, Buddhist and Jain traditions. Indonesia and Thailand both use him in national emblems, and Javanese and Balinese forms blend with local eagle cults. In Buddhist lore he still opposes the nagas, commonly carved beside Buddha images and given guardian roles in Tibetan art.

name: 阎摩
title: 开辟冥途的第一位死者与冥界之王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阎摩是印度的死神与冥界之王，也是方位守护者之一，主南方。其名见于《梨俱吠陀》第十卷第十四曲，那里他是第一个死去的人，为亡者开出道路；后来的往世书把他写成依业报审判亡魂的法官，佛教的阎罗王即由此演化。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 吠陀中说阎摩与妹阎蜜是最早的一对凡人，他死后成为亡者之王，居于天界深处，由两只四眼犬守门。《摩诃婆罗多》与往世书则写他持棒与绳，掌生死簿，遣使拘魂；其侍从“迦罗”（时间）与死亡时刻相关，各派叙事又有调整。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 水牛坐骑、棒杖、绳索与南方方位是主要标识；图像或作骑水牛的王者，或作持镜与簿册的判官，肤色深暗，冠饰庄严。两只斑纹四眼犬为其使者，在葬礼咒文中被请求放行亡者。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阎摩在印度教中是活态信仰的一部分，阎摩二日节与排灯节相连，姊妹为兄弟祈福。佛教的阎魔与藏传阎罗形象大变，汉地十殿阎罗又与之混合，民间图像多为判官而非吠陀中的亡者之王，不宜把各系统等同。

en.name: Yama
en.title: The first mortal to die and lord of the southern realm

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Yama is the god of death and king of the underworld in India, and one of the directional guardians, holding the south. He appears in the tenth mandala of the Rig Veda as the first person to die, who opens the path for others. Later Puranas make him a judge who allots rebirth according to karma.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Vedic hymns Yama and his sister Yami are the first mortals; after death he rules the departed in a distant heaven, guarded by two four-eyed dogs. Epic and Puranic accounts give him a staff and noose, a register of lifespans, and messengers who fetch the dying. Details shift between traditions.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A water buffalo mount, staff, noose and the southern direction mark him. He is painted as a dark-skinned king on a buffalo, or as a scribe-judge with mirror and ledger. Two brindled four-eyed dogs serve as his messengers and are asked in funeral verses to let the dead pass.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Yama remains part of living Hindu practice; Yama Dwitiya follows Diwali, when sisters pray for their brothers. Buddhist Yama and the Tibetan lord of death differ sharply, and Chinese ten-court imagery blends with both. The popular figure of a stern clerk is far from the Vedic first mortal.

name: 阿耆尼
title: 承载祭品的圣火与神人之口

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿耆尼是吠陀的火神，也是祭火本身，在《梨俱吠陀》中受赞颂的次数仅次于因陀罗。他被称为祭司与祭品之口，把供物送往诸神。其名与拉丁语 ignis 同源，属印欧语系的火神谱系；佛教将其吸收为护法之一。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他生于祭坛之火，也生于水中与云中，故有“水生者”之称。诸神派他往返人间与天界，充当使者。史诗与往世书另记他因诅咒隐匿水中，致使世间无火，众神后来请他复出；他与斯瓦哈的婚姻解释了祭献时呼“斯瓦哈”的习俗。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 火焰、赤红肤色、三足或四臂、持酥油勺与念珠，骑公羊，为其标识。图像多作正面端坐、口吐火舌，两脸或三脸表示其遍在。祭仪中的三座火坛对应其三种形态：家主火、供火与南火。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿耆尼是活态祭祀的核心，印度教婚礼、火供与临终仪式仍以火为中介。佛教中他为火天，密教曼荼罗列有其位；琐罗亚斯德教的火庙常被误与之等同，二者虽出同源词根，神学结构并不相同。

en.name: Agni
en.title: The sacred fire that carries offerings and speaks for gods

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Agni is the Vedic god of fire and the ritual flame itself, praised in the Rig Veda more often than any deity except Indra. He is called the priest and the mouth of the offering, carrying gifts to the gods. His name is cognate with Latin ignis, placing him in an Indo-European fire-god family.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He is born from the altar fire, and also from water and the storm cloud, hence his epithet of one born in water. The gods use him as envoy between earth and heaven. Epic and Puranic tales say a curse drove him to hide in water, leaving the world without fire until the gods called him back.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Flame, red skin, three legs or four arms, a butter ladle and prayer beads, with a ram as mount, identify him. He sits facing the worshipper with fire streaming from his mouth; two or three faces express his presence everywhere. Three ritual fires correspond to his forms.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Agni stands at the centre of living ritual: Hindu weddings, fire offerings and funeral rites still work through flame. Buddhism receives him as the fire deity, with a place in esoteric mandalas. Zoroastrian fire temples are often compared with him, but shared etymology does not mean shared theology.

name: 因陀罗
title: 持金刚杵的雷雨之神与天界之王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 因陀罗是吠陀诸神之首，司雷雨与战争，手持金刚杵，饮苏摩，居三十三天。《梨俱吠陀》约四分之一赞歌与他相关。佛教吸收他为帝释天，居忉利天而为护法之主；印度教后期其地位下降，让位于毗湿奴与湿婆。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 最著名的是他与弗栗多之战：蛇形恶魔阻塞水流，因陀罗以金刚杵击杀之，释放七河。另说他因杀弗栗多或触犯婆罗门而获罪，隐居忏悔。史诗中他屡次试探凡人英雄；《薄伽梵往世书》写他因傲慢降下暴雨，被黑天举牛增山对抗。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 金刚杵、白象艾罗婆那、雷云与苏摩酒是标识。图像或作骑白象的王者，或作持杵的战士，周身有千眼，传说因诅咒所化。其天宫与难陀那园在佛典中转为忉利天的善见城，成为帝释天的居所。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 因陀罗在印度仍受祭祀，但相对毗湿奴与湿婆已属次级。尼泊尔加德满都的因陀罗节至今盛大举行，有神像巡游与竹竿仪式。通俗读物常把他比作汉地玉皇大帝，二者功能相近而来源不同，不宜直接等同。

en.name: Indra
en.title: The thunderbolt-wielding king of storm and heaven

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Indra heads the Vedic pantheon as god of storm and war, carrying the vajra, drinking soma, and ruling from the heaven of the thirty-three gods. About a quarter of the Rig Veda addresses him. Buddhism adopts him as Shakra, lord of the Trayastrimsha heaven and protector of the teaching; later Hinduism subordinates him to Vishnu and Shiva.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His great deed is killing Vritra, the serpent demon who holds back the waters, and releasing the seven rivers. Other traditions have him polluted by that killing or by an offence against a brahmin, and he withdraws to do penance. The Bhagavata Purana tells how his pride brings a deluge that Krishna answers by lifting a hill.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The vajra, the white elephant Airavata, storm clouds and soma mark him. He appears as a king on an elephant or a warrior with the bolt, his body covered in a thousand eyes said to come from a curse. His palace and Nandana grove became the Buddhist heaven of Shakra.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Indra is still worshipped in India, though secondary to Vishnu and Shiva. Kathmandu holds a large Indra Jatra with processions and the raising of a pole. Popular writing often equates him with the Chinese Jade Emperor; their functions overlap, but their origins and mythologies do not.

name: 不可杀
title: 以铁为食的朝鲜镇国怪兽

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 不可杀是朝鲜传说中的食铁怪兽，名意为“杀不死之物”。传说它由僧人、铁匠或孤苦老妇以米粒、纸张塑形而成，得气而活，专食铁器。故事散见朝鲜王朝野谈与口传，没有早期定本，成书年代与地域已难确考。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 它初生时只食米粒，渐而吞铁，农具、锅釜、刀剑皆入其腹，民家不堪其扰。一说官方便铸铁像诱其吞食，或以火攻、水淹而无效；蒙古入侵时期的故事则说它吞尽敌军兵器，护佑村庄，故有镇国之称。各本结局不同，或被杀，或隐入山中。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 铁齿、巨口与以铁为食的躯体是核心特征，形象或作四足带鳞之兽，或作鼻端生角的巨怪。1985年电影《不可杀》把它塑造成温顺的守护者，与传说中为害的怪兽形成对照，成为今日最流行的一版。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 不可杀属口传母题，朝鲜王朝野谈与近代童谣各有版本，1950年代后的儿童读物又将其简化为友谊故事。1985年影片因版权纠纷成为著名案例，也使它进入流行文化。研究时应区分电影形象与口传内容。

en.name: Bulgasari
en.title: The iron-eating monster that guards Korean villages

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Bulgasari is an iron-eating monster of Korean legend, its name meaning the unkillable one. Tales say a monk, a blacksmith or a lonely old woman shaped it from rice grains or paper, and that it came alive and fed on iron. The stories appear in Joseon-era miscellanies and oral tellings, with no early fixed text.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: It begins by eating rice, then swallows iron, taking in farm tools, cauldrons and swords, until households cannot bear it. Some versions have officials cast an iron image to lure it, or try fire and water without success. In invasion tales it devours enemy weapons and protects villages, earning a reputation as a national guardian.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Iron teeth, a huge mouth and a body nourished on metal define it. It is drawn as a four-legged scaly beast or a horned monster. The 1985 North Korean film turned it into a gentle protector rather than a menace, and that version is now the one most people know.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Bulgasari is oral material, retold in Joseon miscellanies, modern songs for children and picture books that soften it into a story about friendship. The 1985 film and its copyright dispute made it famous abroad. Scholarship separates the film figure from the older motif, which has several endings.

name: 九尾狐
title: 化为美女夜取人心的千年狐妖

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 九尾狐是中韩共有的狐妖母题，中国《山海经》已有“青丘之狐，其状如狐而九尾”的记载。朝鲜半岛的九尾狐故事见于《三国史记》《三国遗事》及朝鲜朝野谈与口传，通常写修炼千年的狐狸化女惑人、夜取人心或内丹，与中国祥瑞型的九尾狐取向不同。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 典型故事说狐狸修炼千年，化为美貌女子接近男子，吸取精气或取其肝。男子若识破其真身，须严守禁忌：不点破、不从其言，或熬过百日。另一类故事写女子真心爱慕，却因身份暴露而不得不离开。结局随地域与讲述者而异。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 九条尾、月下现身、狐火与内丹是辨识要素；图像多作长发的白衣女子，身后隐现狐尾。九尾象征年久通灵，内丹被人吞下后可获得辨真之力。狐妖形象与山神、巫女在民间叙事中彼此渗透，界限并不固定。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 九尾狐是仍在流传的口传母题，朝鲜半岛的讲述与中国狐仙传统互相影响又各自发展。现代影视与漫画常把它重写为爱情或复仇故事，形象远比口传温柔。应避免把影视设定当成传统信仰，也不宜与日本的狐信仰混为一谈。

en.name: Gumiho
en.title: The nine-tailed fox who takes human form at night

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: The nine-tailed fox is a motif shared by China and Korea; the Classic of Mountains and Seas already describes a fox with nine tails in the Green Hills. Korean versions appear in the Historical Records of the Three Kingdoms, the Memorabilia, Joseon miscellanies and oral tales, where a fox of a thousand years becomes a woman and steals energy or a liver.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the usual plot a fox cultivates for a thousand years, takes the form of a beautiful woman, and approaches men to drain their vitality or take their liver. A man who sees through her must keep strict taboos, saying nothing or surviving a hundred days. Other versions make her genuinely loving and doomed by exposure.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Nine tails, appearances under the moon, fox fire and the fox bead identify her. She is painted as a long-haired woman in white with tails faintly visible behind her. The bead, swallowed by a man, grants the power to see the truth. Fox, mountain spirit and shaman often blur together in these stories.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Gumiho tales are still told, and Korean telling and Chinese fox-lore have influenced each other while developing apart. Film and comics now recast her as a romantic or vengeful figure far gentler than the oral fox. Screen versions should not be taken for traditional belief, nor confused with Japanese fox lore.

name: 舞王湿婆
title: 以舞承载宇宙生灭的舞王湿婆

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 舞王相是湿婆的一种造像形式，盛行于南印度朱罗王朝，约九至十三世纪。梵语名“Nataraja”意为舞之王，所跳为阿难陀之舞，象征宇宙的创造、维持与毁灭。核心圣地是泰米尔纳德邦的奇丹巴拉姆，其黄金大厅至今供奉此像。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 神话中说湿婆在奇丹巴拉姆起舞，以折服异端或向诸神示现。舞姿由若干基本动作组成；他一脚踏住侏儒阿帕斯马拉，象征压伏无明，另一脚抬起，表示解脱与庇护。舞中同时毁灭与再造世界，因此被称为舞中的宇宙。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 右上手持鼓，象征创造之音；左上手持火，象征毁灭；右下作施无畏印，左下手臂指向抬起的脚，表示归依；周身火环代表宇宙循环。发间恒河女神、新月与骷髅为附属标志，像座多作莲花，整体呈均衡的三角构图。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 舞王相属活态宗教艺术，奇丹巴拉姆等地仍有铸造与祭祀；朱罗铜像大量流入欧美博物馆，也引发掠夺与归还的争论。它已成印度文化的重要符号，见于节庆、舞台与科研机构雕塑，但解读时不应脱离湿婆信仰。

en.name: Nataraja
en.title: Shiva as lord of the dance that makes and ends worlds

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Nataraja is a form of Shiva as lord of dance, established in South India under the Chola dynasty between roughly the ninth and thirteenth centuries. The Sanskrit name means king of dancers, and the pose is the dance of bliss, figuring creation, preservation and destruction. Its principal home is the golden hall at Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Temple tradition places the dance at Chidambaram, performed to confound rivals or to reveal himself to the gods. The pose is built from units of dance movement. One foot pins the dwarf Apasmara, meaning ignorance, while the other is raised to offer release. In the dance he destroys and remakes the world.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The upper right hand holds a drum for the sound of creation, the upper left a flame for destruction. The lower right shows the gesture of fearlessness, and the lower left points to the raised foot as refuge. A ring of fire frames the cosmos, with Ganges, crescent moon and skull in the hair.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Nataraja remains living sacred art, still cast and worshipped at Chidambaram and elsewhere. Chola bronzes entered Western museums in large numbers and are now part of debates over repatriation. The image has become a symbol of Indian culture, yet it should not be read apart from Shaiva devotion.

name: 宙斯
title: 雷霆与神圣秩序的统治者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 宙斯是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子，奥林波斯诸神的统治者。瑞亚以襁褓中的石头替换婴儿，使他免遭父亲吞食；他在克里特秘密成长，成年后迫使克洛诺斯吐出兄弟姐妹。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 宙斯率兄弟姐妹与泰坦交战，释放独眼巨人与百臂巨人，获得雷霆并赢得统治权。随后他与波塞冬、哈迪斯抽签分掌天空、海洋和冥界。他又击败怪物堤丰；普罗米修斯盗火帮助人类，则招致他以锁链、神鹰与潘多拉实施惩罚。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 雷霆、鹰和橡树是常见标志，雕像多呈蓄须成年男性，持权杖或雷电。鹰既显示高空视野，也强调王权；橡树与多多纳神谕传统密切相关。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奥林匹亚的祭典与竞技以宙斯为中心，多多纳则以神谕闻名。他保护宾客、求援者和誓约，但诗歌中的私情与争执，也揭示神权并非现代道德典范。

en.name: Zeus
en.title: Sovereign of thunder and sacred order

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Zeus is the son of Cronus and Rhea and ruler of the Olympian gods. Rhea saved him from being swallowed by substituting a wrapped stone. Raised secretly on Crete, he eventually made his father release his swallowed brothers and sisters.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Zeus led the younger gods against the Titans, freeing the Cyclopes and Hundred Handers and receiving thunderbolts. After victory, he shared cosmic territories by lot with Poseidon and Hades. He later defeated Typhon. When Prometheus stole fire for humanity, Zeus punished the thief and sent Pandora into the human world.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Thunderbolts, an eagle, and the oak identify Zeus. Artists usually portray a mature bearded ruler carrying a sceptre. The oak particularly recalls Dodona, where divine messages were interpreted through sacred trees.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Zeus received major worship at Olympia and Dodona. He protected guests, suppliants, and binding oaths. His contentious relationships in poetry should be distinguished from cult practice: divine stories explored authority and vulnerability rather than supplying uncomplicated moral examples.

name: 赫拉
title: 婚姻秩序与王后尊荣的维护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 赫拉是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之女，也是宙斯的姐妹与妻子，在奥林波斯拥有王后地位。她与婚姻、合法结合及女性人生阶段有关；阿尔戈斯和萨摩斯的崇拜显示，她绝非只依附丈夫而存在。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 伊娥被宙斯变成母牛后，赫拉令百眼巨人阿耳戈斯看守；赫尔墨斯杀死守卫，她又派牛虻追逐伊娥。赫拉还长期阻挠赫拉克勒斯，使其出生延迟并派蛇袭击婴儿。史诗中的她则支持阿开亚军，与宙斯围绕特洛伊战争激烈角力。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 赫拉常戴高冠、持权杖或石榴，表现庄严王后形象。孔雀与她的关联尤见于后期传统，尾羽的眼状图案被解释为死去阿耳戈斯的百眼。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 萨摩斯赫拉神庙与阿尔戈斯赫拉圣域都是重要祭祀中心。地方仪式重视婚姻与群体身份；文学中的嫉妒形象，不应遮蔽她独立而复杂的宗教地位。

en.name: Hera
en.title: Guardian of marriage and royal dignity

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hera is a daughter of Cronus and Rhea, sister and wife of Zeus, and queen among the Olympians. Her religious concerns include marriage, legitimate unions, and female life transitions. Important sanctuaries at Argos and Samos demonstrate her substantial independent standing.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After Zeus transformed Io into a cow, Hera entrusted her to the many eyed Argus. Hermes killed the guardian, and Hera sent a gadfly to torment Io. She also obstructed Heracles from birth. In the Iliad, her determined support for the Achaeans repeatedly brings her into conflict with Zeus himself.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A high crown, sceptre, and sometimes a pomegranate mark Hera as queen. Later traditions associate her with the peacock, explaining its patterned feathers as the preserved eyes of her dead guardian Argus.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The sanctuaries of Hera at Samos and Argos anchored regional worship and collective identity. Ritual attention to marriage and womanhood differs from literary portrayals of jealousy; those stories should not erase her independent religious authority or local significance.

name: 雅典娜
title: 智慧与城邦的守护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 雅典娜是宙斯之女，赫西俄德说宙斯吞下怀孕的墨提斯，后来她全副武装从父亲头部出生。她兼掌谋略、纺织与城市保护，以处女神身份维护雅典，也帮助英雄完成艰难任务。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 雅典娜与波塞冬竞争雅典的守护权，献出橄榄树，与海神制造的咸水泉形成对照。她指引珀耳修斯借盾面反光斩杀美杜莎，又在《奥德赛》中屡次化身援助奥德修斯和忒勒马科斯，使漂泊的父亲能够返乡并夺回家园。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 头盔、长矛、圆盾与埃癸斯构成武装形象，胸前常见蛇发女妖头像。猫头鹰代表敏锐观察，橄榄树则关联城邦资源；纺织工具提示她的工艺职能。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 泛雅典娜节以游行、竞技和献织袍纪念女神，帕特农神庙彰显城邦权力。她的军事智慧强调策略与纪律，但各地崇拜并不完全等同雅典的政治解释。

en.name: Athena
en.title: Guardian of wisdom, crafts, and the city

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Athena is the daughter of Zeus. In Hesiod, he swallows the pregnant Metis before Athena emerges armed from his head. A virgin goddess of strategy, weaving, and civic protection, she guards Athens while guiding heroes through difficult and dangerous undertakings.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Athena competed with Poseidon for patronage of Athens, offering an olive tree against his saltwater spring. She helped Perseus approach Medusa through a reflected image rather than a fatal direct glance. In the Odyssey, her disguises and advice protect Telemachus and enable Odysseus to recover his household after prolonged wandering.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Her helmet, spear, shield, and aegis distinguish the armed goddess. A Gorgon head often appears on her breast. The owl suggests alert perception, while olive branches and weaving tools express civic prosperity and skill.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Panathenaic festival celebrated Athena through procession, contests, and presentation of a woven robe. The Parthenon linked her to Athenian power. Her wider Greek worship nevertheless included local traditions that cannot be reduced to one city’s political ideology.

name: 阿波罗
title: 预言、音乐与净化之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿波罗是宙斯与勒托之子，阿耳忒弥斯的兄弟，传统称他出生于提洛岛。他关联神谕、乐艺、弓箭及疫病与疗愈；古希腊的太阳神原本是赫利俄斯，两者的认同主要见于后期发展。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿波罗在德尔斐杀死巨蛇皮同，建立著名的神谕中心，女祭司皮提亚传达他的启示。《伊利亚特》开篇，他因祭司受辱而向阿开亚军营射下瘟疫。另一故事中，他追逐达芙涅，少女化为月桂，他遂将月桂作为自己的标志。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 里拉琴、弓箭和月桂冠最易识别阿波罗，雕像常呈无须青年。乌鸦、海豚和三足鼎也与他有关，其中三足鼎尤其指向德尔斐神谕的祭祀环境。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 德尔斐神谕参与殖民、战争与净化事务，皮提亚赛会兼有音乐和竞技。阿波罗并非单纯温和的艺术神；准确的弓箭与瘟疫同样体现其可怖权能。

en.name: Apollo
en.title: God of prophecy, music, and purification

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Apollo is the son of Zeus and Leto and brother of Artemis, traditionally born on Delos. He governs prophecy, music, archery, disease, and healing. Helios was originally the distinct Greek sun god; stronger identification between the two developed in later traditions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Apollo killed the serpent Python at Delphi and established the sanctuary where the Pythia delivered divine responses. At the opening of the Iliad, he sends plague against the Achaean camp after his priest is dishonoured. Another story describes his pursuit of Daphne, whose transformation into laurel ends her attempted escape.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A lyre, bow, and laurel wreath identify Apollo, normally shown as a youthful, beardless figure. Ravens, dolphins, and the tripod also belong to his imagery, with the tripod particularly recalling Delphic divination.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Delphi advised communities about colonisation, conflict, and ritual purification. Its Pythian festival included musical and athletic competition. Apollo should not be reduced to gentle artistic inspiration: his precise arrows and power over plague make him an equally formidable presence.

name: 阿耳忒弥斯
title: 荒野、狩猎与成长边界的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿耳忒弥斯是宙斯与勒托之女，阿波罗的姐妹，常作为拒绝婚姻的处女猎神出现。她保护野生动物，又能将其猎杀，并关注少女成长和分娩；她与月亮的认同不能取代早期独立的塞勒涅。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿克泰翁意外看见阿耳忒弥斯沐浴，遭她变成鹿，最终被自己的猎犬撕裂。尼俄柏夸耀子女众多、轻视勒托，阿耳忒弥斯与阿波罗便射杀她的儿女。伊菲革涅亚的故事则存在献祭与被女神以鹿替换、迁往陶里斯的不同结局。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 短衣、弓箭、箭囊和鹿表现她的荒野行动力，身旁也可能出现猎犬。以弗所的阿耳忒弥斯具有特殊地方造型，不宜直接按希腊少女猎神解释。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 布劳伦的少女仪式将她与成长和群体过渡联系起来，以弗所神庙则展现另一套地方传统。她既守护生命边界也施加死亡，体现荒野的双重力量。

en.name: Artemis
en.title: Goddess of wilderness, hunting, and transitions

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Artemis is the daughter of Zeus and Leto and sister of Apollo. A virgin huntress, she both protects and kills wild animals, and oversees girls approaching adulthood and childbirth. Her later lunar associations should not obscure the originally distinct moon goddess Selene.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When Actaeon saw Artemis bathing, she transformed him into a stag, and his own hunting dogs destroyed him. She and Apollo also killed Niobe’s children after their mother insulted Leto. Stories of Iphigenia differ: some describe sacrifice, while others let Artemis substitute a deer and transport the girl to Tauris.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A short hunting dress, bow, quiver, deer, and hounds express her mobility outside settled society. The distinctive cult image of Artemis at Ephesus belongs to a local tradition rather than simply reproducing this huntress.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Rituals at Brauron connected Artemis with girls and transitions toward adulthood. Her Ephesian sanctuary expressed a different regional identity. Protection and sudden death coexist in her character, reflecting the dangerous boundaries between human settlement, bodily change, and wild nature.

name: 波塞冬
title: 海洋、地震与马匹的驾驭者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 波塞冬是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子，宙斯及哈迪斯的兄弟。泰坦战争后，他抽签获得海洋领域，但其权能并不限于海水：古老称号撼地者和与马匹相关的崇拜，显示其跨越陆海的力量。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 奥德修斯刺瞎独眼巨人波吕斐摩斯后，波塞冬应儿子的请求阻挠英雄归航，以风暴和海难延长其漂泊。他与雅典娜争夺雅典时击出咸水泉；在特洛伊传说中，他曾修筑城墙，却因拉俄墨冬拒付报酬而派海怪惩罚当地。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 三叉戟是最鲜明的标志，常与蓄须男性、海豚和海马共同出现。他也驾驭马拉战车；马的意象提醒观者，海神并不是仅有航海职能的神祇。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 科林斯地峡赛会奉献给波塞冬，苏尼翁海岬的神庙连接航路与城邦景观。航海者祈求其平息波涛，地震频发的希腊社会也敬畏他的撼地能力。

en.name: Poseidon
en.title: Lord of seas, earthquakes, and horses

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Poseidon is a son of Cronus and Rhea and brother of Zeus and Hades. After the Titan war he received the sea by lot. His ancient title Earth Shaker and strong associations with horses reveal powers extending far beyond maritime travel.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After Odysseus blinded the Cyclops Polyphemus, Poseidon answered his son’s appeal by obstructing the hero’s return with storms and shipwreck. He competed with Athena for Athens by striking a saltwater spring. At Troy, he helped build the walls, then sent a sea monster when King Laomedon withheld the promised payment.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The trident identifies Poseidon, often represented as a mature bearded man accompanied by dolphins or sea horses. Horse drawn chariots also appear, recalling an important dimension of his power beyond the open sea.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Isthmian Games near Corinth honoured Poseidon, while his sanctuary at Sounion overlooked major sea routes. Sailors sought calm passages, but communities exposed to earthquakes also feared him. Maritime protection and destructive instability remained inseparable aspects of his worship.

name: 哈迪斯
title: 冥界与地下财富的君主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 哈迪斯是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子，在兄弟分掌宇宙时获得地下亡者领域。他并非死亡本身的化身塔纳托斯，也不是邪恶魔王；普路同这一称号强调地下矿产与农业生长所含的财富。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《得墨忒耳颂》叙述哈迪斯经宙斯同意带走珀耳塞福涅，引发得墨忒耳停止谷物生长。他让少女吃下石榴籽，使她必须定期返回冥界。俄耳甫斯以音乐求回欧律狄刻时，他允许亡妻随行，却规定出境之前不可回头观看。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 权杖、双齿叉、丰饶角与守门犬刻耳柏洛斯常见于其图像。隐形头盔出现在英雄故事中；严肃的王座形象，比近代流行的恶魔造型更合古代传统。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 希腊人常以委婉称号称呼冥界之主，部分祭祀与大地和丰饶相连。有关来世的观念因时代、地域和秘仪而异，不能拼成一套始终统一的冥界教义。

en.name: Hades
en.title: Ruler of the dead and underground wealth

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hades is a son of Cronus and Rhea who received the realm of the dead when the brothers divided cosmic territories. He is distinct from Thanatos, personified death, and is not a devil. His title Plouton emphasises wealth hidden beneath the earth.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, Hades takes Persephone with Zeus’s approval, provoking her mother to suspend agricultural growth. Pomegranate seeds bind Persephone to recurring residence below. When Orpheus seeks Eurydice, the underworld rulers permit her return on the condition that he does not look back before reaching the surface.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A sceptre, two pronged staff, cornucopia, and the watchdog Cerberus accompany Hades. His helmet grants invisibility in heroic narratives. Ancient images usually present a solemn enthroned king rather than a demonic adversary.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Greeks often used respectful or euphemistic names for the underworld ruler. Some cult contexts connected him with earth and abundance. Beliefs about the dead differed across periods, places, and mystery traditions, rather than forming one universally fixed ancient doctrine.

name: 阿佛洛狄忒
title: 欲望、魅力与结合的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿佛洛狄忒的身世有不同谱系：赫西俄德称她从乌拉诺斯被割下的生殖器所激起的海沫诞生，荷马则称她为宙斯与狄俄涅之女。她掌管吸引、性欲和结合，且在部分城市拥有武装形态。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 特洛伊王子帕里斯评判三位女神的美貌时，阿佛洛狄忒许诺让他得到海伦，从而赢得金苹果，并卷入战争起源。她与凡人安喀塞斯结合，生下埃涅阿斯；在阿多尼斯故事中，她哀悼青年猎人的死亡，使爱情与失落紧密相连。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 鸽子、桃金娘、玫瑰和海中贝壳构成常见意象，厄洛斯常随侍其旁。裸体或出浴形象在古典后期尤为著名，但早期与地方神像也可着衣甚至持械。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 塞浦路斯帕福斯和基西拉是重要崇拜地点，显示她与海上交流的联系。其近东关联值得比较，但不能简单认作异名；古代所谓圣娼制度也须谨慎考证。

en.name: Aphrodite
en.title: Goddess of desire, attraction, and union

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Aphrodite has differing genealogies. Hesiod makes her arise from sea foam surrounding the severed genitals of Uranus; Homer calls her the daughter of Zeus and Dione. She governs attraction, sexuality, and union, while some communities also honoured her in armed forms.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: During the judgement of Paris, Aphrodite promised the Trojan prince Helen and won the golden apple, helping set the Trojan conflict in motion. Her union with the mortal Anchises produced Aeneas. In traditions concerning Adonis, her grief for the young hunter connects erotic attachment with vulnerability, mourning, and irreversible loss.
