sections.text: Sky associations, landscape-forming journeys, and particular local human images provide public points of recognition. An outstretched figure at one site is not a standardized portrait endorsed by all communities. Public visibility or reproduction in a book also does not automatically permit further copying or commercial use.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Colonial records often translated Baiame as creator or heavenly father, potentially importing European religious assumptions. This entry summarizes publicly shared connections between ancestry and Country without describing restricted occasions. Understanding a local narrative should prioritize explanations that the relevant Traditional Owners have chosen to make public.

name: 达拉穆伦
title: 尤因等东南部传统中的祖先人物

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 达拉穆伦见于尤因及澳大利亚东南部若干族群的公开记述，名字存在多种拼写。部分资料将他与拜阿米联系，另一些突出其自身祖先权威。这些说法不能合成全澳共同谱系，也不意味着不同语言族群共享完全相同的叙事权限。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 公开尤因概述把达拉穆伦描述为曾在地上活动、与生活秩序相连，后来居于天空的祖先。其他地方记述把他放在拜阿米的后代位置。这里保留两种公开叙述的差别，不把它们强接为父子历险，也不复述与受限传授有关的器物、声音或仪式情节。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 独腿形象出现在某些公开释义和图像讨论中，但并不是可移用于所有地区的定式。名字译义、岩刻识别和身体特征的解释，都必须带着具体语言及地点背景。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 早期人类学文本常越过今天强调的知识边界，因此已经出版不等于适合再次传播。学习可从族群所在地、公开祖先观和殖民记述差异入手；进一步内容应以相关共同体主动公开和授权为准。

en.name: Daramulum
en.title: Ancestral figure in Yuin and other southeastern traditions

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Daramulum appears under several spellings in public accounts concerning Yuin and other southeastern Australian peoples. Some sources connect him genealogically with Baiame; others emphasize his own ancestral authority. These accounts cannot be assembled into a universal Australian family tree or assumed to share identical permissions for transmission.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Public Yuin summaries describe Daramulum as an ancestor who acted on earth, was associated with social order, and later dwelt in the sky. Other regional accounts position him as Baiame’s offspring. This entry preserves that difference without inventing joint adventures or repeating restricted objects, sounds, or ceremonial episodes.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: A one-legged appearance occurs in some public interpretations and discussions of images, but it is not a template transferable to every region. Translations of his name, identification of engravings, and explanations of bodily features require their particular language and place contexts rather than generalized visual certainty.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Early anthropological publications sometimes crossed boundaries now explicitly recognized by communities, so previous publication does not guarantee appropriate republication. Learning can begin with regional geography, publicly shared ancestral concepts, and differences in colonial records. Further content should depend on what relevant communities actively choose to share and authorize.

name: 公开虹蛇母题
title: 不同族群水域祖先形象的比较标签

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 虹蛇是英语和中文中常用的比较标签，不是一位全澳统一神祇的本名。公开材料可分别讨论西南澳努恩加尔的瓦吉尔，以及西阿纳姆地昆温库等传统中的恩加约德；两者拥有各自的土地、语言与传统守护者，不能视作同一人。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 努恩加尔公开叙事把瓦吉尔在大地上的移动与德巴尔耶里根即天鹅河等水道的形成联系起来。西阿纳姆地的公开介绍则常把恩加约德与水洼、雨水和生命的生成相连。这里并列具体母题，而不把两地故事拼成一次横跨大陆的旅行或共同创世战争。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 蛇形身体、水道与雨季联系是常见线索；角、混合动物特征或色彩会因传统而变。彩虹条纹并非必备外貌，任意蛇形图案也不能未经语境确认就称为虹蛇。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 学校与博物馆常用虹蛇帮助入门，却容易掩盖族群差异。公开艺术也不自动开放所有故事层次；辨识图像应保留艺术家、语言群及土地来源，并尊重水域和相关地点的访问边界。

en.name: Public Rainbow Serpent Motifs
en.title: A comparative label for distinct water-related ancestors

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Rainbow Serpent is a comparative English label, not the personal name of one deity shared throughout Australia. Public examples include the Noongar Wagyl in the southwest and Ngalyod in Kunwinjku and related western Arnhem Land traditions. Each belongs to particular languages, places, and custodians rather than a single merged identity.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Public Noongar accounts link Wagyl’s movements with the formation of waterways including Derbarl Yerrigan, the Swan River. Public western Arnhem Land interpretation connects Ngalyod with waterholes, rain, and generating life. These are distinct narrative settings, not episodes in an invented continent-wide journey or a common creation war.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Serpentine bodies, waterways, and seasonal rain are recurring clues, while horns, composite animal features, and colors differ by tradition. Rainbow stripes are not a required appearance. An arbitrary snake design cannot be identified as a Rainbow Serpent without provenance and an appropriate community explanation.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Schools and museums often use Rainbow Serpent as an introductory category, sometimes obscuring differences among peoples. Public artwork does not automatically reveal every level of its associated story. Interpretation should preserve artist, language-group, and Country information and respect access boundaries around water places and other significant sites.

name: 尤隆古尔
title: 尤尔恩古传统中具地方归属的水蛇祖先

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 尤隆古尔亦有尤尔隆古尔等转写，见于澳大利亚东北阿纳姆地尤尔恩古传统的公开记述。早期文献可能沿用穆尔恩金等旧称。他属于具体氏族、土地与祖先关系，不能把名字当成所有虹蛇的通称，性别称谓也不宜一概固定。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 公开博物馆与文化介绍常把尤隆古尔与瓦吉拉格姐妹的祖先旅程联系起来，突出水边停留及强大水中存在所具有的力量。不同讲述牵涉特定地点和氏族权属，因此这里只说明公开叙事框架，不重演吞食、再生等更详细情节，也不据旧采录推补受限内容。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 巨蛇、水洼、季雨及雷鸣是公开资料中常见关联。画面上的线条与图案可能承载氏族知识，不能将其拆成任意装饰，也不能仅凭蛇形就断言作品描绘此祖先。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 尤尔恩古艺术中心与博物馆公开说明可提供艺术家、氏族和土地背景，但授权范围因作品而异。可学习公开的水域生态与祖先关系；公开展出不等于允许复制氏族设计，更不等于取得完整叙事的传授资格。

en.name: Julunggul
en.title: A locally grounded water-serpent ancestor in Yolngu traditions

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Julunggul, also rendered Yurlunggur and through other spellings, appears in public accounts of Yolngu traditions in northeastern Arnhem Land. Older publications may use labels such as Murngin. The ancestor belongs within particular clan, Country, and ancestral relationships, not as a generic name for every Rainbow Serpent or a universally gendered deity.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Public museum and cultural introductions connect Julunggul with the ancestral travels of the Wagilag sisters and powerful encounters at water places. Accounts involve specific locations and clan authority. This entry gives that public framework without reenacting detailed swallowing or renewal episodes, or using old collections to reconstruct restricted knowledge.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: A great serpent, waterholes, seasonal rain, and thunder recur in public descriptions. Particular lines and designs in artworks may carry clan knowledge and are not freely detachable ornaments. A snake-shaped image alone cannot establish that an artwork depicts this ancestor rather than another locally identified being.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Public interpretation from Yolngu art centers and museums can supply artist, clan, and Country information, with permissions varying by work. Learning can focus on openly shared water ecology and ancestral relationships. Public exhibition does not authorize copying clan designs or confer the right to receive or retell an entire narrative.

name: 胡纳胡纳赫普
title: 基切英雄双子的父亲与冥界球手

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 胡纳胡纳赫普是基切玛雅《波波尔乌》中的球手，名字常译为一胡纳赫普。他与兄弟七胡纳赫普同赴冥界，也是英雄双子胡纳赫普和伊什巴兰克的父亲，不应与同名成分的儿子混淆。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 兄弟在地面打球的声音惊动西巴尔巴诸主，被召入冥界后未能识破考验，遭到杀害。胡纳胡纳赫普的头悬在葫芦树上，使原本不结果的树结满果实。少女伊什基克来到树前，头颅向她掌心吐出唾液，使她怀上双子，故事由此转入下一代对冥界的挑战。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 球场、悬首与结果的树构成主要辨识线索，连结死亡、繁衍和代际延续。他与玉米神的联系是研究议题，不能据此把所有古典玛雅玉米神图像都直接命名为他。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 这一叙事见于殖民时期以拉丁字母记录的基切文本，保留更早的口传传统。应区分基切叙事与其他玛雅社群的不同传统，不把一部作品当作所有玛雅人的统一经典。

en.name: Hun Hunahpu
en.title: Father of the K’iche’ hero twins and an underworld ballplayer

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hun Hunahpu, often translated as One Hunahpu, is a ballplayer in the K’iche’ Maya Popol Wuj. He accompanies his brother Seven Hunahpu to the underworld and fathers Hunahpu and Xbalanque. His name must not be confused with that of his heroic son.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Their ballplaying disturbs the lords of Xibalba, who summon and kill the brothers after failed trials. Hun Hunahpu’s severed head hangs in a calabash tree that becomes fruitful. When Xquic approaches, the head spits into her palm, beginning her pregnancy with the twins.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The ballcourt, severed head, and fruiting tree connect death with generation and continuity. Scholars discuss relationships between this character and maize divinities, but such comparisons do not justify identifying every Classic Maya image of a maize god as Hun Hunahpu.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: His story survives in a K’iche’ text written with the Latin alphabet during the colonial period, preserving earlier oral traditions. This particular literary witness should not be treated as a single uniform scripture representing every Maya community or historical period.

name: 七金刚鹦鹉
title: 以珠玉光辉自比日月的傲慢巨鸟

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 七金刚鹦鹉的基切语名为武库布卡基什，是《波波尔乌》中夸耀自身光辉的巨鸟。他在真正的日月显现之前，凭明亮的眼睛和珠玉牙齿自称太阳与月亮，却并非创造天地的神圣者。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 胡纳赫普与伊什巴兰克用吹箭射中巨鸟的下颌，巨鸟反扯下胡纳赫普的手臂。双子随后请两位老人假扮医者，谎称能够医治牙痛，拔去巨鸟的珠玉牙齿并以白玉米粒替换，又取走他的眼部珍宝。失去所夸耀的光辉后，巨鸟死去，双子也取回被夺的手臂。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 耀眼牙齿、发光眼睛和栖息果树的巨鸟形象最具辨识度。其光芒依赖可被取走的饰物，叙事借此区分炫耀的权势与正当秩序，而不是贬低现实中的金刚鹦鹉。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 故事属于基切玛雅传统，并与巨鸟两个儿子的败亡相互呼应。古代玛雅鸟形图像与此角色的对应仍需具体论证，不能仅凭鸟形或华丽羽毛就断言属于同一人物。

en.name: Vucub Caquix
en.title: Seven Macaw, the bird who claims the light of sun and moon

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Vucub Caquix, commonly called Seven Macaw, is the boastful great bird of the K’iche’ Popol Wuj. Before the true sun and moon appear, he claims their status through his shining eyes and jeweled teeth. He is not the creator of the world.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Hunahpu wounds his jaw with a blowgun, but the bird tears off the hero’s arm. Two elderly helpers then pose as healers. They replace his splendid teeth with white maize and remove his eye ornaments. Deprived of his brilliance, he dies; the arm is recovered.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Jeweled teeth, brilliant eyes, and a great bird perched in a fruit tree distinguish him. His removable splendor exposes the fragility of boastful authority. This narrative function concerns a particular character and is not a condemnation of actual macaws or their beauty.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The episode belongs specifically to K’iche’ Maya narrative and accompanies the downfall of the bird’s two sons. Proposed connections with ancient Maya bird imagery require careful argument; a magnificent bird or elaborate plumage alone cannot establish the identity of this literary character.

name: 希佩托特克
title: 与更新、剥皮祭仪及工匠相关的神祇

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 希佩托特克的纳瓦特尔语名常译为我们的剥皮之主，是墨西加宗教中与农作更新及金工等领域相关的神祇。他的崇拜也见于中部墨西哥其他地区，不能简单视为只属于特诺奇蒂特兰的地方神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 关于他的资料尤其集中于仪式而非连续的英雄传记。在特拉卡希佩瓦利斯特利节期间，俘虏被献祭，一些仪式参与者随后披上受祭者皮肤，经过规定时段再将其脱下保存。资料也记载战士参与的格斗式祭仪，展现战争、献祭与季节更新彼此交织的宗教秩序。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 造像常以外覆的人皮和下垂的皮手形成双层身体效果，也可能持仪式杖。辨识重点是服饰结构与祭仪语境，而非把黄色、金属或任何剥皮图像都等同于此神。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 认识此神需对读考古造像、图绘文献与殖民时期记载，注意记录者的立场。介绍历史献祭应准确而不猎奇，也不应把古代仪式直接投射为今日原住民社群的实践。

en.name: Xipe Totec
en.title: Our Lord the Flayed One, associated with renewal and skilled work

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Xipe Totec’s Nahuatl name is commonly rendered Our Lord the Flayed One. In Mexica religion he is associated with agricultural renewal and fields including metalworking. His worship also occurred elsewhere in central Mexico, so he should not be reduced to a purely Tenochtitlan deity.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Evidence emphasizes ceremonies rather than a continuous heroic biography. During Tlacaxipehualiztli, captives were sacrificed and some participants wore the victims’ skins for a prescribed period before removing and depositing them. Accounts also describe staged combat sacrifices, connecting warfare, ritual transformation, and seasonal renewal.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Sculptures often show an outer human skin, with its dangling hands creating a doubled bodily appearance. An accompanying ritual staff may add context. Identification depends on this structured attire and setting, not on treating every yellow object or skin motif as his emblem.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Understanding Xipe Totec requires comparison of archaeological objects, painted manuscripts, and colonial accounts, including their authors’ perspectives. Historical sacrifice should be described accurately without sensationalism. Ancient ceremonial evidence must not be projected indiscriminately onto the practices or identities of present Indigenous communities.

name: 索奇克察尔
title: 花卉、爱欲与精巧织作的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 索奇克察尔是中部墨西哥纳瓦传统中与花卉、爱欲、美丽及织作相关的女神，名字通常释为珍贵的花羽。她在墨西加宗教中受到敬奉，但不同文献对她的亲属关系和经历并没有完全一致的说法。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 部分殖民时期记述把她说成雨神特拉洛克的妻子，后来被特斯卡特利波卡带走。这是一条特定文献线索，不能整理成所有纳瓦社群共同认可的婚姻传记。围绕她的其他材料更重视花卉、性吸引力与女性织作，说明她在仪式和日常技艺中具有多重意义。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 花朵、华丽羽饰与精美衣物是常见辨识线索，呈现繁盛、吸引力和制作技艺。她不能与名称相近的花之王索奇皮利混为一体，也不能只用现代爱情女神的标签概括。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 她的形象保存在中部墨西哥图绘文献及殖民时期宗教记录中。阐释时应区分纳瓦地方传统与现代艺术再创作，避免把爱欲、劳动和生育等不同关联压缩为单一职能。

en.name: Xochiquetzal
en.title: Goddess associated with flowers, desire, and fine weaving

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Xochiquetzal belongs to central Mexican Nahua traditions and is associated with flowers, sexual desire, beauty, and weaving. Her name evokes a precious flower or flower feather. Mexica worship is well attested, but surviving accounts do not present one consistent family history for her.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Some colonial accounts describe her as Tlaloc’s wife before Tezcatlipoca takes her away. This is a particular textual tradition, not a universally accepted Nahua biography. Other evidence emphasizes flowers, attraction, and women’s textile skills, placing her significance within ritual life as well as accomplished work.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Flowers, elaborate feather ornaments, and fine clothing provide important identifying clues, bringing together abundance, attractiveness, and skilled manufacture. She should not be conflated with the similarly named Xochipilli, nor reduced to a modern category of a goddess concerned only with romantic love.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Central Mexican pictorial manuscripts and colonial religious descriptions preserve her imagery and associations. Interpretation should distinguish particular Nahua traditions from contemporary artistic reinvention. Desire, skilled labor, fertility, and beauty intersect in these materials without collapsing into a single exclusive divine function.

name: 伊利亚帕
title: 安第斯雷鸣、闪电与降雨的神圣力量

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊利亚帕是印加宗教中与雷鸣、闪电及降雨紧密相连的神圣存在，其名也用于雷电现象。雨水关系高地农作与牧养，使他在帝国祭祀中具有重要地位，并与安第斯各地的天气信仰相互联系。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 殖民时期记录保存了一种解释雷雨的叙述：天上的少女持盛水容器，她的兄弟击碎容器，水便降为雨。有关伊利亚帕的描写又常将雷声比作投石索发射时的巨响。这些材料共同呈现雷电与降水的关联，但不同作者的记录不宜拼成细节完全统一的故事。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 投石索、雷光与盛水器是介绍相关叙事时常用的线索，突出雷声和降雨的联系。天象名称、神圣人格与地方祭祀对象之间存在重叠，不能只按现代雷神类别理解。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 关于他的资料主要来自殖民时期的安第斯宗教记述，须与地方历史共同阅读。今日安第斯社群的天气观念仍有丰富差异，不应将帝国祭祀直接当作现代社群的统一信条。

en.name: Illapa
en.title: Andean sacred power of thunder, lightning, and rain

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Illapa is a sacred presence associated with thunder, lightning, and rain in Inca religion; the name also denotes thunderous weather. Rain sustained highland farming and herding, giving this power considerable ceremonial importance while connecting imperial worship with diverse regional Andean understandings of weather.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Colonial accounts preserve a rain explanation in which a heavenly maiden holds a water vessel and her brother strikes it, releasing rain. Descriptions associated with Illapa also compare thunder to a sling’s report. These related records should not be fused into one perfectly standardized biography.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The sling, lightning, and water vessel are useful clues to these traditions, emphasizing the relationship between thunder and rainfall. Weather terminology, divine personhood, and local objects of worship can overlap. A modern classification as merely a thunder god obscures that complexity.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Much evidence comes from colonial descriptions of Andean religion and requires attention to local histories and the circumstances of recording. Living Andean communities maintain varied understandings of weather; imperial Inca ceremonial patterns cannot simply be presented as their uniform contemporary beliefs.

name: 玛玛科查
title: 作为滋养之母受到敬奉的海洋

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 玛玛科查的克丘亚语名常释为海洋之母，是安第斯宗教语境中对海的母性称谓与神圣人格表达。在印加统治及其记录范围内，她尤其关联海洋的滋养力量，不能因此抹去沿海各族自己的海洋传统。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 殖民时期的安第斯记述把海描述为鱼类的母亲，也记录沿海居民向海致敬和献供，以求渔获与航行平安。有关玛玛科查的材料主要呈现人、海与生计之间的互惠关系，而不是一套情节完整的英雄冒险；不宜为填补人物传记而另造她与海怪交战的故事。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 海水、鱼群与海岸是最稳妥的主题线索，突出养育及水域力量。现存材料不足以规定一种通行的古代女神面貌，现代蓝衣持杖画像不应被说成统一的印加标准形象。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 应区分印加帝国对神圣水域的理解与不同沿海社群的地方实践。海洋崇敬也不等同于所有安第斯水域信仰；介绍今日传统时，须尊重社群自身使用的名称和解释。

en.name: Mama Cocha
en.title: The sea honored as a nourishing mother

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Mama Cocha is a Quechua designation commonly understood as Mother Sea, expressing the ocean’s maternal sacred presence. Within accounts of the Inca world, she represents nourishing marine power. This imperial framing should not erase the distinct sea traditions of the many peoples along the coast.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Colonial Andean descriptions call the sea the mother of fish and record coastal offerings seeking catches and safe passage. Such evidence concerns reciprocal relationships among people, ocean, and livelihood rather than a complete heroic biography. Invented adventures against sea monsters would misrepresent the surviving material.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Seawater, fish, and the coastline provide the most secure thematic clues to nourishment and marine power. Surviving evidence does not establish one standard ancient portrait. Modern pictures of a woman in blue carrying a staff should not be presented as canonical Inca iconography.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Imperial Inca perspectives on sacred waters must be distinguished from the practices of particular coastal communities. Reverence for the ocean is not interchangeable with every Andean water tradition. Contemporary descriptions should respect the names, histories, and interpretations maintained by the communities concerned.

name: 奥雅
title: 与尼日尔河、风暴及转变相联的奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥雅是约鲁巴活态宗教中的奥里沙，与尼日尔河及风暴力量关系密切。关于她与尚戈及其他奥里沙的亲属、婚姻叙述因地域而异，她并非仅作为男性神祇的配偶而存在，也有独立的祭祀传统。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一组公开流传的故事说，猎人发现能脱下兽皮化为女子的水牛，藏起兽皮后与她成婚，并答应不泄露她的来历。秘密后来被家人揭破，她取回兽皮恢复水牛形态。这个故事把奥雅的家庭关系、威力与变形联系起来，但人物细节和结局随讲述版本变化。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 强风、尼日尔河与水牛是常见关联，体现流动与突变。她与墓地入口的关系在部分传统及大西洋彼岸传承中突出，不能因此把她简单等同于统治全部死者的死神。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奥雅在尼日利亚及美洲非洲裔宗教中仍受敬奉，不同传承有各自名称、仪式和解释。公开神话只是认识她的一个入口，不能替代社群授权的宗教教导或仪式资格。

en.name: Oya
en.title: Orisha associated with the Niger, storms, and transformation

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Oya is an orisha in living Yoruba religion, closely associated with the Niger River and powerful winds. Accounts of her relationships with Shango and other orishas vary regionally. She possesses religious significance and worship beyond any description of her as a male deity’s wife.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In a publicly circulated story cycle, a hunter hides the skin of a buffalo who becomes a woman. They marry under a promise of secrecy. After relatives expose her origins, she recovers the skin and resumes buffalo form. Details and endings vary between tellings.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Strong winds, the Niger, and the buffalo convey movement and sudden transformation. Connections with cemetery entrances are prominent in some traditions, including Atlantic diaspora religions. Those associations should not turn her into a generic death goddess ruling all the dead everywhere.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Oya remains actively honored in Nigeria and African diaspora religions, whose lineages maintain distinct names, ceremonies, and interpretations. Public narratives offer one approach to understanding her; they do not confer ritual authority or replace religious teaching authorized by the communities that sustain these traditions.

name: 奥伦米拉
title: 智慧、命运见证与伊法传统的奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥伦米拉是约鲁巴宗教中与智慧及伊法占卜传统相联的奥里沙，常被称为命运的见证者。他的知识帮助人们理解选择、责任与处境，但不能把他简化为自动预报未来的神，或等同于至高创造者。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一组公开传说讲述奥伦米拉因儿子拒绝表达应有的敬意而离开人间，失去指导的人们陷入困境。子女寻访并请求他归来，他则留下与棕榈果仁相关的求知方式，使人们仍能寻求指引。故事将伊法的由来与关系修复相连，各传承保存的具体情节有所不同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 伊法使用的棕榈果仁、占卜链与占卜盘是重要关联物，二百五十六种奥杜构成知识分类框架。器物并非随意摆设，公开介绍不等于提供具体仪式程序或授予占卜资格。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊法依靠受训传承者保存和解释庞大的诗句与故事，不只是一套符号算法。尼日利亚与大西洋彼岸社群各有历史脉络，相关知识应尊重传承者和当地宗教规范。

en.name: Orunmila
en.title: Orisha of wisdom, destiny’s witness, and the Ifa tradition

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Orunmila is the Yoruba orisha associated with wisdom and the Ifa divination tradition, often described as a witness to destiny. His knowledge helps people interpret circumstances, choices, and responsibilities. He is neither simply an automatic predictor of events nor identical with the supreme creator.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: One public narrative cycle describes Orunmila leaving the human world after a son refuses proper respect. Without guidance, people suffer. His children seek him and request his return; he instead leaves a means associated with palm nuts for obtaining counsel. Particular versions preserve different details.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Ifa palm nuts, a divining chain, and the divination tray are important associations. Its 256 odu organize a substantial body of knowledge. These objects are not arbitrary decorations, and public description neither supplies ceremonial instructions nor authorizes someone to practice divination.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Trained custodians preserve and interpret extensive verses and stories within Ifa; the tradition is more than a symbolic calculation system. Communities in Nigeria and across the Atlantic possess distinct histories. Their religious standards and the authority of knowledgeable practitioners deserve explicit respect.

name: 奥尼尼
title: 阿坎阿南西购得故事传说中的蟒蛇

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥尼尼是阿坎阿南西故事中的一条蟒蛇，出现在蜘蛛智者向天神尼亚美换取故事的叙事里。他是这个具体情节中的动物角色，不是统辖蛇类的神祇，也不是可以套用于整个西非的通用神名。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 尼亚美要求阿南西取得难以捕获的动物，才肯交出故事。阿南西带着长木杆找到奥尼尼，假称自己正与妻子争论蟒蛇究竟比木杆长还是短。奥尼尼为证明长度而伸直身体，阿南西借口身体必须贴紧木杆才能量准，一段段把他绑牢，随后把活捉的蟒蛇交给尼亚美。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 长木杆、绳索与伸直的蛇身是这段故事的辨识组合，关键在于把自证身长的愿望变成圈套。奥尼尼的失败服务于机智叙事，不代表阿坎社会把所有蛇都视为愚笨。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 故事属于阿坎语言文化中的阿南西叙事群，经口传和书面改写形成多种版本。应保留其阿坎背景，并把角色名称与具体情节相连，不泛称为所有西非民族共同的蟒蛇神。

en.name: Onini
en.title: The python in the Akan tale of Ananse acquiring stories

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Onini is the python in an Akan Ananse tale about obtaining stories from the sky deity Nyame. He is an animal character within that particular narrative, not a god governing snakes and not a universal supernatural figure shared by all West African peoples.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Nyame demands difficult animal captives as the price of stories. Ananse approaches Onini with a pole, claiming a dispute with his wife over the python’s length. Onini stretches alongside it; Ananse insists accurate measurement requires fastening him tightly, binds him, and delivers the captive.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The long pole, binding cord, and straightened snake together identify this episode. A desire to establish bodily size becomes the opening for a trap. Onini’s defeat advances a tale about ingenuity; it does not establish an Akan judgment that all snakes lack intelligence.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The episode belongs to Akan Ananse storytelling and circulates through oral performance and written adaptations with variable wording. Its Akan setting and specific narrative role should remain visible. Labeling Onini a python god common to all West Africa would erase those essential distinctions.

name: 姆莫博罗
title: 被阿南西诱入葫芦的阿坎故事黄蜂群

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 姆莫博罗是阿坎阿南西购得故事传说中的黄蜂群名称，并非一位有独立神庙或神职的黄蜂神。他们与蟒蛇奥尼尼等动物一起，构成尼亚美向阿南西提出的难题，角色身份必须依附具体故事说明。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿南西准备葫芦容器和水，在黄蜂栖处洒水，自己也装作被雨淋湿，宣称暴雨已经来临。他向黄蜂推荐葫芦作为干燥的避难处，黄蜂群便陆续飞入。阿南西随即堵住开口，把整群黄蜂送给尼亚美；这次捕获成为换取故事的条件之一，计谋依靠伪造的天气与虚假的庇护。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 装水器具、避雨的葫芦与被封住的出口构成主要线索。黄蜂原本具有群体防御力量，却被保护承诺诱入困境，故事着重机智的反转，而不是描述真实的养蜂技术。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 不同阿坎讲述及英语改写对名称拼法和细节有所调整，但黄蜂群的故事身份仍应保留。这里采用黄蜂而非泛称蜂神，也不把阿南西叙事中的所有动物自动提升为神祇。

en.name: Mmoboro
en.title: The hornets tricked into a gourd in an Akan Ananse tale

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Mmoboro names the hornets in the Akan tale of Ananse acquiring stories from Nyame. They are a swarm of story animals, not a hornet deity with an independent cult. Together with Onini and other captives, they belong to the sky deity’s demanding conditions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Ananse brings water and a gourd, sprinkles the hornets’ dwelling, and pretends that heavy rain has arrived. He recommends the gourd as dry shelter. Once the hornets enter, he plugs the opening and carries them to Nyame as part of the payment for stories.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Water, the sheltering gourd, and its stopped opening identify the trick. A swarm capable of collective defense becomes vulnerable through a promise of protection. The reversal serves storytelling about resourcefulness and deception; it is not a practical description of actual beekeeping or hornet management.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Akan performances and English adaptations vary in spelling and narrative detail, but the hornets’ particular role should remain clear. Calling them a generic bee god would change both animal identity and cultural status. Not every creature appearing beside Ananse is therefore a deity.

name: 塔菲里马泰阿
title: 毛利传统中风与风暴的阿图阿

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 塔菲里马泰阿是毛利传统中与风、云和风暴有关的阿图阿，为天空父亲朗伊努伊与大地母亲帕帕图阿努库之子。他反对兄弟分开父母，公开叙事由此解释天气力量与其他自然领域之间的冲突。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 塔内把天地分开后，塔菲里马泰阿随父亲来到天上，召集风暴向兄弟进攻。他摧折塔内的森林，搅动坦加罗阿的海域；与栽培食物及野生食物相关的兄弟躲入大地母亲怀中。只有图马陶恩加坚持迎战，故事借这场冲突说明人类与风暴及其他生命之间的关系。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 狂风、云层和暴雨是主要辨识线索，其力量贯穿天空、森林与海面。他不是整个波利尼西亚共同采用同名同貌的风神，毛利阿图阿的亲属关系也不能只按气象职能理解。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 这里采用公开流传的毛利天地分离叙事，不涉及受限仪式知识。不同部族与家族传承对名字、次序和解释可能各有侧重，阅读时应尊重当地讲述者与相关谱系。

en.name: Tāwhirimātea
en.title: Māori atua of winds and storms

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Tāwhirimātea is the Māori atua associated with winds, clouds, and storms, a child of Ranginui and Papatūānuku. He opposes his siblings’ decision to separate their parents. Public narratives use his response to explain relationships between weather and other domains of the living world.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After Tāne separates earth and sky, Tāwhirimātea joins his father above and attacks his brothers with storms. Forests break and seas churn, while the brothers associated with cultivated and uncultivated foods shelter within their mother. Tūmatauenga alone stands firm against the assault.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Strong winds, gathering clouds, and driving rain distinguish his presence across sky, forest, and ocean. He is not a uniformly named wind god shared throughout Polynesia. The kin relationships of Māori atua carry meanings that exceed a simple list of meteorological responsibilities.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: This account draws on publicly shared Māori narratives of earth and sky separating, not restricted ceremonial knowledge. Iwi and whānau traditions may emphasize different names, sequences, and interpretations. Their genealogical settings and the authority of local narrators should remain visible and respected.

name: 希内努伊特波
title: 毛利传统中迎接亡者的夜之伟大女性

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 希内努伊特波的名字常译为夜之伟大女性，是毛利传统中与死亡世界相联的神圣存在。在一组公开叙事里，她原名希内蒂塔玛，发现伴侣塔内也是自己的父亲后离开光明世界，成为迎接后代亡者者。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 公开流传的玛乌伊故事讲述英雄试图消除人类死亡：他打算趁希内努伊特波熟睡，逆向穿过她的身体再从口中出来。他嘱咐同行鸟类保持安静，但一只小鸟忍不住发笑，女神惊醒，将他夹住致死。这次失败说明人类不能靠英雄的计谋越过死亡的界限。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 夜、通向亡者世界的门槛与迎接子孙的角色是重要线索。她并非等同于邪恶魔王，故事也不仅呈现威胁，而是把死亡的不可逃避与亲属延续放在同一关系中理解。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 此处只述毛利公开教育材料中可见的叙事层面，不提供丧葬仪式知识。不同部族保存不同讲法，涉及死亡与祖先时应保持庄重，不把相关神圣叙事当作恐怖猎奇素材。

en.name: Hine-nui-te-pō
en.title: Great woman of night who receives the dead in Māori tradition

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hine-nui-te-pō, often translated as Great Woman of Night, is associated with the realm of death in Māori traditions. In one publicly shared account, she was Hine-tītama, who left the world of light after discovering that her partner Tāne was also her father.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Māui attempts to end human death by passing backward through her sleeping body and emerging from her mouth. He orders accompanying birds to remain silent, but one laughs. Hine-nui-te-pō wakes and crushes him between her thighs, establishing the failure of his challenge to mortality.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Night, the threshold of the dead, and the reception of descendants provide central themes. She is not equivalent to an evil demon. Her role connects the inevitability of death with kinship and continuing relationships, rather than representing an isolated monster for heroes to defeat.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Only narrative material shared in public Māori educational contexts is included here, not funeral procedures or restricted knowledge. Iwi traditions maintain differing accounts. Stories concerning death and ancestors deserve a respectful tone rather than treatment as sensational horror or detached exotic entertainment.

name: 瓦吉尔
title: 努恩加尔国土中与水道相联的祖先存在

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 瓦吉尔是澳大利亚西南部努恩加尔传统中与水、地貌及国土关系密切的蛇形祖先存在，名字也有不同拼写。这里的国土不只是地理空间，还包含祖先、生命与社群责任，不能把其缩减为普通河流神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 努恩加尔社群公开分享的说明把瓦吉尔在大地上的移动与河道、谷地和水域的形成联系起来，珀斯一带的天鹅河即是常见例子。祖先的经过使地景成为承载关系与记忆的所在，而非一张空白地图；这些公开概述不意味着所有地点故事或进一步解释都可自由转述。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 蛇形祖先、弯曲河道与维系生命的水是公开说明中常见的线索。这里不复制任何社群图样，也不规定一幅通用形象；所谓彩虹蛇并不意味着全澳只有同一位祖先。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 瓦吉尔应置于努恩加尔国土和当代社群的持续关系中理解，而非归为已经消失的信仰。本文只用公开通识，不涉及受限地点、仪式或知识，进一步使用须尊重知识持有者。

en.name: Wagyl
en.title: An ancestral presence associated with waterways in Noongar Country

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Wagyl is a serpentine ancestral presence associated with water, landforms, and Noongar Country in southwestern Australia. Spellings vary. Country includes relationships among ancestors, living beings, places, and community responsibilities; the term cannot be reduced to a neutral geographic area or Wagyl to a generic river god.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Public Noongar explanations connect Wagyl’s movements with the making of waterways, valleys, and water places; the Swan River around Perth is a familiar example. These accounts present landscape as ancestral relationship and memory. Public summaries do not imply unrestricted permission to retell every local account.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A serpentine ancestor, winding waterways, and water sustaining life are appropriate public themes. No community designs are reproduced here, and no standardized portrait is prescribed. The broad English label Rainbow Serpent does not establish one identical ancestral being across all Aboriginal Australian peoples.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Wagyl belongs within continuing Noongar relationships with Country, not a religion presumed to have disappeared. This entry uses general public knowledge only. Restricted places, ceremonies, and teachings are excluded, and further use should respect the authority and permissions of relevant knowledge holders.

name: 恩加约德
title: 昆温库传统中与水及祖先力量相联的存在

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 恩加约德是澳大利亚北部阿纳姆地西部昆温库语言文化语境中的蛇形祖先存在，公开介绍常将其称为彩虹蛇。其身份依托当地国土与传承，并非努恩加尔瓦吉尔的另一拼法，两者属于不同社群。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 公开通识把恩加约德与水潭、雨季及塑造地貌的祖先力量联系起来。一些公开讲述描述其在行为规范被触犯时，以洪水或吞没带来严厉后果，强调人对地点及社会关系负有责任。这里不拼接不同地点的故事，也不补写受限仪式的经过，只呈现已经公开的共同主题。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 蛇形身体与水域力量是公开可述的辨识线索，但具体造型并非随意可复制的装饰。本条不摹写族群图样，不把其他地区彩虹蛇的外貌或属性自动添加到恩加约德身上。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 相关知识由具体社群和知识持有者维系，公开艺术或解说并不等于所有故事均已开放。介绍应保留昆温库背景，尊重地方许可与知识边界，不以泛原住民神话替代其文化身份。

en.name: Ngalyod
en.title: An ancestral presence of water in Kunwinjku traditions

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ngalyod is a serpentine ancestral presence in Kunwinjku cultural and language contexts of western Arnhem Land in northern Australia, often introduced publicly as a Rainbow Serpent. This identity belongs to particular Country and traditions, not another spelling of the Noongar ancestral presence Wagyl.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Public accounts associate Ngalyod with waterholes, seasonal rains, and ancestral forces shaping land. Some describe flooding or swallowing as consequences of violated obligations, emphasizing responsibilities to places and relationships. This summary does not combine site narratives or reconstruct restricted ceremonies beyond those openly shared themes.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A serpentine body and powerful associations with water provide appropriate public identifying themes. Specific representations are not automatically available as decorative resources. No community designs are copied here, and attributes of Rainbow Serpent traditions elsewhere are not added indiscriminately to Ngalyod’s identity.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Particular communities and knowledge holders sustain these traditions. Public artworks or educational descriptions do not make every associated story unrestricted. Interpretation should retain the Kunwinjku context, respect local permissions and knowledge boundaries, and avoid replacing this identity with an undifferentiated category of Aboriginal mythology.

name: 路西法
title: 晨星之名的由来与误读

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 路西法不是基督教所敬拜的神，而是一个称号。它出自拉丁语，意为“带光者”，即晨星金星。《武加大译本》以赛亚书十四章用它指巴比伦王，语境是讽刺其傲慢必倾的短歌。后世神学家把这词与福音书中撒但坠落的话相连，才渐成堕落天使之名。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 圣经正典并未给路西法立传。以赛亚书的“晨星”是讥讽人间君王的比喻；《路加福音》提到“我看见撒但从天上坠落”；《启示录》十二章描写大龙被摔在地上。把这些经文串成完整故事的是后来的传统与文学，而非单一经文叙事。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 常见形象是晨星、坠落的光、折断的翅膀与号角。图像学多取自中世纪与近代艺术：《失乐园》的雄辩独白、但丁《神曲》冰湖中的巨影、布莱克的水彩，都不是古代文本的描写，却塑造了今日大众想象。辨析时宜分清经文、传统与文学三层。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 对许多基督徒而言，这段话题属神学与灵修范畴，而非神话人物传记；不同教派解读也不一致。文学、绘画与流行文化又把他变成反抗者的象征。论述时应避免把他当作“神”，也不宜虚构其生平细节，而应说明经文、教父传统与后世创作各自的层次。

en.name: Lucifer
en.title: A name for the morning star, not a god

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Lucifer is not a deity in Christian worship but a title. It comes from Latin for “light-bearer”, the morning star Venus. Jerome’s Vulgate uses it in Isaiah 14 for the king of Babylon, inside a taunt-song about a proud ruler who will fall.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: No canonical text gives Lucifer a biography. Isaiah’s morning star is a satirical image of a human king; Luke records a saying about Satan falling like lightning; Revelation 12 pictures a dragon thrown down. Later tradition stitched such passages into a single story.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Artists gave him broken wings, falling light and horns, drawing on Dante, Milton’s Paradise Lost and Blake rather than on scripture. Readers should separate the biblical verses, patristic teaching and later literature, because popular imagery is largely a literary inheritance.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: For most Christians this is a matter of theology and devotion, not a mythic life story, and interpretations differ between churches. Literature and film also turned him into a symbol of rebellion. Respectful accounts avoid calling him a god or inventing episodes, and name their sources plainly.

name: 夏娃
title: 《创世记》中的众生之母

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 夏娃见于《创世记》二至四章，希伯来文名意为“活者”，常译作“众生之母”。她与亚当同被安置在伊甸园，是犹太教、基督教与伊斯兰教共享的人物，伊斯兰传统称她为哈娃。经文对她的描写十分简省，因此留下广阔的诠释空间。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 叙事中她受蛇劝诱，与亚当同食禁果，眼睛明亮而察觉赤身，随后被逐出乐园。耶和华宣告她将承受生育之苦，与后裔的争战也由此展开。该隐与亚伯的故事紧接其后，使她成为人类家庭纷争叙事的起点。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 艺术中常以无花果叶、果实、蛇与纺锤辨识她。苹果并非经文所载，而是拉丁语双关与欧洲绘画的附加物；东方教会图像让她着红袍、持纺锤。这些符号多属后世的视觉传统，不能直接当作经文细节来引用。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 犹太释经传统对她的评价分歧，有视其为智慧与母亲者，也有以她为过失之源者，米德拉什各有说法。基督教神学借她展开原罪与救赎的讨论，保罗书信以“第二亚当”对观。今日释经多强调叙事的象征性，并反省历代加于女性的责难。

en.name: Eve
en.title: Mother of the living in Genesis

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Eve appears in Genesis 2–4; her Hebrew name is linked to “living” and she is called the mother of all living. Placed with Adam in Eden, she belongs to Jewish, Christian and Islamic scripture alike, where she is named Hawwa. The text says little about her.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: She is persuaded by the serpent, eats the forbidden fruit with Adam, sees their nakedness and is expelled from the garden. Childbirth pain and conflict with her offspring are announced, and the Cain and Abel story follows at once, making her the starting point of human family strife.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Fig leaves, fruit, a serpent and a spindle identify her in art. The apple is not in the text but enters through Latin wordplay and European painting; Eastern icons show her in red with a spindle. These are visual conventions rather than scriptural detail.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Jewish interpretation is divided, reading her as wise mother or as the source of loss, and midrash develops both. Christian theology debates original sin and redemption through her, while modern scholarship stresses the narrative’s symbolic character and reviews centuries of blame placed on women.

name: 大卫
title: 牧童出身的以色列君王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 大卫是《撒母耳记》所载的以色列王，约当公元前十一至十世纪。他出身伯利恒的耶西家，少年牧羊、弹琴，被撒母耳膏立。他同时受犹太教、基督教与伊斯兰教尊崇，《古兰经》称他为达乌德，并说他获赐《诗篇》。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 最著名的故事是以投石索击败非利士巨人歌利亚。此后他因扫罗嫉妒而流亡，最终成为犹大与以色列之王，定都耶路撒冷，把约柜迎入城中。他与拔示巴的私情、借刀杀乌利亚以及押沙龙的叛乱，构成王权叙事里沉重的阴影。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 常见标识是投石索、竖琴、王冠与耶路撒冷城。《诗篇》传统归于他名下，故他被视为诗人与礼拜者；“大卫之星”之名虽流行，其六角形符号实为中世纪后期犹太社群所采用，与圣经时代并无直接关联。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 犹太传统视他为弥赛亚谱系的祖先与理想君王；基督教福音书以家谱接续他，称耶稣为“大卫的子孙”；伊斯兰传统强调他的公正、歌喉与《诗篇》。历代君主也常借其形象正当化王权，使他在宗教与政治上被反复引用。

en.name: David
en.title: Shepherd boy who became king

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: David is the king of Israel in the books of Samuel, dated roughly to the eleventh to tenth centuries BCE. Youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, he herded sheep and played the lyre before Samuel anointed him. Jews, Christians and Muslims honour him; the Quran names him Dawud.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His best-known deed is felling the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling. Fleeing Saul’s jealousy, he later ruled Judah and Israel, took Jerusalem and brought the ark into it. His affair with Bathsheba, the death of Uriah and Absalom’s revolt darken the royal story.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A sling, lyre, crown and the city of Jerusalem identify him. The Psalms are traditionally ascribed to him, making him a poet and worshipper. The six-pointed “Star of David” is a later medieval Jewish emblem, not a biblical attribute, despite its popular name.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Jewish tradition treats him as ancestor of the Messiah and model king; the Gospels trace Jesus to him as “son of David”; Islam praises his justice, voice and Psalms. Rulers have repeatedly borrowed his image to legitimise power, which is why he is cited in both devotional and political settings.

name: 所罗门
title: 以智慧与圣殿著称的君王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 所罗门是大卫与拔示巴之子，《列王纪上》记他继位后求智慧，上帝赐他“聪明的心”。他主持建造耶路撒冷第一圣殿，使王国达到鼎盛。他同样是伊斯兰教尊崇的先知苏莱曼，被视为通晓鸟语、役使精灵的君王。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 最脍炙人口的是两位妇人争婴的判案：他命人将婴儿劈开，真母遂放弃争夺，智慧由此显明。叙事也记他大兴土木、与列国通婚、晚年受外邦神祇影响，导致王国在他死后分裂。示巴女王的访问是另一段著名情节。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 标志物为圣殿、王座、智慧之书与指环。后世传说赋予他驱使精灵、统御百兽的权能，《所罗门遗训》与犹太、阿拉伯民间故事皆然；“所罗门之印”的六角或五角护符亦属这些传说层，并非经文原载。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 犹太传统以《箴言》《传道书》《雅歌》归其名下，视为智慧文学的代表；基督教以此喻示真正的智慧；埃塞俄比亚传统另有《列王荣耀记》，叙述他与示巴女王之子。各地传说繁多，讨论时宜区分经文记载与后世增益的奇幻材料。

en.name: Solomon
en.title: King famed for wisdom and the Temple

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Solomon, son of David and Bathsheba, asks for wisdom in 1 Kings and is given a discerning heart. He builds the First Temple in Jerusalem and rules at the kingdom’s height. Islam honours him as the prophet Sulayman, said to know bird speech and command jinn.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His most famous case is two women claiming one infant: he orders the child cut in two, and the true mother yields. The narrative also records forced labour, foreign marriages and late idolatry that split the kingdom after his death. The queen of Sheba’s visit is another celebrated episode.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The Temple, throne, wisdom book and ring are his marks. Later legend grants him power over demons and beasts, as in the Testament of Solomon and Jewish and Arabic tales; the “seal of Solomon” amulet belongs to that legendary layer, not the biblical text.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Jewish tradition ascribes Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs to him; Christianity reads him as a figure of true wisdom; Ethiopian tradition adds the Kebra Nagast, telling of his son by the queen of Sheba. Accounts should separate scripture from later fantasy material.

name: 犹大
title: 十二门徒中出卖耶稣者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 犹大·伊斯加略是耶稣十二门徒之一，负责钱囊。福音书说他以三十块银钱为价，向祭司长交出耶稣。他的名字在西方语言中几乎成为“背叛者”的代称，但经文对他动机的交代极少，留下许多猜测空间。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 最后的晚餐上耶稣预言被卖，随后犹大以亲吻为记号指认他，四福音都记载此事而细节不同。关于他的结局，正典内部即有差异：《马太福音》说他懊悔、退还银钱后自缢；《使徒行传》则说他仆倒腹裂而死，两说并列而未被统一。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 记号是三十块银钱、钱袋与亲吻。中世纪的受难剧与绘画常把他画成红发、左手持钱袋的形象，这些是戏剧化的惯例，而非福音书记载。银钱与“血田”的来历，在两种结局叙述中的解释也不相同。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 基督教神学把他放在救赎计划与人的责任之间的张力里讨论：经文既说他“灭亡”了，也说所发生的事按着定命成就。历代反犹宣传曾借他攻击犹太人，教会近年多明确谴责此类曲解。讨论应以经文为本，避免煽情与集体归罪。

en.name: Judas
en.title: The disciple who handed Jesus over

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples and kept the common purse. The Gospels say he handed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver. His name became a byword for betrayal in European languages, yet the texts say very little about his motives.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: At the last supper Jesus foretells the betrayal, and Judas identifies him with a kiss. All four Gospels report this with differing detail. Their accounts of his end differ too: Matthew has him remorseful, returning the money and hanging himself; Acts says he fell and burst open.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Coins, a purse and the kiss mark him out. Medieval passion plays and paintings gave him red hair and a money bag in the left hand, theatrical conventions rather than gospel detail. The origin of the thirty pieces and the “field of blood” is explained differently in each ending.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Theology discusses him where providence meets human responsibility, since the texts call him lost while also saying events unfolded as determined. Anti-Jewish polemic long used him against Jews, a distortion churches have increasingly condemned. Accounts should stay close to the texts and avoid sensation.

name: 抹大拉的马利亚
title: 复活清晨的首位见证者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 抹大拉的马利亚是四福音都提到的妇女，其名指明她来自加利利海西岸的抹大拉村。路加记耶稣曾从她身上赶出七个鬼，此后她以自己的财物供给耶稣与门徒的团体，是随行门徒中常被点名的女性。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 她在十字架旁远远观看，又于安息日后的清早带着香料前往坟墓，成为最先看见空墓与复活之主的人。《约翰福音》记她与复活者对话，误认其为园丁；她随后向门徒报信，故被早期教会称为“使徒们的使徒”。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 传统图像给她香膏罐、长发与红色披风。西方教会自六世纪起把她与路加福音中无名的“罪妇”、伯大尼的马利亚合并，遂生出“堕落女子”的误读；东方教会从未如此合并，其圣像多只是持香罐的见证者。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 二十世纪以来的研究重新审视这些合并：正典并未说她曾是妓女，路加的无名罪妇亦未指名。诺斯替文献《马利亚福音》等又呈现另一种形象，但属正典之外。今日她被视为复活的首位见证人，也是女性门徒身份的重要范例。

en.name: Mary Magdalene
en.title: First witness of the resurrection

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Mary Magdalene appears in all four Gospels; her name means she came from Magdala on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. Luke says seven demons left her, and afterwards she supported Jesus and the disciples from her own means, a woman named among his followers.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: She watched from afar at the cross and went to the tomb with spices at dawn after the sabbath, becoming the first to see it empty and to meet the risen Lord. John has her mistake him for a gardener before she announces the news, so early tradition called her apostle to the apostles.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Jars of ointment, long hair and a red cloak identify her in art. From the sixth century the Western church merged her with Luke’s unnamed sinful woman and with Mary of Bethany, creating the “fallen woman” misreading; Eastern icons never merged them and show a jar-bearing witness.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Modern scholarship has reassessed those mergings: the canon never calls her a prostitute, and Luke’s sinner is unnamed. Gnostic works such as the Gospel of Mary add another portrait outside the canon. She is now honoured as first resurrection witness and a model of women’s discipleship.

name: 库库尔坎
title: 尤卡坦玛雅的羽蛇神祇

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 库库尔坎是尤卡坦玛雅人崇奉的羽蛇神，名字在尤卡坦玛雅语中意为“羽蛇”。他的形象与中部墨西哥的羽蛇神克察尔科亚特尔同源，随贸易与政治势力传入玛雅地区，但两者并非同一位格，祭祀方式与神话细节各有在地变化。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 传说他率众自西方而来，在奇琴伊察建都施政，后因争执返回西方，临行许诺归返。殖民时期的玛雅文献如《奇兰巴兰之书》与兰达的记述混合了这些记忆；西班牙人到来时，当地人也曾以“库库尔坎归来”的传闻理解外来者。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 特征是羽蛇之身、太阳圆盘与螺旋形浮雕，常与风、雨、金星及统治者的权威相联。奇琴伊察的库库尔坎金字塔在春分秋分时出现蛇形光影，被视为建筑与天象的结合；但他的神格图像远比“历法奇观”复杂。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 前哥伦布时期的玛雅城邦各有主神与祭祀体系，库库尔坎的地位随政治中心起伏。殖民时代焚毁大量抄本后，相关知识多经西班牙教士与本地记载者转述。今日尤卡坦社区仍存与之相关的地景记忆，研究时宜区分古代信仰、殖民记述与观光叙述。

en.name: Kukulkan
en.title: Feathered serpent of the Yucatec Maya

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Kukulkan is the feathered serpent honoured by the Yucatec Maya, his name meaning “feathered serpent” in Yucatec Maya. His figure shares roots with the central Mexican Quetzalcoatl and arrived through trade and political contact, yet the two are not identical, with local differences in cult and story.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Traditions tell of a lord who came from the west, ruled at Chichen Itza and returned west after a dispute, promising to come back. Colonial Maya texts such as the Books of Chilam Balam and Landa’s account blend these memories, and rumours of his return shaped how locals first read the Spaniards.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: He is shown as a plumed serpent with solar discs and spiral reliefs, linked to wind, rain, Venus and rulerly authority. At the pyramid of Kukulkan the equinox throws a serpent-shaped shadow, a fusion of architecture and sky; his iconography is far richer than that single spectacle.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Maya city-states each had their own pantheons, and Kukulkan’s standing rose and fell with political centres. After colonial book burnings, knowledge survives largely through Spanish priests and Maya writers. Landscape memories persist in Yucatan today, so ancient cult, colonial report and tourist narrative should be told apart.

name: 索洛特尔
title: 双生、落日与引路的犬神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 索洛特尔是纳瓦人神系中的一位神祇，名字意为“双生者”或“玩偶”，与金星、落日、火及双生子相关。在《佛罗伦萨抄本》等纳瓦文献里，他是羽蛇神克察尔科亚特尔的双生兄弟，二者常在神话中成对出现，共赴冥界取回人类骨骸。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 讲述创世的一则故事中，羽蛇神与索洛特尔下到冥界，向冥王求取前代人类的遗骨；索洛特尔受诱戴上羽毛冠而破戒，骨殖落地碎裂，故世人高矮不一。另一类叙述里他化身为犬，为亡者引路过冥河，成为送葬图像常见的身影。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识标记是犬首、倒置的脚、残缺或不对称的面部，以及螺旋与骨饰。倒足与下垂的眼睛指向落日与幽冥的方向；双生神像常左右成对。他的形象在后古典期墨西哥中部的石雕与彩绘中频繁出现。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 纳瓦人的宗教在十六世纪被西班牙传教士记录与压制，材料多出自抄本与教士的民族志访谈，需谨慎对待其编排。索洛特尔兼具金星晨昏之象、双生子观念与亡者引路者三重职能，反映出纳瓦人对时间循环与死亡过渡的思考。

en.name: Xolotl
en.title: Twin, evening star and dog guide

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Xolotl is a Nahua deity whose name means “twin” or “puppet”, associated with Venus, the setting sun, fire and twins. In the Florentine Codex and related sources he is the twin brother of Quetzalcoatl, the two appearing as a pair, notably in the journey to fetch human bones.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In one creation account the two descend to the underworld to ask Mictlantecuhtli for the bones of earlier people; Xolotl breaks the rule by wearing a feather crown, the bones shatter and humans differ in height. Elsewhere he becomes a dog guiding the dead across a river.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: He is identified by a dog head, reversed feet, a damaged or asymmetrical face, spirals and bone ornaments. The backward foot and downcast eye point to sunset and the underworld, and twin figures are carved in pairs. His image is common in Late Postclassic sculpture and painting of central Mexico.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Nahua religion was recorded and suppressed by sixteenth-century friars, so the surviving corpus reflects their editing and questions. Xolotl’s linked roles as evening star, twin and psychopomp show how Nahua thought connected cyclical time with the passage of the dead.

name: 埃埃卡特尔
title: 带来风与雨的羽蛇面相

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 埃埃卡特尔是纳瓦神系中的风神，名字意为“风”。他常被视为羽蛇神克察尔科亚特尔的另一面相或称号，二者共祀于圆形风神庙。在《佛罗伦萨抄本》的叙述中，正是风神之形为大地清路，使雨神得以下行降雨。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 创世叙事里，前代人类曾被风毁灭，幸存者化为猿猴；另一则说明雨神与风神如何合作，先由风清扫道路，雨水才能落下。他又与呼吸、生命气息相连，初生婴儿的洗礼仪与呼名常求他护佑；口吹之息被视为他的临在。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识特征是锥形嘴或红色鸟喙状面罩、猴形耳饰、贝壳胸饰与旋纹。锥形口面具象征吹风；他常与九风之日、北方及金星相关。圆形神庙的圆基正是为适应风的流动形态而建，是其崇拜的标志性建筑。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 风既赐生命又具破坏力，因此他在纳瓦宗教中兼具创造与毁灭的双面。殖民时期的记载把他与圣灵、神圣气息相比附，这属于传教士的解释框架，未必等同原意。今日墨西哥中部的民俗与舞蹈中，仍可辨识其面具母题的延伸。

en.name: Ehecatl
en.title: Wind god, an aspect of the feathered serpent

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ehecatl is the Nahua god of wind, his name simply meaning “wind”. He is often treated as an aspect or title of Quetzalcoatl, and the two were worshipped in round temples. In the Florentine Codex it is the wind god who clears a path so that the rain gods can descend.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Creation accounts say an earlier humanity was destroyed by wind and survivors became monkeys. Other stories show wind sweeping the road before rain falls. He is also tied to breath and life: naming and bathing rites for newborns asked his protection, and blown breath signalled his presence.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A conical mouth or red beak mask, monkey ear ornaments, a shell pectoral and spiral motifs identify him. The cone stands for blowing wind, and he links to the day Nine Wind, the north and Venus. Round temple platforms, built for moving air, are the signature of his cult.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Wind gives life and destroys it, so he holds both faces in Nahua religion. Colonial writers compared him to the Holy Spirit and sacred breath, a missionary frame rather than a native equation. Mask motifs descended from his imagery still appear in central Mexican dance and festival.

name: 查斯卡
title: 印加历中的金星与晨昏

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 查斯卡是印加宗教中被崇奉的金星，其名在克丘亚语中与“鬈发”相关，因金星如乱发般闪烁。它既是晨星也是昏星，印加人分别以两个名号称呼其晨出与夕现之相，视为太阳的侍从与信使，与月神、太阳共同构成天界秩序。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 编年史家记述，印加人观察金星的运行以定时节与祭祀，认为其出现预示播种或战事。据瓜曼·波马等人的记载，查斯卡的显现与太阳神的事务相关，祭祀在特定的观测点举行，相关仪式多与农业周期和王权庆典相连。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 标识是金星、双重的晨昏之相与金色饰物。在殖民时期的图画中，金星常被绘作头戴发光饰物的形象，与太阳、月亮并列显示天界层级。因印加人没有文字，今日所依多是西班牙编年史与克丘亚口头传统的转述。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 安第斯地区至今仍以晨昏之星安排农事与节庆，金星在克丘亚语社区中被称为查斯卡，与黎明、牧群和雨水相联系。研究时须注意：印加帝国时代的天象崇拜与今日村民的实践相隔数百年，不能简单等同，但两者共享对金星周期的长期关注。

en.name: Chasca
en.title: Venus, the dawn and dusk star of the Inca

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Chasca is the planet Venus as honoured in Inca religion; the Quechua name is linked to tangled or radiant hair, because Venus flickers like dishevelled locks. As morning and evening star it was named in two aspects and seen as attendant and messenger of the sun, completing a sky order with moon and sun.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Chroniclers report that the Inca watched Venus to fix seasons and sacrifices, taking its appearance as a sign for sowing or war. Guaman Poma and others link its rising to the sun god’s affairs, with rites held at set observation points and tied to farming and royal festivals.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Venus, its double aspect and gold ornaments are the markers. Colonial drawings show the star with a radiant headdress beside sun and moon to grade the heavens. Because the Inca left no writing, accounts depend on Spanish chronicles and Quechua oral tradition.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Andean communities still time farm work and festivals by the dawn and dusk star, called Chasca in Quechua and linked to dawn, herds and rain. Imperial sky worship and present practice are centuries apart and should not be simply equated, though both share a long attention to the Venus cycle.

name: 耶莫雅
title: 水域之母与奥贡河的奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 耶莫雅是约鲁巴信仰中受供奉的奥里沙，与奥贡河、孕产、母婴及水域相关，被视为众奥里沙之母。她不是民间故事里的角色，而是活生生的崇拜对象：信众通过祭祀、占卜与节庆与她建立关系，奥贡河畔的伊巴马节至今仍有庆典。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 神话说法随地区而异：一说她是奥卢杜马雷之女，嫁给奥古恩或以水之形流入奥贡河；一说她生养众多奥里沙，因水流受阻而化入河中。诸版本并不统一，崇拜者各有传承，叙述时不宜当作单一的“官方”版本。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识之象是水、扇子、白布、螺旋贝壳与蓝白两色的串珠。她的祭司与信众多着白、青色衣物，以示水与洁净；祭祀常见凉水、葫芦与母羊。图像与法器在不同教区与家族传统中差别不小。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 跨大西洋奴隶贸易中，她的信仰随被掳非洲人传入古巴、巴西等地，演化为古巴的圣拉·雷格拉与巴西的伊曼雅，在天主教圣像下隐藏供奉，形成至今活跃的离散传统。援引时应说明其与约鲁巴本土传统的连续与变形，而不应简化为“民俗”。

en.name: Yemoja
en.title: Mother of waters, orisha of the Ogun River

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Yemoja is an orisha of living Yoruba religion, linked to the Ogun River, pregnancy, mothers and children and honoured as mother of the orishas. She is no folktale character but a worshipped presence: devotees approach her through offerings, divination and festivals, and the Ibama festival still draws crowds to the river.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Myths vary by region. Some make her a daughter of Olodumare who married Ogun or flowed into the Ogun River; others have her bear many orishas and enter the water when its flow was blocked. Versions disagree, each lineage keeps its own, and none should be presented as the single official account.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Water, a fan, white cloth, spiral shells and blue-and-white bead strands identify her. Priests and devotees dress in white and pale blue for water and purity, and offerings include cool water, gourds and ewes. Images and implements differ widely between houses and families.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Through the Atlantic slave trade her worship reached Cuba and Brazil, becoming Regla de Ocha’s Yemayá and Brazilian Iemanjá, hidden under Catholic images and still flourishing. Such references should show both continuity with Yoruba tradition and its transformation, never reducing her to folklore.

name: 奥绍西
title: 林中猎手与奥里沙的弓

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥绍西是约鲁巴信仰中的奥里沙，被尊为猎手、林地之主与正义的守望者。他的称号常与“独行者”相关，传说他惯于独自走入丛林，以弓箭与铁器狩猎；他也是奥古恩的兄弟或伙伴，二者在铁、战争与狩猎上的职能相邻。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 传说中他曾因水之女神未予清水而举箭相向，被众奥里沙责难，后得谅解并与水神订约，这则故事解释了他的信众为何在仪式中以水相敬。另有叙述讲他射落巨鸟，为村庄带来安宁；诸版本细节因城镇而异。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识标志是单弦弓、铁箭、鸟羽与独居猎人的装束，串珠多为绿、蓝与黄色。供奉他的神龛常置弓箭与铁器，祭品包括猎物与蜂蜜；其祭仪强调在野外举行，与城市型奥里沙的庙堂供奉有所不同。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奥绍西崇拜在约鲁巴兰、贝宁与多哥一带延续，并随离散社群进入古巴与巴西的奥里沙传统。他在本土常被视为正义与守约的守护者，在当代语境中也被引作生态与承诺的象征；讨论时仍应尊重其作为崇拜对象的地位。

en.name: Oshosi
en.title: Hunter of the forest, owner of the bow

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Oshosi is a Yoruba orisha honoured as hunter, master of the forest and guardian of justice. His praise names stress the solitary one who walks into the bush with bow and iron, and he is brother or companion to Ogun, whose domains of iron, war and hunting lie close to his.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: One story has him shoot at a water goddess who refused him cool water; the other orishas reproach him, and a pact with the waters follows, explaining why his rites honour water. Other accounts tell of him shooting a great bird to bring peace to a town, with details varying by locality.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A single-string bow, iron arrows, bird feathers and a hunter’s solitary dress identify him, with green, blue and yellow beads. Shrines hold bows and iron, offerings include game and honey, and his rites stress the open bush rather than the town shrines of other orishas.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: His worship continues in Yorubaland, Benin and Togo and travelled with dispersed communities into Cuban and Brazilian orisha traditions. At home he guards justice and promises, and today he is also invoked for ecology and keeping faith; accounts should respect his standing as a worshipped power.

name: 阿丁克拉符号
title: 阿坎人的谚语纹样系统

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 首先要说明：阿丁克拉不是神明，而是阿坎人，包括阿散蒂、芳蒂等群体使用的一套视觉符号，多见于布料印花、印章与建筑装饰。每个符号各有名称与对应的谚语，承载伦理、历史与人生哲理，是阿坎文化中的格言图像，而非神话人物。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 其起源有两则流传较广的说法：一说源于十九世纪阿散蒂与邻邦战争时仿制的敌方纹样，一说来自阿克拉商人的印染工艺。无论何者，符号系统在二十世纪随蜡染布流行而扩充，形成数百个纹样，各有谚语，用于丧礼、婚礼与日常。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识方法是把纹样与谚语配对：如“吉耶·尼阿梅”以双手承神之意表达至上，桑科法为回望之鸟，杜阿费为梳。符号多为黑底印于深红或赭色布上，也见于金饰与木雕；单看图形常不足以断定含义，须结合谚语与场合。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿丁克拉布在加纳是常见衣着与礼赠，丧礼上尤其讲究纹样选择，以纹样说明逝者品格与生者情谊。这些符号也被用于现代设计、首饰与教育材料。讨论时应明确其为谚语与价值观的图像编码，与崇拜对象不同，并留意商业使用与文化语境的落差。

en.name: Adinkra symbols
en.title: Akan proverb symbols, not deities

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Adinkra is not a deity but a system of visual symbols used by Akan peoples, including Asante and Fante, printed on cloth and carved on stamps, buildings and goldweights. Each symbol carries a name and a proverb about ethics, history or conduct: these are proverbial images, not mythic persons.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Two origin stories circulate: one derives the patterns from designs copied during nineteenth-century Asante wars, the other from printers in Accra. Either way the repertoire expanded with the twentieth-century wax-print trade into hundreds of motifs, each with a proverb, worn at funerals, weddings and daily life.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Read them by pairing motif with proverb: Gye Nyame, “except God”, expresses divine supremacy; Sankofa is the bird looking back; Duafe is the comb. Printed black on deep red or ochre cloth, they also appear in gold and woodwork. The shape alone rarely fixes meaning without proverb and occasion.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Adinkra cloth is everyday dress and ceremonial gift in Ghana, with motifs chosen at funerals to praise the dead and console the living. The symbols also serve modern design, jewellery and teaching. They encode values and proverbs rather than objects of worship, and their commercial reuse deserves scrutiny.

name: 桑科法
title: 回望之鸟与返取的谚语

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 桑科法同样不是神祇，而是阿坎文化中的符号与观念，常绘为一只回头取蛋的鸟。其谚语意为“回到过去取回所失，并不违逆”，强调从往昔经验中汲取智慧以面对当下，属阿丁克拉符号体系中最广为人知的一则。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 与此符号相关的故事多讲一只鸟因须前行而回身取回遗落的蛋，解说者以之比拟人应审视过去。它常出现于丧礼、成年礼与纪念场合，提醒生者承继先人之训；也见于谚语对答与说谚语的游戏中，由长者向年轻人解说。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 图形要素是鸟身、回折的头颈与蛋，或简化为螺旋式的鸟形。颜色多取黑、赭与黄，可织于布、刻于木或铸于金。与其他阿丁克拉符号一样，其含义依附于谚语，单看图形不足以理解，须说明出处与使用场合。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 二十世纪泛非运动与非洲裔教育者广泛采用桑科法，作为回溯历史以重建自我的象征，加纳的旅游与工艺也大力推广此图。它因此在离散社群中常被误当作古老的神秘符号；说明时应指出其阿坎本源与现代的再造过程。

en.name: Sankofa
en.title: The bird that looks back, and its proverb

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Sankofa too is no deity but an Akan symbol and idea, usually drawn as a bird turning its head to take back an egg. The proverb says it is no wrong to go back for what you have forgotten, urging wisdom drawn from the past to guide the present. It is the best known of the Adinkra motifs.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Stories attached to it describe a bird that must go back for a dropped egg as it moves forward, and explainers read this as a call to examine the past. It appears at funerals, initiations and memorials, reminding the living of ancestral teaching, and in proverb games led by elders.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The design shows a bird body, an arched neck and an egg, or a spiralling bird form. Colours are usually black, ochre and yellow, worked in cloth, wood or gold. As with other Adinkra symbols, meaning depends on the proverb, so shape alone is not enough.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Pan-African movements and African-descended educators adopted Sankofa in the twentieth century as a sign of retrieving history to rebuild the self, and Ghanaian tourism and craft promote it widely. It is therefore often mistaken abroad for an ancient mystical sign, obscuring its Akan origin and modern reinvention.

name: 卡马普阿阿
title: 夏威夷传说中的猪形半神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 卡马普阿阿是夏威夷传统中的一位半神，名字意为“野猪之子”，兼具人形与猪形，力大无比，与土地肥沃、芋头种植及雨水相关。他被视为库普阿（kupua，超自然存在）之一，故事在夏威夷诸岛流传，各岛版本侧重不同。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 传说中他与火山女神佩莱长期争斗，情节包括争地、斗法与求爱；佩莱以火与熔岩相逼，他则以水与变形相抗，最终二人划定界线，分居迎风与背风之地。另一类故事讲他掘土成田、引水灌芋，解释地景与水系的由来。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识特征是猪首或全身猪形、獠牙、粗糙的鬃毛与强壮体格，也常与芋头田、湿地和雨相联系。夏威夷的木雕与树皮布图案中可辨人形与兽形并置；不同岛上的图像细节差异明显，不宜一概而论。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 这些故事属夏威夷原住民的口述传统，十九世纪由夏威夷学者与记录者写成文字，其中部分内容涉及只有特定家族或社群才可讲述的层次。今日的呼拉舞与土地运动中仍可见其形象。引用时应注明来源岛屿与版本差异，避免把诸说混成单一故事。

en.name: Kamapuaa
en.title: Hawaiian pig demigod of the land

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Kamapuaa is a Hawaiian demigod whose name means “pig child”, shifting between human and hog form. He is enormously strong and tied to fertile soil, taro cultivation and rain, counted among the kupua, beings of extraordinary power. Stories spread across the islands with different emphases.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He contends for years with the volcano goddess Pele over land, contests of power and courtship, she pressing with fire and lava while he answers with water and transformation, until they divide the island into windward and leeward domains. Other tales explain taro terraces and water channels as his digging.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A pig head or whole hog form, tusks, coarse bristles and great strength identify him, along with taro patches, wetlands and rain. Hawaiian carving and barkcloth patterns set human and animal shapes side by side, though details differ noticeably from island to island.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: These are Native Hawaiian oral traditions written down in the nineteenth century by Hawaiian scholars and recorders, and some layers belong only to particular families or communities. His image persists in hula and land struggles today. Citations should name island and version rather than merging them.

name: 西娜
title: 玻利尼西亚传统中的西娜

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 西娜是玻利尼西亚广泛流传的女性人物之名，萨摩亚、汤加、纽埃与毛利传统中都出现同名或近名的形象，含义与故事却并不同一。萨摩亚的传说讲述她与一条鳗鱼之间的交往，这则故事与椰子的起源相连，是当地最知名的叙述之一。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 萨摩亚版本多讲：鳗鱼为西娜所爱或所惧，被村人杀死后嘱其将头埋下，由此长出椰树，树冠的纤维与果实被视为其形态的延续。另有以她为月神或女神者，说她居于月亮的背面，与潮汐和女性技艺相关；各岛谱系不同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识特征是椰树、鳗鱼或海蛇、月光与花饰。萨摩亚的椰子传说常在影像与舞蹈中以此为题；在毛利传统中，同源的名字更多与月、女性工艺及潮汐相连，形象与萨摩亚的西娜并不同一，不应按字形直接等同。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 这些名字的相似反映出玻利尼西亚诸岛共同的南岛语渊源与长期的航海往来，但各社群对人物的理解自有脉络，需按岛屿与家族分别对待。传教士记录以及夏威夷、萨摩亚学者整理的口述文本，构成今日研究的主要依据；通俗读物常简化其差异。

en.name: Sina
en.title: A Polynesian woman of many versions

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Sina is a widely shared Polynesian name, appearing in Samoan, Tongan, Niuean and Maori traditions with related names but unlike stories. The Samoan tale of her dealings with an eel is the best known, since it explains the origin of the coconut and is told throughout the islands.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Samoan versions the eel, loved or feared by Sina, is killed by villagers and asks that its head be buried, from which the coconut palm grows, its husk and fruit continuing its form. Other accounts make her a moon deity living on the moon’s far side, tied to tides and women’s crafts.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Coconut palms, eels or sea snakes, moonlight and flower ornaments identify her. Samoan dance and film often take the coconut story as subject; in Maori tradition the cognate name belongs more to the moon, women’s weaving and tides, a distinct figure rather than the same person.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The similar names reflect shared Austronesian roots and centuries of Polynesian voyaging, yet each community holds its own understanding, best treated island by island and family by family. Missionary records and texts compiled by Hawaiian and Samoan scholars are the main sources, while popular books flatten the differences.

name: 天空鸸鹋
title: 银河暗带中的鸸鹋身影

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 天空鸸鹋不是单一的神话人物，而是澳大利亚部分原住民族在夜空暗带中辨认出的鸸鹋形象，其轮廓由银河的尘埃暗带构成，头在南十字附近，身在银河之中。这一讲法由特定地区的原住民族公开讲述，并不具有全澳通用的地位。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 公开流传的版本中，鸸鹋的形影与季节、蛋巢和泉水的出现相关：它在夜空中出现的时段指示何时寻蛋、何时雨水将至。相关叙述常以鸸鹋的坐姿或张开的身影描画暗带轮廓，并与邻近的星座、动物故事一并讲述。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨认方法是观察银河的暗尘带：南十字附近的头部、颈部的暗隙与银河中心的躯体。它属“暗云星座”一类，与以亮星连线的星座不同；不同语言群体对其命名、分段与解释各异，图形并非全澳统一的图案。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 相关故事与知识由特定民族持有，如维多利亚西北部的布隆人，以及中部与北部的若干语族，各地讲述者决定何者可以外传。近年天文教育与博物馆展示多引用这一天文知识，引用时须标明来源民族，并避免使用受限制的细节。

en.name: Sky Emu
en.title: The emu shaped by the Milky Way’s dark lanes

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: The Sky Emu is not a single mythic person but an emu recognised in the dark lanes of the Milky Way by particular Aboriginal peoples, its head near the Southern Cross and body within the galactic band. Such knowledge is told publicly by specific groups and is not pan-Australian.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In published versions the emu’s position marks seasons, nests and water: when it stands in the sky tells people when to seek eggs or expect rain. Narrators trace the dark shape as a sitting or open-winged bird and tell it alongside neighbouring star stories and animal narratives.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Look for the dust lanes: the head near the Southern Cross, the dark gap of the neck, the body toward the galactic centre. It belongs with “dark constellations” rather than star-linked figures. Different language groups name and divide it differently, so no single design is universal.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The stories are held by particular nations, such as the Boorong of north-western Victoria and various central and northern language groups, and each determines what may be shared. Astronomy education and museums now cite this knowledge, and should name its source peoples and avoid restricted detail.

name: 凯霍斯鲁
title: 《列王纪》中的理想君王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 凯霍斯鲁是波斯史诗《列王纪》中凯扬王朝的君王，出自菲尔多西的叙述，其原型可追溯到更早的中古伊朗传说与《阿维斯陀》传统。他被塑造成智慧、公正与勇武兼备的理想君主，是伊朗民族记忆中极为重要的形象。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他的故事包括少年在土兰受教育、回国夺回王位、为父复仇而与土兰王阿夫拉西亚布长期征战；最终在击败宿敌后，他主动放弃王权，把王位交与卢赫拉斯普，独自隐入雪山，从此不知所终。史诗以他的消失作结，留下“隐遁君王”之说。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 标志是王冠、凯扬之旗与王者灵光，以及他与众英雄并列的宫廷场景。细密画常绘他登基、渡海与雪中隐没的画面，其面容多为蓄须、华服。图像传统晚于史诗文本，多受波斯与中亚绘画风格影响。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《列王纪》成书于十至十一世纪，以新波斯语诗体汇集古伊朗传说，是波斯语文学的基石。凯霍斯鲁被后世用以论说公正王权与弃权的智慧；一些伊斯兰与民间传统附会其隐遁与末世期待，但这些说法与史诗文本应加区分。

en.name: Kay Khosrow
en.title: The ideal king of the Shahnameh

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Kay Khosrow is a king of the Kayani dynasty in Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh, his figure rooted in older Middle Iranian legend and Avestan tradition. He is drawn as the ideal ruler, combining wisdom, justice and martial courage, and stands among the most important figures of Iranian national memory.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His story takes him to exile and schooling in Turan, back to reclaim the throne, and into long war with Afrasiyab to avenge his father. After defeating his enemy he gives up kingship, hands the throne to Lohrasp and vanishes into the mountains, leaving the epic’s theme of the hidden king.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Crown, the Kaviani banner and royal glory mark him, together with court scenes shared with the heroes. Miniatures show his enthronement, sea crossings and snowy disappearance, with bearded face and rich robes. This painting tradition postdates the poem and draws on Persian and Central Asian styles.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Shahnameh was completed in the tenth to eleventh centuries, gathering ancient Iranian legend in New Persian verse as a foundation of Persian literature. Later writers cite Khosrow on just rule and the wisdom of renouncing power, while Islamic and folk traditions add hidden-imam expectations distinct from the epic itself.

name: 乌特纳皮什提姆
title: 《吉尔伽美什》中的洪水生还者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 乌特纳皮什提姆出自《吉尔伽美什史诗》第十一块泥板，是洪水之后获得永生的智者。他向吉尔伽美什讲述众神决定以洪水灭绝人类，而他受神示造舟，携家眷、工匠与鸟兽渡过洪灾，获赐居于河口之地的永生，其名意为“找到生命者”。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他的洪水叙事与更早的《阿特拉哈西斯》及苏美尔洪水故事同源，情节结构相近：神祇决定毁灭、一人受启示造船、放鸟试探水退、献祭与神祇的悔意。它与《创世记》挪亚的故事有显著平行，但细节、神学与文类并不相同，不宜直接等同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 标识是方舟、鸽子与燕子、洪水后的献祭与河口之地。泥板上他被称为“远者”，居于诸河汇流之处；史诗借他考验吉尔伽美什，以“永生不可得”作答。图像材料稀少，主要凭泥板文本辨识。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 泥板于十九世纪在尼尼微的亚述巴尼拔图书馆出土，其洪水段落与圣经的相似性当时引起轰动。学界一般认为美索不达米亚传统更早，但两者关系属共享母题而非简单抄袭。史诗本身也有多个版本与残片，叙述时宜说明其苏美尔、巴比伦与亚述的层次。

en.name: Utnapishtim
en.title: Flood survivor of the Gilgamesh epic

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Utnapishtim appears on tablet eleven of the Epic of Gilgamesh as the sage made immortal after the flood. He tells Gilgamesh how the gods resolved to destroy humanity, how he was warned to build a boat and carried family, craftsmen and animals through, and was granted life at the river mouths; his name means “he found life”.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His flood shares a source with the older Atrahasis and Sumerian flood stories: a divine decision, one man warned to build, birds released to test the water, sacrifice and divine regret. It parallels Noah in Genesis markedly, but the details, theology and genre differ, so the two are not the same tale.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The ark, dove and swallow, the sacrifice after the waters fall, and the place where rivers meet identify him. The tablet calls him “the distant one” at the confluence; the epic uses him to test Gilgamesh and answer that immortality cannot be won. Images are scarce, so the text is the main evidence.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The tablet came from Ashurbanipal’s library at Nineveh in the nineteenth century, and its likeness to the Bible caused a sensation. Scholars usually date the Mesopotamian material earlier, while treating the relation as shared motifs rather than simple copying. Multiple recensions exist, Sumerian, Babylonian and Assyrian.

name: 涅尔伽勒
title: 战争、瘟疫与冥府之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 涅尔伽勒是美索不达米亚的冥府之神，兼掌战争与瘟疫。其名早见于苏美尔文献，主要城邦中心为库塔。他原是星神与战神，后被纳入冥界权力结构，与冥后埃蕾什基伽勒并治下界，成为“不再返回之地”的统治者之一。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 著名故事讲他因不肯向冥后致敬而被邀入冥府，受胁不得复返，遂夺其权柄并与她成婚，共治冥界。这则神话解释了他由天界神祇转为冥府之主的由来。另有叙事把他与瘟疫、战场上的死亡相连；亚述王常祈求他赐予胜利。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 标志是双狮头权杖、弯刀与火焰，其形象常与瘟疫之热和战争之火相联。天文上他与火星相关，占卜文献视其行星运行预兆战乱与疫病。库塔的神庙、出土的犬形塑像与仪式文本，是辨识其崇拜的重要材料。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 冥府观念在美索不达米亚宗教中占重要位置：亡者居于尘土之屋，需供祭与记念，涅尔伽勒因此既可怕又不可或缺。他的职能在后期与埃蕾什基伽勒分工明确，也影响了周边地区对冥神的想象。相关研究多依赖泥板文书与印章图像，须注意版本与地方差异。

en.name: Nergal
en.title: God of war, plague and the underworld

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Nergal is the Mesopotamian god of the underworld who also governs war and plague. His name appears early in Sumerian texts, and his main cult centre was Kutha. Originally a stellar and warrior god, he was drawn into the powers of the netherworld and ruled it with Ereshkigal as lord of the land of no return.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: A famous myth has him enter the underworld because he refused to show deference to its queen, then seize power there when return is denied, marrying Ereshkigal and sharing her rule. This explains his shift from sky god to underworld king. Other texts tie him to pestilence and battle death; Assyrian kings prayed for victory.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: His mace with twin lion heads, curved sword and flames identify him, and he is linked to plague fever and the fire of war. In astronomy he is Mars, whose movements omen texts read as portents of war and disease. Temples at Kutha, dog figurines and ritual texts are the key evidence.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Underworld belief mattered greatly in Mesopotamian religion: the dead lived in a house of dust and needed offerings and remembrance, making Nergal both feared and necessary. His later division of roles with Ereshkigal shaped neighbouring ideas of the netherworld. Study rests on tablets and seals, with variant and local versions.
